盡知人之知，成愛人之仁，此聖人告賢者也。蓋舉直錯枉，知也；使枉者直，則仁矣。然則仁知二者，豈不相為用而不悖哉？昔者樊遲問仁知，未達夫子愛人知人之旨。夫子復告之，若曰：「知主於知人，而知人莫要於分別仁直；仁主於愛人，而愛人莫大乎化人為善。是故宅心中正，徑德
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Raise up the upright and place them above the crooked, and you can make the crooked upright.”

Luo Qinshun

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔When the topic was set from the books [?], there was initially no predetermined interpretation. Most candidates in the examination hall missed its purport. This composition [?] develops it clearly, with refined diction and tone; hence its inclusion.〕

Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out fully the meaning of the Sage’s reply to Fan Chi, leaving nothing unexplored. An accomplished writer [?].〕

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔This composition brings out the idea that knowing people and loving people function together without contradiction. This emerges abundantly in its language. Surely an accomplished writer.〕

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The language and reasoning are lucid and clear.〕

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is short, but its meaning is rich and ample. This composition captures it.〕

To exercise fully the wisdom of knowing people and accomplish the benevolence of loving people: this is what the Sage taught the worthy disciple. For raising up the upright and setting them above the crooked is wisdom; making the crooked upright is benevolence. Do not benevolence and wisdom, then, function together without contradiction? Formerly, Fan Chi asked about benevolence and wisdom but did not grasp the Master’s meaning in speaking of loving people and knowing people. The Master instructed him further, as if to say: “Wisdom consists chiefly in knowing people, and in knowing people nothing is more essential than distinguishing the benevolent and the upright [?]. Benevolence consists chiefly in loving people, and in loving people nothing is greater than transforming them toward goodness. Thus, those whose hearts are centered and correct, whose virtue is upright [?] …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不回而循乎天理之公者所謂直也若人也人
所同好我則舉而用之使得以行其志秉志奸
邪制行頗僻而徇乎人欲之私者所謂枉也若
人也人所同惡我則錯而舍之俾不得以售其
奸邪正分辨而無或混淆用舍允當而不至顛
倒知人之知一何明哉夫惟舉直錯枉如此將
見彼枉者皆自訟曰同此性也何彼直而我枉
乎於是自然自艾悉改其舊日之非亦化而直
矣鈞是人也何彼舉而我錯乎于焉是則是效
===
咸趨於至善之地無復為枉矣直者既舉而無
一善之或遺枉者亦直而無一人之不化愛人
之仁又何博哉夫如是則二者不惟不相悖而
反相為用矣聖人以是而開示樊遲何其至歟
惜乎其猶未喻必待問諸子夏而聞舜湯之事
然後釋然也抑考樊遲〔他日嘗問仁夫子告以〕
居處恭執事敬與人忠又問仁知告以先難後
獲務民之義敬鬼神而遠之先後各異何也蓋
遲之學所至有淺深故夫子隨問隨答使之以
punctuated: 不回，而循乎天理之公者，所謂直也。若人也，人所同好，我則舉而用之，使得以行其志。秉志奸邪，制行頗僻，而徇乎人欲之私者，所謂枉也。若人也，人所同惡，我則錯而舍之，俾不得以售其奸。邪正分辨，而無或混淆；用舍允當，而不至顛倒，知人之知一何明哉！夫惟舉直錯枉如此，將見彼枉者皆自訟曰：「同此性也，何彼直而我枉乎？」於是自然自艾，悉改其舊日之非，亦化而直矣。「鈞是人也，何彼舉而我錯乎？」于焉是則是效，咸趨於至善之地，無復為枉矣。直者既舉，而無一善之或遺；枉者亦直，而無一人之不化，愛人之仁又何博哉！夫如是，則二者不惟不相悖，而反相為用矣。聖人以是而開示樊遲，何其至歟！惜乎其猶未喻，必待問諸子夏，而聞舜湯之事，然後釋然也。抑考樊遲〔他日嘗問仁，夫子告以〕居處恭，執事敬，與人忠。又問仁知，告以先難後獲，務民之義，敬鬼神而遠之。先後各異，何也？蓋遲之學所至有淺深，故夫子隨問隨答，使之以
translation_en: …without deviation, and following the impartiality of Heaven’s principle: this is what is meant by being upright. Such people are those whom everyone alike esteems; I therefore promote and employ them, enabling them to carry out their aspirations. Those whose intentions are wicked and depraved, whose conduct is distorted and perverse, and who pursue the selfishness of human desires: these are what are meant by the crooked. Such people are those whom everyone alike detests; I therefore set them aside and leave them unused, preventing them from putting their wicked schemes into effect. When wickedness and uprightness are distinguished without confusion, and employment and rejection are properly assigned without reversal, how clear is the wisdom of knowing people! Indeed, when one promotes the upright and sets aside the crooked in this way, one will see the crooked all reproach themselves, saying: “We share this same nature; why are they upright while I am crooked?” Then they will naturally repent, entirely reform their former faults, and likewise be transformed into upright people. “We are equally human; why are they promoted while I am set aside?” Thereupon they will take the upright as their models and emulate them, all advancing toward the highest goodness and no longer remaining crooked. Once the upright have been promoted, no worthy person is overlooked; when the crooked too become upright, no person remains untransformed. How expansive, then, is the benevolence of loving people! In this way, these two virtues not only do not conflict but actually assist one another. How consummate was the sage’s instruction of Fan Chi through these words! Regrettably, he still did not understand and had to wait until he questioned Zixia and heard about the deeds of Shun and Tang before his doubts were dispelled. Yet consider Fan Chi: 〔On another occasion he asked about benevolence, and the Master instructed him to〕 be respectful in private life, reverent in undertaking affairs, and loyal in dealing with others. He also asked about benevolence and wisdom, and was told to put difficult tasks first and rewards afterward, to devote himself to what is right in serving the people, and to revere ghosts and spirits while keeping them at a distance. Why did the teachings given earlier and later differ? Because Chi’s learning had reached different depths, the Master answered each question as it arose, enabling him, by…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
漸而進耳聖人教人猶化工之妙均各付物於
此見之
所求乎子以事父未能也所求乎臣以事
君未能也所求乎弟以事兄未能也所求
乎朋友先施之未能也
汪偉
同考試官教諭馮　批〔中庸此節四事而語意相同場中作者多雜於立說且鮮知未能之為未能如其所以責人者此篇〕〔得之矣又以道之全體為聖人所不能為結而引大舜周公之事證之尤見學識〕
同考試官教諭黄　批〔此篇以忠孝之盡其誠盡其實與盡夫盡〕〔倫講君子之道隱然寓慥慥意必如此方見聖人有未能處〕
===
考試官訓導孫　批〔典實〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔文從理順可愛〕
責諸人以當然責諸已有未然此聖人歷言不
遠人以為道之事也蓋道者人已之所同然者
也我之所以責人與反之而自責者皆不外乎
是道焉則不遠人以為道可見矣中庸十三章
引夫子之言以明道之費隱如此蓋謂孝以事
punctuated:
漸而進耳。聖人教人，猶化工之妙均，各付物，於此見之。

所求乎子以事父，未能也；所求乎臣以事君，未能也；所求乎弟以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友先施之，未能也。

汪偉

同考試官教諭馮　批〔中庸此節四事，而語意相同。場中作者多雜於立說，且鮮知未能之為未能如其所以責人者。此篇〕〔得之矣。又以道之全體為聖人所不能為結，而引大舜、周公之事證之，尤見學識。〕

同考試官教諭黄　批〔此篇以忠孝之盡其誠、盡其實，與盡夫盡〕〔倫，講君子之道，隱然寓慥慥意。必如此，方見聖人有未能處。〕

考試官訓導孫　批〔典實。〕

考試官教諭柯　批〔文從理順，可愛。〕

責諸人以當然，責諸已有未然，此聖人歷言不遠人以為道之事也。蓋道者，人已之所同然者也。我之所以責人與反之而自責者，皆不外乎是道焉，則不遠人以為道可見矣。《中庸》十三章引夫子之言，以明道之費隱如此。蓋謂孝以事
translation_en:
…advance gradually, that is all. Here we see how the sage’s teaching resembles the wondrous workings of the transforming power of nature, endowing each thing appropriately.

“What I require of a son, I have not been able to carry out in serving my father; what I require of a minister, I have not been able to carry out in serving my ruler; what I require of a younger brother, I have not been able to carry out in serving my elder brother; what I require of friends, I have not been able to offer them first.”

Wang Wei 汪偉

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: “This passage of the Doctrine of the Mean concerns four matters, but its language conveys the same meaning throughout. Many candidates in the examination introduce a jumble of arguments; moreover, few understand that ‘not having been able’ means not having been able to meet the very standard one demands of others. This essay grasps that point. It further concludes that the Way in its entirety is something even a sage cannot fully realize, adducing the deeds of the great Shun and the Duke of Zhou as evidence. This especially reveals the author’s learning and discernment.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “This essay explains the gentleman’s Way through loyalty and filial devotion—giving full expression to sincerity and actual practice—and through fully fulfilling human relationships [?]. It implicitly conveys the idea of earnest practice. Only through such an approach can one show that there are things even a sage has not yet been able to accomplish.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: “Well grounded in the classics and substantial.”

Comment by Examiner Ke, Instructor: “The writing flows and the reasoning is coherent: admirable.”

One demands of others what ought to be done, and calls oneself to account for what one has not yet done. These are the matters the sage enumerates in speaking of practicing the Way without departing from what is close to human beings. For the Way is what holds true alike for oneself and others. Both the standards by which I hold others accountable and those by which I turn back and hold myself accountable lie entirely within this Way. Thus we can see what it means to practice the Way without departing from what is close to human beings. Chapter thirteen of the Doctrine of the Mean quotes the Master’s words to illuminate the Way’s broad operation and hidden subtlety in this manner. Its meaning is that filial devotion is how one serves …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
親而盡其實此君子之道也所責乎子之盡其
孝者如此然反求諸己則我之所以事其父者
未能如其所以責子者焉忠以事君而盡其誠
亦君子之道也所責乎臣之盡其忠者如此然
反求諸身則我之所以事其君者未能如其所
以責臣者焉以至盡事兄之悌固道也所責乎
弟之敬其兄者如是然以之而自責焉則己之
所以悌乎其兄者果能如是乎盡交友之信亦
道也所責乎朋友之施于我者如是然以之而
===
自求焉則己之所以先施于彼者果能如是乎
是則道不外乎人倫日用之常我之所以責人
者在是我之所以自責者亦在是則道不遠人
而亦不遠於人以為道矣子思子引之以明道
之費隱而申道不可離之意如此何其明且盡
哉抑又論之孝弟忠信四者皆日用常行之道
衆人之所能知能行者而夫子乃曰丘未能一
焉何也蓋聖人之心不自滿假而道之全體則
聖人固亦有所不能盡者此惟大舜周公所以
punctuated:
親而盡其實，此君子之道也。所責乎子之盡其孝者如此，然反求諸己，則我之所以事其父者，未能如其所以責子者焉。忠以事君而盡其誠，亦君子之道也。所責乎臣之盡其忠者如此，然反求諸身，則我之所以事其君者，未能如其所以責臣者焉。以至盡事兄之悌，固道也。所責乎弟之敬其兄者如是，然以之而自責焉，則己之所以悌乎其兄者，果能如是乎？盡交友之信，亦道也。所責乎朋友之施于我者如是，然以之而自求焉，則己之所以先施于彼者，果能如是乎？是則道不外乎人倫日用之常，我之所以責人者在是，我之所以自責者亦在是，則道不遠人，而亦不遠於人以為道矣。子思子引之以明道之費隱，而申道不可離之意如此，何其明且盡哉！

抑又論之，孝弟忠信四者，皆日用常行之道，衆人之所能知能行者，而夫子乃曰：「丘未能一焉。」何也？蓋聖人之心不自滿假，而道之全體，則聖人固亦有所不能盡者。此惟大舜周公所以
translation_en:
…one’s parents and fully realizing filial devotion in practice: this is the way of the gentleman. Such is the complete filial devotion one demands of a son. Yet, turning back to examine oneself, one finds that one’s own service to one’s father has not met the standard one demands of a son. Serving one’s ruler loyally and with complete sincerity is also the way of the gentleman. Such is the complete loyalty one demands of a minister. Yet, turning back to examine oneself, one finds that one’s own service to one’s ruler has not met the standard one demands of a minister. Likewise, fully realizing fraternal deference in serving an elder brother is certainly part of the Way. Such is the respect for an elder brother that one demands of a younger brother. Yet, holding oneself to this standard, can one truly show such deference to one’s own elder brother? Fully realizing trustworthiness in dealings with friends is also part of the Way. Such is the conduct toward oneself that one demands of friends. Yet, examining oneself by this standard, can one truly take the initiative in treating them in this way? Thus, the Way lies entirely within the ordinary human relationships of daily life. What I demand of others lies here, and what I demand of myself also lies here. The Way, then, is not far from people, nor does one depart from people in practicing it. Master Zisi quotes these words to illuminate the Way’s pervasive operation and hidden subtlety, and thus to elaborate the meaning of its inseparability from us. How clear and complete his explanation is!

Let us consider this further. Filial devotion, fraternal deference, loyalty, and trustworthiness are all ways of conduct regularly practiced in daily life, which ordinary people can understand and carry out. Yet the Master says: “I, Qiu, have not been able to achieve even one of them.” Why is this? The sage’s mind is never complacent; moreover, even a sage cannot fully realize every aspect of the Way in its entirety. This is why only the great Shun and the Duke of Zhou…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲能盡事親事君之道也使孝不如舜忠未至
於周公弟友之道有毫髮之未盡則終未至於
天道終未免爲全德之累矣噫道之體用其大
無外此聖如孔子所以猶不敢自以爲能也歟
君子所性仁義禮智根於心其生色也睟
然見於面盎於背施於四體四體不言而
喻
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林　批〔題似易而實難作者多爲所窘惟此篇見理明白措詞穩當錄出〕
===
同考試官教諭王　批〔積中發外類能言之惟此篇理明詞瑩獨異衆作非熟於理書者不能〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔明淨〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔詞理俱到可嘉〕
大賢論君子所性之德本於心而潤於身焉蓋
有諸中必形諸外也君子所性之德既本於心
又豈不有以潤其身乎昔孟子論君子所性之
分與所欲所樂不同而此則言其蘊也蓋謂性
punctuated:
爲能盡事親事君之道也。使孝不如舜，忠未至於周公，弟友之道有毫髮之未盡，則終未至於天道，終未免爲全德之累矣。噫！道之體用，其大無外，此聖如孔子所以猶不敢自以爲能也歟？

君子所性，仁義禮智根於心，其生色也睟然見於面，盎於背，施於四體，四體不言而喻。
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林批〔題似易而實難，作者多爲所窘，惟此篇見理明白，措詞穩當，錄出。〕
同考試官教諭王批〔積中發外，類能言之，惟此篇理明詞瑩，獨異衆作，非熟於理書者不能。〕
考試官訓導孫批〔明淨。〕
考試官教諭柯批〔詞理俱到，可嘉。〕

大賢論君子所性之德，本於心而潤於身焉。蓋有諸中，必形諸外也。君子所性之德既本於心，又豈不有以潤其身乎？昔孟子論君子所性之分，與所欲所樂不同，而此則言其蘊也。蓋謂性
translation_en:
…were able to fulfill the Way of serving parents and serving the ruler. If one's filial devotion falls short of Shun's, one's loyalty does not reach that of the Duke of Zhou, or the Way of younger-brotherly respect and elder-brotherly affection remains unfulfilled by even a hair's breadth, then one has yet to attain the Way of Heaven and cannot avoid a blemish upon complete virtue. Ah! The substance and functioning of the Way are so vast that nothing lies outside them. Is this why even a sage such as Confucius still dared not consider himself fully capable?

“What the gentleman possesses as his nature—benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and wisdom—is rooted in his heart. The radiance it produces appears with tranquil clarity in his face, fills his back, and extends to his four limbs. His four limbs convey it without words.”
Chen Ying
Associate Examiner Lin, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic seems easy but is actually difficult, and many writers have been stymied by it. This essay alone displays a clear understanding of principle and assured wording; it is selected for inclusion.〕
Associate Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: 〔Most can speak of what accumulates within finding expression without. This essay alone has clear reasoning and polished language, distinguishing it from all the others. No one unfamiliar with writings on principle could achieve this.〕
Examiner Sun, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and clean.〕
Examiner Ke, an Instructor, comments: 〔Both language and reasoning are fully accomplished. Commendable.〕

The great worthy discusses how the virtues belonging to the gentleman's nature are rooted in his heart and lend lustre to his person. For what exists within must manifest itself without. Since the virtues belonging to the gentleman's nature are rooted in his heart, how could they fail to lend lustre to his person? Mencius discussed how the endowment belonging to the gentleman's nature differs from what he desires and delights in; here he speaks of what that nature contains. His meaning is that nature…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者人所得於天之理也莫不有之而存焉者寡
矣惟君子也氣禀清明無物欲之累則能全所
性焉彼仁也義也乃性之德皆有以根於心而
方寸之間一天理之渾然禮也智也亦性之德
皆有以本於心而靈臺之内一天德之湛然夫
其積之也既極其盛則其發之也宜無不順吾
見其生色也見於面睟然清和而潤澤一四德
之呈露形於背盎然豐厚而盈溢一四德之發
越以至見於動作威儀之間如手容自恭不俟
===
吾言而自能曉吾之意足容自重不待吾說而
自能喻吾之旨何莫非此四德之所致乎夫以
君子所性之藴如此則所欲所樂無所興而窮
達豈能加損也哉嗟夫時至戰國王道不明人
心陷溺徒知所欲所樂之為已貴而不知所性
為已有也故孟子指以示之無非欲人求盡其
性分之在内者而無所慕於勢分之在外者也
亦遏人欲而擴天理耳
易
punctuated:
者，人所得於天之理也。莫不有之，而存焉者寡矣。惟君子也，氣禀清明，無物欲之累，則能全所性焉。彼仁也、義也，乃性之德，皆有以根於心，而方寸之間，一天理之渾然。禮也、智也，亦性之德，皆有以本於心，而靈臺之内，一天德之湛然。夫其積之也既極其盛，則其發之也宜無不順。吾見其生色也，見於面，睟然清和而潤澤，一四德之呈露；形於背，盎然豐厚而盈溢，一四德之發越。以至見於動作威儀之間，如手容自恭，不俟吾言而自能曉吾之意；足容自重，不待吾說而自能喻吾之旨。何莫非此四德之所致乎？夫以君子所性之藴如此，則所欲所樂無所興，而窮達豈能加損也哉？嗟夫！時至戰國，王道不明，人心陷溺，徒知所欲所樂之為已貴，而不知所性為已有也。故孟子指以示之，無非欲人求盡其性分之在内者，而無所慕於勢分之在外者也。亦遏人欲而擴天理耳。

易
translation_en:
…is the principle that human beings receive from Heaven. Everyone possesses it, yet few preserve it. Only the gentleman, whose endowment of vital energy is clear and luminous and who is unburdened by material desires, can fully preserve what belongs to his nature. Benevolence and righteousness are virtues of that nature. Both are rooted in the heart, so that within that tiny space the principle of Heaven forms a single, undivided whole. Ritual propriety and wisdom are likewise virtues of that nature. Both have their foundation in the heart, so that within this spiritual chamber Heaven’s virtue is wholly clear and still. Once their accumulation within has reached its fullest abundance, their outward expression must naturally be harmonious in every respect. I see how they impart a glow: appearing in the face, clear, peaceful, and lustrous, they are entirely the manifestation of these four virtues; showing in the back, ample and overflowing, they are entirely the radiance of these four virtues. They appear even in movements and dignified bearing. The hands, for example, are naturally respectful: without waiting for me to speak, they can themselves make my intention understood. The feet are naturally composed: without awaiting my explanation, they can themselves convey my meaning. What among these is not brought about by these four virtues?

Since the gentleman’s inherent nature holds such riches, what he desires and delights in cannot compare with it [?]; how could adversity or success add to it or diminish it? Alas! By the Warring States period, the Way of the Kings was no longer manifest, and human hearts had sunk into delusion. People knew only to value what they desired and delighted in, without knowing that what belonged to their nature was already their own. Thus Mengzi pointed this out to them solely because he wished people to seek the full realization of their inward endowment of nature, without coveting the outward advantages of rank and power. This, too, was simply a matter of restraining human desires and extending Heaven’s principle.

Book of Changes

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
盥而不薦有孚顒若　汪偉
同考試官教諭馮　批〔彖傳取盥而不薦之誠以明為觀之道此篇能發明之且文理燦然可敬可愛〕
同考試官教諭黄　批〔能以本義中正示人為人所仰之意融會成文且又能以經講經不泛不拘蓋典則之文也宜〕
表出之以式後學
考試官訓導孫　批〔為觀之道發揮得出〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔辭理兼至〕
===
惟有德以為觀則其德為可仰此聖人繫觀之
辭然也蓋上者下之觀瞻所繫也自非有德以
為觀於上又何以致人之瞻仰於下哉昔文王
繫觀之辭而戒其占如此其意謂夫祭必用盥
所以致潔清也盥而後薦所以奉酒食也為觀
者能以中而示人耶惟精惟一執厥中於正位
凝命之時而不輕於自用殆猶祭者但盥手以
致其潔而酒食之未奉此心必純然紛華之不
雜矣能以正而示人耶其難其慎守是正於嚮
punctuated:
盥而不薦，有孚顒若。汪偉

同考試官教諭馮批〔彖傳取盥而不薦之誠，以明為觀之道。此篇能發明之，且文理燦然，可敬可愛。〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔能以本義中正示人、為人所仰之意，融會成文；且又能以經講經，不泛不拘，蓋典則之文也。宜〕表出之，以式後學。
考試官訓導孫批〔為觀之道，發揮得出。〕
考試官教諭柯批〔辭理兼至。〕

惟有德以為觀，則其德為可仰，此聖人繫觀之辭然也。蓋上者，下之觀瞻所繫也。自非有德以為觀於上，又何以致人之瞻仰於下哉？昔文王繫觀之辭，而戒其占如此。其意謂夫祭必用盥，所以致潔清也；盥而後薦，所以奉酒食也。為觀者能以中而示人耶？惟精惟一，執厥中於正位凝命之時，而不輕於自用，殆猶祭者但盥手以致其潔，而酒食之未奉，此心必純然，紛華之不雜矣。能以正而示人耶？其難其慎，守是正於嚮
translation_en:
“The hands have been washed, but the offerings have not yet been presented; there is sincerity and a solemn, reverent bearing.” Wang Wei.

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔The Commentary on the Judgments draws upon the sincerity of washing the hands before presenting the offerings to explain the way of serving as an example for others to contemplate. This essay succeeds in elucidating it; its composition and reasoning are brilliant, worthy of respect and admiration.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The essay successfully integrates into its composition the idea in the Original Meaning that one displays centrality and correctness to others and is looked up to by them. Moreover, it explains the classic through the classic, neither straying into generalities nor becoming constrained. It is indeed an exemplary composition. It should〕be singled out as a model for later students.
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The way of serving as an example for others to contemplate is successfully expounded.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔Both expression and reasoning attain excellence.〕

Only when one possesses virtue and thereby serves as an example for contemplation does that virtue become worthy of admiration: this is why the sage appended these words to the hexagram Contemplation (Guan). For those above are the focus of the gaze of those below. Unless one possesses virtue and serves as an example above, how can one inspire those below to look up in admiration? Formerly, King Wen appended these words to Contemplation, thus admonishing those who consulted the oracle. His meaning was that sacrifice necessarily involves washing the hands, by which purity and cleanliness are attained; the presentation that follows the washing is the offering of wine and food.

Can one who serves as an example display centrality to others? Being discerning and single-minded, he holds fast to that centrality when taking his proper position and securing Heaven’s mandate, and does not rashly rely upon his own judgment. This is much like the sacrificer who has merely washed his hands to attain cleanliness, before the wine and food have been offered: his heart must be wholly pure, unmixed with distracting splendor. Can he display correctness to others? Mindful of the difficulty and exercising caution, he preserves this correctness when facing…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
明而治之際初不妄有所為有如祭者但潔手
以致其誠而腥熟之未獻此中必粹然專物之
無間矣夫惟執中以示人而不輕於自用則維
德不顯而此中之存於內者充實而無妄充
實則輝光由是濟濟令儀足以為四方之瞻仰
不猶盥而不薦則孚信在中而顒然可仰乎夫
惟守正以示人而不妄有所為則至德淵微而
至正之在於我者積盛而無斁矣積中則發外
由是雍雍王度足以為萬國之觀瞻不猶盥而
===
未薦則誠敬在躬而肅然可觀乎是則為觀之
道在有德以觀示於下如此占而值之者可不
知所戒哉雖然有其德无其位固不足以為觀
有其位无其德亦不足以為觀我稽古人若大
舜之恭己南面而四方風動文王之不大聲色
而萬邦作孚之二聖人者蓋有德有位而足以
為觀於天下者也噫當其位而欲盡其道者宜
於舜文求之
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺
punctuated:
明而治之際，初不妄有所為，有如祭者但潔手以致其誠，而腥熟之未獻，此中必粹然專物之無間矣。夫惟執中以示人而不輕於自用，則維德不顯，而此中之存於內者充實而無妄。充實則輝光，由是濟濟令儀，足以為四方之瞻仰，不猶盥而不薦，則孚信在中而顒然可仰乎？夫惟守正以示人而不妄有所為，則至德淵微，而至正之在於我者積盛而無斁矣。積中則發外，由是雍雍王度，足以為萬國之觀瞻，不猶盥而未薦，則誠敬在躬而肅然可觀乎？是則為觀之道，在有德以觀示於下如此，占而值之者可不知所戒哉？雖然，有其德无其位，固不足以為觀；有其位无其德，亦不足以為觀。我稽古人，若大舜之恭己南面而四方風動，文王之不大聲色而萬邦作孚，之二聖人者，蓋有德有位而足以為觀於天下者也。噫！當其位而欲盡其道者，宜於舜文求之。

範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺。
translation_en:
…when facing the dawn to govern, he never acts rashly, just as one performing a sacrifice merely cleanses his hands to express his sincerity, before the raw and cooked offerings have been presented. Within, he must then be utterly pure, with no intrusion of distracting things [?]. Only by holding to the mean to set an example for others, without lightly relying on his own judgment, does his virtue remain unobtrusive, while the mean preserved within him becomes full and substantial, free of falsity. Inner fullness then shines forth. Thus his dignified and excellent bearing suffices to command the admiration of the four quarters. Is this not like washing the hands without yet presenting the offerings: sincerity and trustworthiness reside within, and his imposing presence inspires reverence? Only by maintaining rectitude to set an example for others, without acting rashly, does his supreme virtue become profound and subtle, while the utmost rectitude within him accumulates abundantly and never flags. What accumulates within then manifests itself outwardly. Thus his harmonious royal bearing suffices to command the regard of the myriad states. Is this not like washing the hands before presenting the offerings: sincerity and reverence abide in his person, and his solemn presence commands respect?

Such, then, is the way of serving as an example: possessing virtue with which to instruct those below through one's visible conduct. Can anyone who encounters this hexagram in divination fail to recognize its admonition? Nevertheless, possessing the virtue without the position is certainly insufficient to serve as such an example; possessing the position without the virtue is likewise insufficient. Examining the ancients, I find such figures as the great Shun, who held himself reverently and faced south, while the four quarters responded as grass bends before the wind; and King Wen, who made no display through loud words or stern looks, yet inspired trust throughout the myriad states. These two sages possessed both virtue and position, and were therefore sufficient to serve as examples to all under Heaven. Ah! Those who occupy such a position and wish to fulfill its Way should seek their guidance in Shun and Wen.

Encompassing the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding them, bringing the myriad things to completion according to their particular circumstances without omitting any…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
通乎晝夜之道而知故神无方而易无體
蔡吉
同考試官教諭馮　　批〔此題場中作者多於聖人神易處剖析不明此篇獨能反覆發明殆无餘蘊蓋老於易學者也是宜錄出〕
同考試官教諭黄　　批〔聖人以易至命之事皆神易之所為此篇得之末又以通章之義為結尤佳〕
考試官教諭柯　　批〔能發明至命之事〕
考試官訓導孫　　批〔得旨〕
大傳論聖人至命之事一用易之極功焉蓋命
===
者理性之原也聖人贊化知化而神易之妙從
可見焉則用易之極功而命於是乎至矣大傳
此章論易道之大聖人既用之以窮理盡性矣
至此乃言其至命之事謂夫命行於氣而為化
天地之化无窮盡也聖人為之立法定制以範
圍之不使過於中焉命賦於形而為物人物之
生无紀極也聖人為之脩道立教以曲成之未
始有或遺焉以至命運於陰陽而為晝夜之道
聖人於晝之道如明也生也神也皆有以知其
punctuated:
通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而易无體。
蔡吉
同考試官教諭馮批〔此題場中作者多於聖人神易處剖析不明，此篇獨能反覆發明，殆无餘蘊，蓋老於易學者也，是宜錄出。〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔聖人以易至命之事，皆神易之所為，此篇得之。末又以通章之義為結，尤佳。〕
考試官教諭柯批〔能發明至命之事。〕
考試官訓導孫批〔得旨。〕
大傳論聖人至命之事，一用易之極功焉。蓋命者，理性之原也。聖人贊化知化，而神易之妙從可見焉，則用易之極功，而命於是乎至矣。大傳此章論易道之大，聖人既用之以窮理盡性矣，至此乃言其至命之事。謂夫命行於氣而為化，天地之化无窮盡也，聖人為之立法定制以範圍之，不使過於中焉。命賦於形而為物，人物之生无紀極也，聖人為之脩道立教以曲成之，未始有或遺焉。以至命運於陰陽而為晝夜之道，聖人於晝之道，如明也、生也、神也，皆有以知其
translation_en:
…comprehends the Way of day and night and knows it; thus the numinous has no fixed location, and change has no fixed form.

Cai Ji

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔Among those in the examination who wrote on this topic, many failed to distinguish clearly the sage, the numinous, and change. This essay alone elucidates these repeatedly, leaving virtually no meaning unexplored. Its author is evidently well versed in the study of the Changes; it deserves to be selected for inclusion.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The sage’s use of the Changes to fathom Heaven’s mandate is entirely the work of the numinous and change. This essay grasps that point. Its conclusion, which draws on the meaning of the entire chapter, is especially fine.〕

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔It succeeds in elucidating the fathoming of Heaven’s mandate.〕

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps the essential meaning.〕

The Great Commentary discusses the sage’s fathoming of Heaven’s mandate as entirely the ultimate achievement of using the Changes. For Heaven’s mandate is the source of principle and nature. The sage assists transformation and understands transformation, and through this the subtle workings of the numinous and change become apparent. This is the ultimate achievement of using the Changes, and through it Heaven’s mandate is fathomed.

This chapter of the Great Commentary discusses the greatness of the Way of the Changes. Having already used it to investigate principle exhaustively and fully realize nature, the sage now proceeds to fathom Heaven’s mandate. The meaning is this: Heaven’s mandate operates through vital energy and becomes transformation. The transformations of Heaven and Earth are inexhaustible. The sage establishes standards and institutions to encompass them, preventing them from exceeding the proper mean. Heaven’s mandate is imparted to forms and becomes things. The coming into being of people and things has no limit. The sage cultivates the Way and establishes instruction to bring each to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances, never leaving anything out. Furthermore, Heaven’s mandate moves through yin and yang and becomes the Way of day and night. Regarding the Way of day—such aspects as brightness, life, and spirit—the sage has the means to know their …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
於夜焉於夜之道若幽也死也鬼也又有以知
其因乎晝焉是又能通知之而不偏矣然是道
也皆此心神易之所為耳聖人之神妙不可測
无方所之可拘運是神於天地萬物晝夜之間
則所以範圍曲成知道而无不盡者此神之无
方也使有未盡則在陰者或不能在陽而有方
矣夫豈至神之妙哉聖人之易變動不居无形
體之可求運此易於天地萬物晝夜之間則所
以範圍曲成知道而无不至者此易之无體也
===
使有未至則為陽者或不能為陰而有體矣又
豈易之變化乎可造化陰陽皆命之所在也聖
人以易而至之如此用易之極功於是乎可見
矣抑考大傳此章言易道之大而用於聖人者
如此前言其知幽明之故死生之說鬼神之情
狀而已此則通知晝夜之道而默契其本原焉
前言其與天地相似不違而已此則能範圍曲
成而有以脗合其妙用焉意理也性也命也有
淺深而無二道也然皆聖人以易而窮之盡之
punctuated:
於夜焉。於夜之道，若幽也、死也、鬼也，又有以知其因乎晝焉，是又能通知之而不偏矣。然是道也，皆此心神易之所為耳。聖人之神，妙不可測，无方所之可拘。運是神於天地萬物晝夜之間，則所以範圍、曲成、知道而无不盡者，此神之无方也。使有未盡，則在陰者或不能在陽，而有方矣，夫豈至神之妙哉？聖人之易，變動不居，无形體之可求。運此易於天地萬物晝夜之間，則所以範圍、曲成、知道而无不至者，此易之无體也。使有未至，則為陽者或不能為陰，而有體矣，又豈易之變化乎？可造化陰陽，皆命之所在也。聖人以易而至之如此，用易之極功，於是乎可見矣。

抑考《大傳》此章，言易道之大而用於聖人者如此。前言其知幽明之故、死生之說、鬼神之情狀而已，此則通知晝夜之道，而默契其本原焉。前言其與天地相似不違而已，此則能範圍、曲成，而有以脗合其妙用焉。意理也、性也、命也，有淺深而無二道也。然皆聖人以易而窮之、盡之，
translation_en:
…in relation to night [?]. As for the way of night—such things as darkness, death, and ghosts—the sage also has the means to know its dependence upon day. Thus he comprehends both fully, without partiality. Yet this way is entirely the working of the spiritual efficacy and change within this mind. The sage’s spiritual efficacy is wondrous and unfathomable; no particular location can confine it. He brings this spiritual efficacy into operation amid Heaven and Earth, the myriad things, and day and night. That through which he encompasses them, brings them to completion in all their particularities, and knows their way, leaving nothing unfulfilled, is precisely this spiritual efficacy’s freedom from any fixed location. Were anything left unfulfilled, what was present in yin might be unable to be present in yang, and would thus have a fixed location. How could that be the wonder of supreme spiritual efficacy? The sage’s change moves and transforms without remaining fixed; no definite form or substance can be sought in it. He brings this change into operation amid Heaven and Earth, the myriad things, and day and night. That through which he encompasses them, brings them to completion in all their particularities, and knows their way, reaching everywhere without exception, is precisely this change’s freedom from any fixed form. Were anything left unreached, what constituted yang might be unable to constitute yin, and would thus have a fixed form. How could that be the transformation wrought by change? The processes of creation and transformation, and yin and yang, are all where the heavenly mandate resides [the preceding 可 is doubtful]. Such is the way the sage uses the Changes to reach it. Here we can see the highest achievement of applying the Changes.

Now, examining this chapter of the Great Commentary, we find that it describes the greatness of the way of the Changes and its application by the sage in this manner. Earlier it spoke only of his knowing the causes of the hidden and manifest, the explanation of death and life, and the circumstances and forms of ghosts and spirits. Here, however, he fully comprehends the way of day and night and tacitly accords with its ultimate source. Earlier it spoke only of his resembling Heaven and Earth and not departing from them. Here, however, he can encompass things and bring them to completion in all their particularities, thereby according with their wondrous operation. Presumably, principle, nature, and the heavenly mandate differ in depth, yet do not constitute separate ways. Nevertheless, it is through the Changes that the sage fathoms and fully realizes them…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以至之則易道之大信乎其與天地相準而能
彌綸其道也學易者宜合而觀之
書
咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批〔塲中作此題者多為所窘惟此篇包括無遺且説臣克相君君克相天之意之見有學識是用錄出〕
同考試官教諭陸　批〔帝舜總命羣臣之意隱然見於篇中〕
===
考試官訓導孫　批〔筆勢老健語意精到非熟於辭經者不能〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔以敬立說而詞氣舂容佳作也〕
聖君總命羣臣惟欲各敬其職以相天事也盖
事出於天而代之者君臣也苟羣臣不能各敬
其職以相之安得不廢事以慢天哉是宜聖君
總舉為羣臣告歟昔帝舜於告廟即位之初分
punctuated:
以至之，則易道之大，信乎其與天地相準而能彌綸其道也。學易者宜合而觀之。

書
「咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。」
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李批〔塲中作此題者多為所窘，惟此篇包括無遺，且説臣克相君、君克相天之意，之見有學識，是用錄出。〕
同考試官教諭陸批〔帝舜總命羣臣之意，隱然見於篇中。〕
考試官訓導孫批〔筆勢老健，語意精到，非熟於辭經者不能。〕
考試官教諭柯批〔以敬立說，而詞氣舂容，佳作也。〕

聖君總命羣臣，惟欲各敬其職，以相天事也。盖事出於天，而代之者君臣也。苟羣臣不能各敬其職以相之，安得不廢事以慢天哉？是宜聖君總舉為羣臣告歟！昔帝舜於告廟即位之初，分
translation_en:
…and thereby attained it. So vast is the Way of the Changes: truly it accords with Heaven and Earth and comprehensively embraces their Way. Students of the Changes should consider these passages together.

Book of Documents
“Ah, you twenty-two men, be reverent! Thus assist in accomplishing Heaven’s work.”
Luo Qinshun

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: 〔Many candidates who attempted this topic in the examination hall were constrained by its difficulties. This essay alone encompasses everything without omission. Moreover, it explains how ministers can assist their ruler and the ruler can assist Heaven, demonstrating learning and discernment [?]. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: 〔Emperor Shun’s intention in issuing a collective charge to his ministers is subtly apparent throughout the essay.〕

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: 〔The writing is seasoned and vigorous, its language and meaning precise and fully realized. Only someone thoroughly familiar with the language of the classics [?] could achieve this.〕

Comment by Examiner Ke, Instructor: 〔It establishes its argument upon reverence, and its diction and cadence are measured and expansive. An excellent composition.〕

When the sage ruler issued a collective charge to his ministers, he desired only that each should attend reverently to his office and thereby assist in Heaven’s work. For affairs originate in Heaven, while the ruler and his ministers act on its behalf. If the ministers cannot each attend reverently to their offices and lend their assistance, how can they avoid neglecting affairs and slighting Heaven? It was therefore fitting that the sage ruler should bring these matters together in an admonition to his ministers! Formerly, when Emperor Shun had first announced his accession at the ancestral temple and assumed the throne, he separately…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
命岳牧九官之後又進羣臣總告之若曰
汝二十有二人四岳總十二牧十二牧養萬民我固已
各舉其職而命汝矣汝可不欽乃攸司而無敢
荒寧乎九官分內治百揆統庶官我固已歷舉
其任而命汝矣汝可不敬爾有官而罔或怠忽
乎然我所以欲汝欽敬者豈有他哉良以羣臣
所治無非天功耳蓋天不能自治而命之君君不
能獨治而任之臣苟一職之或曠則天功以之廢
矣汝為岳牧者必及時趨事寅亮此天功使四
===
門洞闢而聰明旁達五事脩舉而蠻夷率服也
為九官者惟時赴工激明此天事使教養工虞
無舉而無遺禮樂刑政四達而不悖也如此則
庶幾衆職脩舉天功明亮臣克相乎君而君克
相乎天矣汝羣臣其可忽哉大抵欽之一言非
特人臣治事之要寔帝王心法之傳觀諸經傳
稱堯曰欽明舜曰溫恭禹曰祗承湯曰聖敬文
武曰敬止敬勝可見矣故虞廷君臣交相告戒
皆不出此是以當時任官之簡如此卒使庶政
punctuated:
命岳牧九官之後，又進羣臣，總告之，若曰：「汝二十有二人，四岳總十二牧，十二牧養萬民，我固已各舉其職而命汝矣。汝可不欽乃攸司而無敢荒寧乎？九官分內治，百揆統庶官，我固已歷舉其任而命汝矣。汝可不敬爾有官而罔或怠忽乎？然我所以欲汝欽敬者，豈有他哉？良以羣臣所治，無非天功耳。蓋天不能自治而命之君，君不能獨治而任之臣。苟一職之或曠，則天功以之廢矣。汝為岳牧者，必及時趨事，寅亮此天功，使四門洞闢而聰明旁達，五事脩舉而蠻夷率服也。為九官者，惟時赴工，激明此天事，使教養工虞無舉而無遺，禮樂刑政四達而不悖也。如此，則庶幾衆職脩舉，天功明亮，臣克相乎君，而君克相乎天矣。汝羣臣其可忽哉！」
大抵欽之一言，非特人臣治事之要，寔帝王心法之傳。觀諸經傳，稱堯曰欽明，舜曰溫恭，禹曰祗承，湯曰聖敬，文武曰敬止、敬勝，可見矣。故虞廷君臣交相告戒，皆不出此。是以當時任官之簡如此，卒使庶政
translation_en:
…after assigning duties to the Four Chiefs, the regional governors, and the nine officials, he again summoned his ministers and addressed them collectively, as if to say: “You twenty-two men: the Four Chiefs oversee the twelve regional governors, and the twelve regional governors nurture the myriad people. I have already specified each office’s duties and charged you with them. Should you not reverently attend to your responsibilities, never daring to indulge in idleness and ease? The nine officials divide the administration of internal affairs, and the General Regulator oversees the various officials. I have already enumerated their responsibilities and charged you with them. Should you not respect your offices and allow no negligence or indifference?
“Yet could there be any other reason why I require reverence and respect from you? It is precisely because everything administered by my ministers is Heaven’s work. Heaven cannot administer affairs itself and so entrusts them to the ruler; the ruler cannot administer them alone and so delegates them to his ministers. If even one office is neglected, Heaven’s work is thereby left undone. Those of you serving as Chiefs and regional governors must attend promptly to your duties and reverently assist in this work of Heaven, so that the gates on all four sides stand wide open and sight and hearing reach everywhere, the five affairs are duly carried out, and the Man and Yi peoples all submit. Those serving as the nine officials must undertake their work at the proper time and vigorously illuminate [?] these affairs of Heaven, so that education, sustenance, crafts, and the management of natural resources leave no undertaking omitted [?], while rites, music, punishments, and government extend in all directions without discord. In this way, we may hope that all offices will discharge their duties and Heaven’s work will be made manifest: ministers will be able to assist their ruler, and the ruler will be able to assist Heaven. Can you, my ministers, possibly neglect this?”
In general, the single word ‘reverence’ is not merely the essential principle by which ministers administer affairs; it is truly the transmitted teaching of the emperors and kings concerning the mind. This can be seen in the classics and their commentaries, which describe Yao as ‘reverent and enlightened,’ Shun as ‘gentle and respectful,’ Yu as ‘reverently receiving,’ Tang as possessing ‘sagely reverence,’ and Kings Wen and Wu in terms of ‘abiding in reverence’ and ‘prevailing through reverence.’ Thus, at the court of Shun, ruler and ministers admonished one another without ever departing from this principle. For this reason, the appointment of officials in those days was so simple, and ultimately brought all branches of government…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
惟和萬國咸寧而雍熙之治卓乎非千萬世所
能企及其亦以是也歟
協于克一俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一
哉王心
徐威
同考試官訓導李　批〔協于克一此心學最妙工夫此作體貼殆盡又能說出伊尹忠愛之意出爲〕
〔世用事君之心可卜於今日矣〕
同考試官教諭陸　批〔得伊尹告太甲之旨〕
===
考試官訓導孫　批〔伊尹欲𠔃純一其德之意正如此〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔典則〕
人君取衆善而會一心天下極稱頌而同一詞
蓋善者人心所同有也人君苟能取衆善而會
諸一心焉則此感彼應天下有不稱頌之者哉
昔伊尹恐太甲德不純一因告以取人爲善之
要而推言及此意若曰吾王主善爲師固能盡
天下之博矣使不能協于一何以守吾心之約
乎一者吾心之本體衆善之統會者也蓋善有
punctuated:
惟和，萬國咸寧，而雍熙之治卓乎非千萬世所能企及，其亦以是也歟？

協于克一，俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」

徐威

同考試官訓導李，批〔協于克一，此心學最妙工夫，此作體貼殆盡，又能說出伊尹忠愛之意。出爲世用，事君之心可卜於今日矣。〕
同考試官教諭陸，批〔得伊尹告太甲之旨。〕
考試官訓導孫，批〔伊尹欲𠔃純一其德之意，正如此。〕
考試官教諭柯，批〔典則。〕

人君取衆善而會一心，天下極稱頌而同一詞。蓋善者，人心所同有也。人君苟能取衆善而會諸一心焉，則此感彼應，天下有不稱頌之者哉？昔伊尹恐太甲德不純一，因告以取人爲善之要，而推言及此。意若曰：「吾王主善爲師，固能盡天下之博矣。使不能協于一，何以守吾心之約乎？一者，吾心之本體，衆善之統會者也。蓋善有
translation_en:
…were harmonious, and all the states enjoyed peace. That flourishing and harmonious governance stood so far above what countless generations could hope to attain—was this not also the reason?

“Bring them into accord with unity, so that all the people say, ‘Great are the king’s words!’ and also say, ‘Undivided is the king’s heart!’”

Xu Wei 徐威

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔“Bringing them into accord with unity” is the most subtle work of the learning of the mind. This composition apprehends it almost completely and also articulates Yi Yin’s loyal affection. When the author enters public service, the spirit in which he will serve his ruler can already be discerned today.〕
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔It captures the purport of Yi Yin’s admonition to Tai Jia.〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Yi Yin’s intention to have [?] his virtue become pure and undivided was precisely like this.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕

The ruler gathers the many forms of goodness and unites them in a single heart; all under Heaven offer the highest praise with one voice. Goodness is something all human hearts possess in common. If the ruler can gather the many forms of goodness and unite them in his own heart, then his influence here will elicit a response there: would anyone under Heaven fail to praise him?

Formerly, Yi Yin feared that Tai Jia’s virtue was not pure and undivided. He therefore instructed him in the essential principle of drawing upon others to practice goodness, and extended his explanation to this point. His meaning was as though he said: “Our king takes goodness as his teacher and can indeed encompass the vast range of all under Heaven. But if he cannot bring it into accord with unity, how can he preserve the concentrated simplicity of his own heart? title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
偶殊初無常主或在此爲善在彼則不善或在
前日則不善而今日則爲善要必以我之心度
彼之善使是非可否毫釐之不差以彼之善會
我之心使巨細精麤運融而無閒如此則天下
之萬理皆會于吾之一心而吾心之一理足以
應天下之萬事矣人君惟其心之一故其發諸
言也大由是將使萬姓之衆得於觀感之餘者
莫不曰大哉吾王之言乎其綸音之渙發誠乎
萬理而無一善之或遺擧天下之言無以加矣
===
萬姓見其言之大故能知其心之一又莫不曰
一哉吾王之心乎其本體之虛明純乎天理而
無一毫之或雜與天地之心無以異矣是何也
蓋君有此心民亦同此心君有此善民亦有此
善感應之妙自然而然此可以見人心之不可
欺而誠之不可掩如此太甲可不知所以一其
德哉抑考上文曰主善爲師卽虞書之惟精此
曰協于克一卽虞書之惟一此聖學始終條理
之序帝王傳心之要典也伊尹平日樂堯舜之
punctuated:
偶殊，初無常主。或在此爲善，在彼則不善；或在前日則不善，而今日則爲善。要必以我之心度彼之善，使是非可否毫釐之不差；以彼之善會我之心，使巨細精麤運融而無閒。如此，則天下之萬理皆會于吾之一心，而吾心之一理足以應天下之萬事矣。人君惟其心之一，故其發諸言也大。由是將使萬姓之衆得於觀感之餘者，莫不曰：「大哉，吾王之言乎！其綸音之渙發，誠乎萬理，而無一善之或遺，擧天下之言無以加矣。」萬姓見其言之大，故能知其心之一，又莫不曰：「一哉，吾王之心乎！其本體之虛明，純乎天理，而無一毫之或雜，與天地之心無以異矣。」是何也？蓋君有此心，民亦同此心；君有此善，民亦有此善。感應之妙，自然而然。此可以見人心之不可欺，而誠之不可掩如此。太甲可不知所以一其德哉？

抑考上文曰「主善爲師」，卽《虞書》之「惟精」；此曰「協于克一」，卽《虞書》之「惟一」。此聖學始終條理之序，帝王傳心之要典也。伊尹平日樂堯舜之
translation_en:
…may differ [?] and initially have no fixed governing standard. What is good in one situation may not be good in another; what was not good in the past may be good today. What is essential is to assess that goodness with my own mind, so that judgments of right and wrong, of what is acceptable and unacceptable, do not err by the slightest degree; and to bring that goodness together within my mind, so that the great and small, the fine and coarse, function harmoniously without any gap. In this way, the myriad principles of the world all converge in my single mind, while the single principle within my mind suffices to respond to the myriad affairs of the world. It is precisely because the ruler’s mind is unified that what he expresses in words is great. Thus, all the people, through what they gain by observing him and being moved by his example, will say: “How great are our king’s words! His imperial pronouncements, issuing far and wide, are true to the myriad principles and omit no good whatsoever. Nothing said throughout the world could surpass them.” Seeing the greatness of his words, the people can therefore recognize the unity of his mind. They will also all say: “How unified is our king’s mind! Empty and luminous in its original substance, it accords purely with heavenly principle, without the slightest admixture. It is no different from the mind of Heaven and Earth.” Why is this so? The ruler has this mind, and the people share this same mind; the ruler possesses this goodness, and the people also possess it. The subtle working of stimulus and response occurs of itself. From this we can see that people’s minds cannot be deceived and that sincerity cannot be concealed. Could Tai Jia fail to understand how to unify his virtue?

Furthermore, examining the preceding passage, its words “Take goodness as your master” correspond to “Be discerning” in the Documents of Yu; the words here, “Bring them into accord so as to attain unity,” correspond to “Be single-minded” in the Documents of Yu. This is the orderly sequence of sagely learning from beginning to end, and the essential canon through which emperors and kings transmit the mind. Yi Yin had long delighted in Yao and Shun’s …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
道恒欲使是君爲堯舜之君今欲退老厥邑尚
惓惓擧舜禹授受之微旨爲太甲告其愛君之
忠至老不變有如是者厥後太甲果能克終允
德爲有商令主謂非得於伊尹告戒之力歟
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
彼有不穫穉此有不歛穧彼有遺秉此有
滯穗伊寡婦之利
陳嬰

利之盛而溥其餘惠蓋天澤降而後地利盛也
然非賴君德以致之亦何能溥其惠於下哉宜
punctuated:
道，恒欲使是君爲堯舜之君。今欲退老厥邑，尚惓惓擧舜禹授受之微旨爲太甲告。其愛君之忠，至老不變，有如是者。厥後太甲果能克終允德，爲有商令主，謂非得於伊尹告戒之力歟？

translation_en:
…the Way, and always wished to make this ruler a ruler like Yao and Shun. Now, wishing to retire to his own settlement in his old age, he still earnestly invoked the subtle import of the transmission from Shun to Yu to instruct Tai Jia. Such was his loyalty and love for his ruler, unchanged even in old age. Subsequently, Tai Jia indeed remained steadfast to the end in true virtue and became a worthy ruler of the Shang. Can one say that this was not due to the power of Yi Yin’s admonitions?

Book of Odes

“Dense clouds gather,
And gentle rain begins to fall.
Rain upon our public fields,
Then reach our private plots.
There is young grain left unreaped there,
And harvested grain left ungathered here;
There are handfuls left behind there,
And ears left lying here:
These are the widow’s gain.”

Chen Ying

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: 〔This essay is organized around praising those above. Rich in expression and resonant in cadence, it is a delight to read.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Candidates in the examination hall often base their arguments on benevolence and righteousness, making them tiresome to read. Coming upon this script late in the proceedings, I found it imbued with the original spirit of praise; I could not help rubbing my eyes and looking afresh.〕

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: 〔The poet’s intention in offering praise was precisely this.〕

For only after Heaven’s beneficent rain descends does the earth yield abundantly. Yet without relying on the ruler’s virtue to bring this about, how could its benefits spread widely to those below? title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛時農夫以是而頌美其上也歟吾想農夫當
望雲雨之際意若曰雲欲盛盛則多雨吾願雲
之興也萋萋乎其盛雨欲徐徐則入土吾願雨
之降也祁祁乎其徐然所以降是雨者天之賜
而所以致是雨者君之德天其眷我君德先雨
我之公田中百畝以為君之祿者而既優既渥
矣遂及我之私田外八百畝為野人之所受者
亦既霑既足焉蓋枯君德而蒙其餘惠使收成
之際彼有不及獲之穉禾此有不及歛之穧束
===
而彼此同一豐年之祥也彼有遺棄之禾把此
有滯漏之禾穗而公私同一有年之慶也然彼
穉此穧不棄之於無用而寡婦尚得取之以為
利非有以補其不足乎彼秉此穗不置之於狼
戾而寡婦尚得取之以為食非有以助其不給
乎吁天澤佑君德而降則私田之澤固公卿之
澤也地利得天澤而盛則寡婦之利亦公卿之
利也盛時農夫以是答其上何其忠愛也哉大
抵有周盛時君之愛民無所不用其極民之愛
punctuated: 盛時農夫以是而頌美其上也歟！吾想農夫當望雲雨之際，意若曰：「雲欲盛，盛則多雨，吾願雲之興也，萋萋乎其盛；雨欲徐，徐則入土，吾願雨之降也，祁祁乎其徐。然所以降是雨者，天之賜；而所以致是雨者，君之德。天其眷我君德，先雨我之公田，中百畝以為君之祿者，而既優既渥矣；遂及我之私田，外八百畝為野人之所受者，亦既霑既足焉。」蓋枯君德而蒙其餘惠，使收成之際，彼有不及獲之穉禾，此有不及歛之穧束，而彼此同一豐年之祥也；彼有遺棄之禾把，此有滯漏之禾穗，而公私同一有年之慶也。然彼穉此穧，不棄之於無用，而寡婦尚得取之以為利，非有以補其不足乎？彼秉此穗，不置之於狼戾，而寡婦尚得取之以為食，非有以助其不給乎？吁！天澤佑君德而降，則私田之澤固公卿之澤也；地利得天澤而盛，則寡婦之利亦公卿之利也。盛時農夫以是答其上，何其忠愛也哉！大抵有周盛時，君之愛民無所不用其極，民之愛
translation_en:
…that farmers in an age of prosperity should praise their superiors for this! I imagine that, as the farmers looked expectantly for clouds and rain, their thoughts were something like these: “Clouds should be abundant, for abundant clouds bring plentiful rain. I wish the clouds would rise in luxuriant profusion! Rain should fall gently, for gentle rain enters the soil. I wish the rain would descend in a gentle, steady shower! Yet the falling of this rain is Heaven’s gift, while what brings it about is our ruler’s virtue. May Heaven regard our ruler’s virtue with favor and first rain upon our public field—the central hundred mu that provide the ruler’s revenue—until it is generously drenched. Then may the rain reach our private fields—the outer eight hundred mu allotted to us country people—so that these too are thoroughly watered.”

Thus, relying on the ruler’s virtue [?], they receive its overflowing benefits. At harvest time, here there is young grain they have not had time to reap, and there are sheaves they have not had time to gather: both alike are signs of an abundant year. Here are abandoned handfuls of stalks, and there are ears of grain left behind and overlooked: public and private fields alike share the joy of a good harvest. Yet this young grain and these sheaves are not discarded as useless; widows can still take them for their benefit. Does this not make up what they lack? These handfuls and ears are not left scattered to waste; widows can still take them for food. Does this not help meet their needs?

Ah! When Heaven’s beneficent rain descends in support of the ruler’s virtue, the blessing received by the private fields is indeed also a blessing for the dukes and ministers. When the earth’s yield flourishes through Heaven’s rain, the benefit received by widows is likewise a benefit for the dukes and ministers. How loyal and loving were the farmers of that prosperous age, who thus reciprocated the kindness of their superiors! Generally speaking, in the flourishing age of the Zhou, rulers carried their love for the people to the utmost, and the people’s love for…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
君亦無所不用其極今觀公卿以我田既臧爲
農夫之慶而欲報之以介福農夫以雨我公田
遂及我私而欲其饗祀以介景福上下之情所
以相賴而相報者如此可見君德固厚而民德
亦歸於厚矣猗歟盛哉
昭茲來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
楊　逵用

===

詩人美聖君道在於已極其著道傳於後又其
福蓋道之不著不足傳於後也今聖君之道昭
明如此豈不足以垂裕於無疆也哉下武之詩
美武王而作謂夫孝體於身而行於一家未足
爲道之明也孝行於家而及於一國亦未足爲
punctuated:
君亦無所不用其極。今觀公卿以我田既臧爲農夫之慶，而欲報之以介福；農夫以雨我公田，遂及我私，而欲其饗祀以介景福。上下之情，所以相賴而相報者如此，可見君德固厚，而民德亦歸於厚矣。猗歟，盛哉！

translation_en:
…the people likewise went to the utmost in loving their ruler. Now we see that the high ministers regarded “our fields have yielded well” as cause for rejoicing on behalf of the farmers, and wished to repay them with great blessings. The farmers, for their part, said, “May rain fall on our public fields, and then reach our private fields,” and wished that the ministers’ sacrifices might be accepted, bringing them great blessings. Such were the feelings through which those above and below relied upon and repaid one another. We can see that the ruler’s virtue was indeed generous, and that the people’s virtue likewise became generous. Ah, how flourishing an age!

“Illumine those who come after; follow the footsteps of your ancestors. For ten thousand years, receive Heaven’s blessings.”

Yang Kuiyong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: 〔The divisions are clear, and the writing has vigor and brilliance; it ranks foremost among the essays on the ‘Qian Classic’ [?].〕 Who but you could claim this distinction?
