title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對寬猛因時而不泥乎古此
聖祖撥世救時之卓見寬猛相濟而必酌其宜
此
聖世長治久安之良圖盖易亂為治固不得不
施之以猛而貽謀燕翼又不得不示之以
寬寬猛因時神矣哉
聖祖卓越之見也政猛則必節之以寬政寬則
必振之以猛寬猛相濟允矣哉
聖世致治之法也請因執事之問而陳其槩昔
===
孔子論居上為政而必有取於寬者所以
示人為政之常道也伊尹傅說之告其君
而皆欲其法祖者亦示之以法其常道而
已洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺
天眷命為生民主丁元政縱弛之餘遭華風淪
沒之際教化陵夷人紀廢墜思欲示國法
於臣民乃作
大誥三編鋤凶芟惡之典凛乎秋霜之肅殺
punctuated:
對：寬猛因時而不泥乎古，此聖祖撥世救時之卓見；寬猛相濟而必酌其宜，此聖世長治久安之良圖。盖易亂為治，固不得不施之以猛；而貽謀燕翼，又不得不示之以寬。寬猛因時，神矣哉，聖祖卓越之見也！政猛則必節之以寬，政寬則必振之以猛。寬猛相濟，允矣哉，聖世致治之法也！請因執事之問而陳其槩。
昔孔子論居上為政，而必有取於寬者，所以示人為政之常道也。伊尹、傅說之告其君，而皆欲其法祖者，亦示之以法其常道而已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天眷命，為生民主，丁元政縱弛之餘，遭華風淪沒之際，教化陵夷，人紀廢墜。思欲示國法於臣民，乃作《大誥》三編，鋤凶芟惡之典，凛乎秋霜之肅殺
translation_en:
In reply: To employ leniency and severity according to the times, without being bound by antiquity—this was the Sagely Founder’s outstanding insight in setting the world right and rescuing his age. To make leniency and severity complement each other, always weighing what is appropriate—this is the excellent plan by which the sagely reign secures lasting order and enduring peace. To transform disorder into good government, severity was indeed indispensable; yet to bequeath plans for the peace and welfare of descendants, it was also indispensable to demonstrate leniency. How inspired was the Sagely Founder’s exceptional insight in adapting leniency and severity to the times! When government is severe, it must be tempered with leniency; when government is lenient, it must be invigorated with severity. How sound is the sagely reign’s method of achieving good government through the mutual balancing of leniency and severity! Allow me to set out its essentials in response to your question.
In former times, when Confucius discussed governing from a position of authority, he invariably commended leniency, thereby showing people the constant Way of government. When Yi Yin and Fu Yue counseled their sovereigns, both urged them to emulate their ancestors; this likewise meant only that they should follow that constant Way. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s favor and mandate and became lord of the people. He came in the aftermath of lax government under the Yuan, at a time when Chinese civilized customs had fallen into oblivion, moral instruction was declining, and the bonds of human relationships had broken down. Wishing to make the laws of the state manifest to his officials and people, he composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao). Their statutes for rooting out the violent and eliminating the wicked were as stern and deadly as autumn frost…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也戢姦剔蠹之法肅乎雷霆之威斷也若
是者似異於孔子之言矣然而
御宇建極餘三十年教化已晦而復明人紀
已墜而復立
盛德大業視殷湯周武而無愧者蓋以其用
法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳及其
駿命已凝大統已定思欲示家法於子孫乃
作
祖訓一書論用法特以前日之嚴為戒論致
===
治惟於先王之道是程若是者又似異於
伊傅之言矣然而
聖子神孫傳六七世九有奠安而至治益隆四
夷賓服而
鴻業益固
重熙累洽視太甲高宗而有光者以其垂訓
有合於孔子論為政之道故耳夫猛於立
國之初者一時之用也寬於繼統之後者
萬世之常也寬猛各因其時而效驗各臻
punctuated: 也。戢姦剔蠹之法，肅乎雷霆之威斷也。若是者，似異於孔子之言矣。然而御宇建極餘三十年，教化已晦而復明，人紀已墜而復立，盛德大業視殷湯周武而無愧者，蓋以其用法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳。及其駿命已凝，大統已定，思欲示家法於子孫，乃作祖訓一書。論用法，特以前日之嚴為戒；論致治，惟於先王之道是程。若是者，又似異於伊傅之言矣。然而聖子神孫傳六七世，九有奠安而至治益隆，四夷賓服而鴻業益固，重熙累洽，視太甲高宗而有光者，以其垂訓有合於孔子論為政之道故耳。夫猛於立國之初者，一時之用也；寬於繼統之後者，萬世之常也。寬猛各因其時，而效驗各臻
translation_en:
…indeed. His laws for restraining evildoers and rooting out pernicious elements were as stern and decisive as thunder. Such measures might seem to differ from Confucius’s words. Yet, in more than thirty years of ruling the realm and establishing the supreme standard, he restored moral instruction after it had fallen into obscurity and reestablished human relationships after they had collapsed. His magnificent virtue and great achievements could stand without shame beside those of Tang of Yin and Wu of Zhou. This was because his application of the law accorded with the prescription in the Offices of Zhou for punishing a disorderly state.

Once his great mandate was secured and the imperial succession established, he wished to set forth his family’s rules for his descendants, and therefore composed the Ancestral Instructions. In discussing the application of law, he specifically warned against the severity of his earlier days; in discussing the attainment of good government, he took only the Way of the former kings as his standard. This, in turn, might seem to differ from the words of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Yet his sagely sons and inspired grandsons have succeeded one another for six or seven generations: the nine regions are securely at peace, and consummate government flourishes ever more; the peoples of the four quarters submit, and the great imperial enterprise grows ever more secure. Successive reigns of prosperity and accumulated peace shine in comparison with those of Tai Jia and Gaozong. This is because the instructions he bequeathed accorded with Confucius’s discussion of the Way of government.

Severity at the founding of a state is a measure for a particular time; leniency after succession to its rule is the enduring norm for ten thousand generations. Leniency and severity each suit their particular time, and their effects each attain…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
其極非
聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古曷能然哉雖然嘗
聞之孔子有曰政寬則民慢慢則糾之以
猛猛則民殘殘則施之以寬寬以濟猛猛
以濟寬政是以和
列聖相承迄今百二十餘年矣記不云乎異世
殊時不相沿襲愚竊以為因俗為政尚當
以孔子之言為法因時制宜隨事取中猛
以警之使頹靡之綱無不振寬以行之使
仁厚之意無不存則唐虞三代之治無以
易此而其所以垂裕於
後昆者將億萬斯世而無窮矣謹因明問所
及而述其管見如此他日倘得徹聽
九重亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也
第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林 批〔究道學之淵源探先儒之閫〕
奥無如此篇
punctuated:
其極，非聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古，曷能然哉？雖然，嘗聞之，孔子有曰：「政寬則民慢，慢則糾之以猛；猛則民殘，殘則施之以寬。寬以濟猛，猛以濟寬，政是以和。」列聖相承，迄今百二十餘年矣。《記》不云乎：「異世殊時，不相沿襲。」愚竊以為因俗為政，尚當以孔子之言為法，因時制宜，隨事取中。猛以警之，使頹靡之綱無不振；寬以行之，使仁厚之意無不存。則唐虞三代之治無以易此，而其所以垂裕於後昆者，將億萬斯世而無窮矣。謹因明問所及，而述其管見如此。他日倘得徹聽九重，亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也。

第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林 批〔究道學之淵源，探先儒之閫〕奥，無如此篇。
translation_en:
…their fullest effect. Had the sagely founding emperor’s profound intentions and discerning wisdom not surpassed those of all ages, how could this have been so? Nevertheless, I have heard that Confucius said: “When government is lenient, the people grow lax; when they grow lax, correct them with severity. When government is severe, the people suffer; when they suffer, extend leniency to them. Temper severity with leniency and leniency with severity: through this, government achieves harmony.” Successive sage emperors have inherited the throne, and more than 120 years have now passed. Does not the Record of Rites say: “Different ages and different times do not simply follow one another’s practices”?

In my humble view, governing in accordance with prevailing customs should still take Confucius’s words as its rule: devise suitable measures for the times and find the proper balance in each matter. Use severity to admonish, so that every weakened bond of discipline is restored; practice leniency, so that the spirit of benevolence and generosity is preserved throughout. Then even the government of Tang Yao, Yu Shun, and the Three Dynasties could offer no improvement upon this, and the prosperity thereby bequeathed to future descendants would endure for countless generations without end. In respectful response to the matters raised in your illuminating question, I have thus set forth my limited views. Should they someday reach the emperor’s hearing, perhaps they too might offer some small help—like the humble gifts of celery and sunshine.

Second Policy Question
Chen Ying
Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor, comments: “For tracing the origins of the Learning of the Way and probing the innermost teachings of earlier Confucian scholars, no essay equals this one.”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭王　批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人蓋疑其未有能受之者此策於先天太極通書西銘諸書同異條答無遺其亦深有所得而可受之者耶〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔精粹〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔策能答所問足見學識〕
對濂溪未作而千聖相傳之道學晦而不
明濂溪既作而千聖相傳之道統斷而復
續夫道之大原出於天而具於人心蓋渾
然一太極也濂溪周子手為圖筆為書使斯
===
道已晦而復明已斷而復續是其生乎千
載之下而有以接道統於千載之上奮乎
百世之上而有以啓道學於百世之下也
先生之學其粹矣哉愚顧何人而能發其
精蘊乎麤陳大義以復明問之萬一且夫
伏羲先天之易備天地鬼神之奧萬事萬
物之理誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也堯舜湯武
之相禪繼以治天下者以是孔曾思孟之
相傳授以淑天下者以是孟子既歿聖學
punctuated:
同考試官教諭王　批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人，蓋疑其未有能受之者。此策於先天、太極、通書、西銘諸書同異，條答無遺，其亦深有所得而可受之者耶？〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔精粹。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔策能答所問，足見學識。〕
對：濂溪未作，而千聖相傳之道學晦而不明；濂溪既作，而千聖相傳之道統斷而復續。夫道之大原出於天，而具於人心，蓋渾然一太極也。濂溪周子手為圖，筆為書，使斯道已晦而復明，已斷而復續。是其生乎千載之下，而有以接道統於千載之上；奮乎百世之上，而有以啓道學於百世之下也。先生之學，其粹矣哉！愚顧何人，而能發其精蘊乎？麤陳大義，以復明問之萬一。且夫伏羲先天之易，備天地鬼神之奧、萬事萬物之理，誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也。堯舜湯武之相禪繼以治天下者，以是；孔曾思孟之相傳授以淑天下者，以是。孟子既歿，聖學
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Cheng never showed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate to others, presumably because he doubted that anyone was yet capable of receiving it. This policy essay answers, point by point and without omission, the questions concerning the similarities and differences among the writings on the Prior-to-Heaven system and the Supreme Ultimate, the Comprehensive Treatise (Tongshu), and the Western Inscription (Ximing). Might its author likewise be someone who has attained a profound understanding and is capable of receiving it?〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Refined and pure.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay answers what was asked, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.〕
Reply: Before Lianxi arose, the learning of the Way transmitted through a thousand sages had become obscure and unclear. Once Lianxi arose, the succession of the Way transmitted through a thousand sages, having been broken, was restored. The great source of the Way issues from Heaven and is fully present in the human heart; it is, indeed, a single, undivided Supreme Ultimate. Master Zhou of Lianxi drew a diagram with his own hand and composed a book with his brush, thereby bringing this Way back to light after its obscuration and restoring its continuity after its interruption. Thus, although born a thousand years later, he was able to join the succession of the Way extending from a thousand years before; rising a hundred generations earlier, he was able to open up the learning of the Way for a hundred generations to come. How pure was the Master's learning! Yet who am I, in my ignorance, to elucidate its essential depths? I shall set forth its broad meaning in rough outline, thereby answering some tiny part of your discerning question.
Now, Fuxi's Prior-to-Heaven Changes encompasses the mysteries of Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, and the principles of all affairs and all things. It is truly the earliest source of this cultural tradition for all ages. It was through this that Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, succeeding one another through abdication or succession, governed all under Heaven; it was through this that Kongzi, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mengzi, transmitting their teachings from one to another, brought goodness to all under Heaven. After Mengzi died, the learning of the sages …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不傳先生崛起千載之後獨得不傳之秘
祖先天之易作太極之書所謂太極云者
蓋本於易有太極而陰陽五行人物由此
而生即太極生兩儀兩儀生四象四象生
八卦之謂也自太極之在造化者言之則
即天地可以推太極動靜之妙所謂立天
之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛也自
太極之在品彙者言之惟聖人會太極動
靜之全所謂立人之道曰仁與義也至於
===
易通之書又與此圖相為表裏所謂誠者
即圖之言太極而大哉乾元萬物資始乾
道變化各正性命即圖之陽動而陰靜也
所謂五殊二實二本則一此自末以緣本
萬物統體一太極也所謂一實萬分萬一
各正此自本而之末一物各具一太極也
太極之書祖先天之易則其象數宜無不
同今觀太極自一而二自二而五即推至
於萬物其則自一而二自二而四自四而
punctuated:
不傳，先生崛起千載之後，獨得不傳之秘，祖先天之易，作太極之書。所謂太極云者，蓋本於「易有太極」，而陰陽五行人物由此而生，即「太極生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦」之謂也。自太極之在造化者言之，則即天地可以推太極動靜之妙，所謂「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛」也。自太極之在品彙者言之，惟聖人會太極動靜之全，所謂「立人之道曰仁與義」也。至於《易通》之書，又與此圖相為表裏。所謂誠者，即圖之言太極；而「大哉乾元，萬物資始」「乾道變化，各正性命」，即圖之陽動而陰靜也。所謂「五殊二實，二本則一」，此自末以緣本，萬物統體一太極也。所謂「一實萬分，萬一各正」，此自本而之末，一物各具一太極也。

太極之書祖先天之易，則其象數宜無不同。今觀太極，自一而二，自二而五，即推至於萬物；其則自一而二，自二而四，自四而
translation_en:
…was not transmitted. The Master arose a thousand years later and alone grasped the secret that had gone untransmitted. Taking the Earlier Heaven Changes as his foundation, he composed his work on the Supreme Ultimate. What he called the Supreme Ultimate derives from the statement, “The Changes contains the Supreme Ultimate.” Yin and yang, the Five Phases, human beings, and all other things arise from it. This is precisely what is meant by “The Supreme Ultimate generates the Two Modes; the Two Modes generate the Four Images; the Four Images generate the Eight Trigrams.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate as it exists in the process of creation and transformation, one can infer from Heaven and Earth the subtle workings of its movement and stillness. This is what is meant by “The Way of Heaven is established as yin and yang; the Way of Earth is established as yielding and firm.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate as it exists in the various classes of beings, only the sage comprehends its movement and stillness in their entirety. This is what is meant by “The Way of humanity is established as benevolence and righteousness.” As for the book Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), it and this diagram illuminate one another as inner meaning and outward expression. What the book calls sincerity is what the diagram calls the Supreme Ultimate. The statements “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! All things depend upon it for their beginnings” and “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, each thing attaining its proper nature and allotted destiny” correspond to the diagram’s yang in movement and yin in stillness. The statement “The five are distinct, yet their substance is the two; the two are rooted in the one” traces the branches back to the root: all things, taken together, constitute a single Supreme Ultimate. The statement “The one reality differentiates into the myriad, and each of the myriad attains its proper condition” proceeds from the root to the branches: each individual thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

Since the work on the Supreme Ultimate takes the Earlier Heaven Changes as its foundation, its images and numbers should agree with it in every respect. Yet, examining the Supreme Ultimate, we see that it proceeds from one to two, from two to five, and then extends directly to the myriad things; the latter [?] proceeds from one to two, from two to four, and from four to …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
八自八而十六自十六而三十二自三十
二而六十四然後萬物之理備誠若有可
疑者然物理本同而象數亦無二致但推
得有詳畧耳通書一篇本名易通則六十
四卦疑皆有其說今考其書獨有乾損益
家人睽復無妄蒙艮等說則亦有未安者
然先生之書散逸頗多盖本有而今亡矣
先天太極二圖雖同一發明造化之妙也
然先天乃伏羲本圖非康節所自作雖無
===
言語而所談甚廣太極却是濂溪自作發
明易中大槩綱領意思而已故格局則太
極不如先天之大而詳義理則先天不如
太極之精而約也太極西銘二書雖同一
開示學者之言也然西銘則推人以之天
即近以明遠於學者日用最為親切太極
則詳於性命之原而畧於進為之目有不
可以驟而語者故程子於西銘嘗屢言以
示門人而太極未嘗一言及之也至若劉
punctuated:
八，自八而十六，自十六而三十二，自三十二而六十四，然後萬物之理備，誠若有可疑者。然物理本同，而象數亦無二致，但推得有詳畧耳。《通書》一篇，本名《易通》，則六十四卦疑皆有其說。今考其書，獨有乾、損、益、家人、睽、復、無妄、蒙、艮等說，則亦有未安者。然先生之書散逸頗多，盖本有而今亡矣。
先天、太極二圖，雖同一發明造化之妙也，然先天乃伏羲本圖，非康節所自作，雖無言語，而所談甚廣。太極却是濂溪自作，發明《易》中大槩綱領意思而已。故格局則太極不如先天之大而詳，義理則先天不如太極之精而約也。
太極、西銘二書，雖同一開示學者之言也，然西銘則推人以之天，即近以明遠，於學者日用最為親切。太極則詳於性命之原，而畧於進為之目，有不可以驟而語者。故程子於西銘，嘗屢言以示門人，而太極未嘗一言及之也。至若劉
translation_en:
…eight, from eight to sixteen, from sixteen to thirty-two, and from thirty-two to sixty-four; only then are the principles of the myriad things fully encompassed. There does indeed seem to be grounds for doubt. Yet the principles of things are fundamentally the same, and their images and numbers likewise admit of no divergence; it is merely that some derivations are more detailed and others more abbreviated. The work entitled Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu) was originally called Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), so presumably it contained explanations of all sixty-four hexagrams. Examining the book now, however, we find explanations only of such hexagrams as Qian, Sun, Yi, Jiaren, Kui, Fu, Wuwang, Meng, and Gen. This, too, leaves something unresolved. Yet a considerable portion of the Master's writings has been scattered and lost; presumably these explanations originally existed but are now lost.
Although the Diagram of the Prior Heaven and the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate both elucidate the subtleties of creation and transformation, the former is Fuxi's original diagram, not something Kangjie himself devised. Though it contains no words, what it conveys is exceedingly broad. The Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, by contrast, was Lianxi's own creation, intended merely to elucidate the general framework and purport of the Book of Changes. Thus, in scope and arrangement, the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate is less expansive and detailed than the Diagram of the Prior Heaven; in elucidating moral principles, however, the Diagram of the Prior Heaven is less refined and concise than the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate.
Although the two works, the Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription, alike offer instruction to students, the Western Inscription proceeds by extending from humanity to Heaven, elucidating what is distant through what is near, and is therefore especially immediate and pertinent to students' daily lives. The Supreme Ultimate is detailed concerning the source of human nature and destiny, but brief concerning the specific steps of moral advancement; some of its teachings cannot be conveyed all at once. Thus Master Cheng repeatedly spoke of the Western Inscription to instruct his disciples, yet never said a word about the Supreme Ultimate. As for Liu…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
子所謂天地之中即濂溪太極之謂蓋中
只是恰好處極是在中至極之理也橫渠
太虛之說本爲無極之意殊不知無極是
該虛實清濁而言太虛只說得清虛一邊
耳嗟夫伊洛道喪寖失其真賴有考亭朱
夫子上接聖賢相傳之道統著書立言私
淑後人其本義啓蒙諸書皆所以闡揚乎
太極之理也噫道學得濂溪而始傳濂溪
得朱子而益明朱子實有大造於萬世學
===
者矣謹對
第三問
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批〔塲中答此策者多不能以其述而求其心惟此篇能推原聖心步步著實無異當時親炙者焉〕
同考試官教諭陸　批〔隨問隨答略無蹇詞策塲中作者〕
薦何疑
考試官訓導孫　批〔足見用心希聖之學〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔三塲多可録録此以例其餘〕
punctuated:
子所謂「天地之中」，即濂溪太極之謂。蓋中只是恰好處，極是在中至極之理也。橫渠太虛之說，本爲無極之意，殊不知無極是該虛實清濁而言，太虛只說得清虛一邊耳。嗟夫！伊洛道喪，寖失其真，賴有考亭朱夫子，上接聖賢相傳之道統，著書立言，私淑後人。其《本義》《啓蒙》諸書，皆所以闡揚乎太極之理也。噫！道學得濂溪而始傳，濂溪得朱子而益明，朱子實有大造於萬世學者矣。謹對。

第三問
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批〔塲中答此策者，多不能以其述而求其心，惟此篇能推原聖心，步步著實，無異當時親炙者焉。〕
同考試官教諭陸　批〔隨問隨答，略無蹇詞，策塲中作者。〕
薦，何疑？
考試官訓導孫　批〔足見用心希聖之學。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔三塲多可録，録此以例其餘。〕
translation_en:
…What Master Liu calls “the center of Heaven and Earth” is precisely what Lianxi calls the Supreme Ultimate. For “the center” is simply the point that is exactly right, while “the ultimate” is the principle of utmost perfection within that center. Hengqu’s doctrine of the Great Void was originally intended to convey the meaning of the Non-Ultimate. Yet he failed to understand that the Non-Ultimate encompasses both the empty and the substantial, the clear and the turbid, whereas the Great Void expresses only the clear and empty side.

Alas! The Way of the Yi and Luo masters declined, and its true meaning was gradually lost. Fortunately, Master Zhu of Kaoting carried forward the succession of the Way transmitted by the sages and worthies, writing books and setting forth teachings through which later generations could learn from him indirectly. His works, including Original Meaning and Introduction to the Study of the Changes, all elucidate the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. Ah! Learning of the Way began to be transmitted through Lianxi, and Lianxi’s teachings became still clearer through Master Zhu. Master Zhu has indeed rendered an immense service to learners for ten thousand generations. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Third Question
Luo Qinshun

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Among those answering this policy question in the examination hall, most could not seek the sage’s mind through what he related. This essay alone traces matters back to the sage’s mind, proceeding soundly at every step, as though its author had personally received his instruction in his own day.〕

Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: 〔Each question receives its answer, without the slightest awkwardness of expression: an accomplished writer among the policy-essay candidates.〕

What doubt can there be about recommending him?

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔This amply demonstrates learning devoted to aspiring to sagehood.〕

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔Much from all three sessions merits inclusion. We include this piece as a specimen of the rest.〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對欲觀聖人之迹當知聖人之道欲知聖
人之道當原聖人之心蓋聖人之心一道
之所寓而言行之迹一道之所形也得其
心則可以知其道知其道則凡跡之同異
皆可以會而通之合而一之而無所疑矣
苟徒泥其跡而不原其心明其道以會其
同異惡足以知聖人也哉嗟夫尼丘毓秀
孔聖肇生窮宇宙而一人亘古今而獨盛
道參于兩間法垂於萬世誠非後人所敢
===
妄議也然其言行之載諸經傳者似有小
異不能無疑愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸
矣姑即其一二而論之如里必擇乎仁厚
較之居不陋乎九夷者若戾矣殊不知化
於人者常人之事固當擇化人者聖人之
事不必擇也亂邦不居比之公山欲往者
似背矣殊不知趨善避惡固君子潔身之
常道而化惡為善又聖人誨人之本心也
從先進以示損過就中之意從周制以盡
punctuated: 對：欲觀聖人之迹，當知聖人之道；欲知聖人之道，當原聖人之心。蓋聖人之心，一道之所寓；而言行之迹，一道之所形也。得其心，則可以知其道；知其道，則凡跡之同異，皆可以會而通之，合而一之，而無所疑矣。苟徒泥其跡，而不原其心、明其道，以會其同異，惡足以知聖人也哉！嗟夫！尼丘毓秀，孔聖肇生，窮宇宙而一人，亘古今而獨盛，道參于兩間，法垂於萬世，誠非後人所敢妄議也。然其言行之載諸經傳者，似有小異，不能無疑。愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸矣。姑即其一二而論之。如里必擇乎仁厚，較之居不陋乎九夷者，若戾矣。殊不知，化於人者，常人之事，固當擇；化人者，聖人之事，不必擇也。亂邦不居，比之公山欲往者，似背矣。殊不知，趨善避惡，固君子潔身之常道；而化惡為善，又聖人誨人之本心也。從先進以示損過就中之意，從周制以盡
translation_en:
In reply: To examine the sage’s deeds, one must understand the sage’s Way; to understand the sage’s Way, one must trace it to the sage’s heart. For the sage’s heart is where the one Way resides, and his words and deeds are where that one Way takes form. If we grasp his heart, we can understand his Way. If we understand his Way, we can reconcile all the similarities and differences in his deeds, bringing them together into a coherent unity and leaving no room for doubt. If we merely cling to his deeds without tracing them to his heart and illuminating his Way so as to reconcile their similarities and differences, how could we adequately understand the sage?

Ah! Niqiu nurtured its finest essence, and the sage Confucius was born. Throughout the universe he stands alone; across past and present his greatness is unmatched. His Way ranks alongside Heaven and Earth, and his example extends through ten thousand generations. Truly, he is not someone whom later people would dare discuss presumptuously. Yet his words and deeds as recorded in the classics and their commentaries seem to contain minor discrepancies, which cannot but occasion doubts. I, an ignorant student, have also recited and studied them and grasped their underlying purport. Let me discuss one or two examples.

His insistence that one choose a neighborhood marked by benevolence and generosity seems at odds with his assertion that living among the Nine Yi would not be uncouth. What this overlooks is that being transformed by others is the lot of ordinary people, who certainly should choose their surroundings; transforming others is the work of the sage, who need not choose. His refusal to dwell in a disordered state seems inconsistent with his wish to go to Gongshan. What this overlooks is that pursuing goodness and avoiding evil is indeed the gentleman’s constant way of preserving his integrity, while transforming evil into goodness is also the sage’s fundamental intention in teaching others. By following the earlier practitioners, he expressed his intention to reduce excess and attain the mean; by following the institutions of Zhou, he fully fulfilled…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
為下不倍之道從夫先進非即所以從周
乎言無類是我之教化有善反之功云不
移乃彼之暴棄無自反之道教雖無類豈
能移其下愚乎大學之道自致知始此聖
人文行忠信之先夫文小學之事自力行
始此弟子餘力學文之先夫行民無信不
立者全體之大信故為為政之先必信於
言者一事之小信故為為士之次知魯火
而不知麁焚非明於遠而暗於近也蓋桓
===
僖之廟功德不足以存火之者天道之必
然也麁牧之地人馬之所雨集焚之者人
事之偶然也拜南子而不拜陽貨非重於
此而輕於彼也古者仕於其國有見小君
之禮彼頒見而吾則往見非行其禮之當
然乎大夫有賜於士雖有往拜之禮彼矙
亡而吾亦矙亡非欲其禮之相稱乎箕子
比干微子也觀其行雖有死生去就之殊
原其心同一至誠惻怛之意所以同謂之
punctuated: 為下不倍之道。從夫先進，非即所以從周乎？言無類，是我之教化有善反之功；云不移，乃彼之暴棄無自反之道。教雖無類，豈能移其下愚乎？大學之道自致知始，此聖人文行忠信之先夫文；小學之事自力行始，此弟子餘力學文之先夫行。民無信不立者，全體之大信，故為為政之先；必信於言者，一事之小信，故為為士之次。知魯火而不知麁焚，非明於遠而暗於近也。蓋桓僖之廟，功德不足以存，火之者天道之必然也；麁牧之地，人馬之所雨集，焚之者人事之偶然也。拜南子而不拜陽貨，非重於此而輕於彼也。古者仕於其國，有見小君之禮，彼頒見而吾則往見，非行其禮之當然乎？大夫有賜於士，雖有往拜之禮，彼矙亡而吾亦矙亡，非欲其禮之相稱乎？箕子、比干、微子也，觀其行，雖有死生去就之殊；原其心，同一至誠惻怛之意，所以同謂之
translation_en:
…the way of serving as a subordinate without disloyalty. Is following the earlier practitioners not precisely the means of following Zhou? When he says that there are no distinctions of kind in teaching, this means that my instruction has the power to bring people back to goodness; when he says that some cannot be changed, this means that they have ruined and abandoned themselves and have no way of returning to goodness on their own. Although teaching makes no distinctions of kind, how could it change the lowest fools?

The way of greater learning begins with extending knowledge: this is why the sage places learning first among learning, conduct, conscientiousness, and trustworthiness. The work of elementary learning begins with earnest practice: this is why, in saying that disciples should study texts when they have strength to spare, he places conduct first. That the people cannot stand without trust concerns trust in its comprehensive, greater sense; hence it takes precedence in governing. Being invariably faithful to one’s word concerns trustworthiness in a single matter, in its lesser sense; hence it takes a secondary place in being a gentleman.

Knowing about the fire in Lu but not about the burning of the stables [?] does not mean that he understood distant affairs but was ignorant of those nearby. The achievements and virtue of Dukes Huan and Xi were insufficient to warrant preserving their temples, so their destruction by fire was a necessary consequence of Heaven’s way. The stables and pastures [?] were places where men and horses gathered in numbers [?]; their burning was an accidental occurrence in human affairs.

Paying respects to Nanzi but not to Yang Huo does not mean that he esteemed the former and slighted the latter. In antiquity, those serving in a state observed the rite of an audience with the ruler’s consort. When she summoned him to an audience [?] and he went to see her, was this not performing the rite as was proper? When a grand master bestowed a gift upon a gentleman, there was indeed a rite requiring a visit to offer thanks. Yet, since the other had watched for his absence, he too watched for the other’s absence: was this not a desire to make their observance of ritual correspond?

As for Jizi, Bi Gan, and Weizi, if we examine their actions, they differed in dying or living, withdrawing or remaining in service. If we trace their intentions, however, they shared the same utmost sincerity and compassionate concern. For this reason, they were all called…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
三仁大伯文王也或當為而不欲為以全
人子之孝或可為而不忍為以盡人臣之
忠所以同謂之至德殷夏之後尚有杞宋
之所存也故有據而可考杞宋之後無復
杞宋之所存矣此無徵而不信其於孔子
之知何所損不待結纓之日而豫知于路
之死人事之可必也不能於終日之頃而
先知顏淵之夭天命之不幸也其於孔子
之知何所虧荅郰公以為知禮所以諱其
===
君之過以存吾之忠厚斥管仲以不知禮
所以暴其人之罪以著彼之僭竊勤農事
以利天下者君子之公心也不适之褒而
譏褒學農事以利一已者小人之私心也
不遲之貶而譏貶必竭其兩端於鄙夫者
是我固無倦教之心不復於三隅之不反
者是彼終無受教之地論父母之國道在
可久也則遲遲於三日不朝之魯何過耶
論無道之君道在可去也則急急於一問
punctuated: 三仁。大伯、文王也，或當為而不欲為，以全人子之孝；或可為而不忍為，以盡人臣之忠，所以同謂之至德。殷夏之後，尚有杞宋之所存也，故有據而可考；杞宋之後，無復杞宋之所存矣，此無徵而不信，其於孔子之知何所損？不待結纓之日，而豫知于路之死，人事之可必也；不能於終日之頃，而先知顏淵之夭，天命之不幸也，其於孔子之知何所虧？荅郰公以為知禮，所以諱其君之過，以存吾之忠厚；斥管仲以不知禮，所以暴其人之罪，以著彼之僭竊。勤農事以利天下者，君子之公心也，不适之褒而譏褒；學農事以利一已者，小人之私心也，不遲之貶而譏貶。必竭其兩端於鄙夫者，是我固無倦教之心；不復於三隅之不反者，是彼終無受教之地。論父母之國，道在可久也，則遲遲於三日不朝之魯，何過耶？論無道之君，道在可去也，則急急於一問
translation_en: …the three humane men. As for Taibo and King Wen, one was obliged to act but chose not to, thereby fully preserving a son's filial devotion; the other could have acted but could not bear to, thereby fulfilling a subject's loyalty. Thus both were said to possess consummate virtue. After the Yin and Xia dynasties, their surviving traditions were still preserved in Qi and Song, providing evidence that could be examined. After Qi and Song, nothing comparable remained to preserve those traditions. Without corroboration, they could not command belief; how did this detract from Confucius's knowledge? That he foresaw the death of Yulu [?; apparently Zilu] before the day when he tied his cap strings was because human affairs can have predictable outcomes. That he could not foresee Yan Yuan's early death even within the course of a day was because this was a misfortune decreed by Heaven. How did this diminish Confucius's knowledge? His reply that the Duke of Zou [?] understood ritual concealed his ruler's faults and preserved his own loyalty and generosity. His denunciation of Guan Zhong as ignorant of ritual exposed that man's offenses and made his usurpation of prerogatives manifest. To labor at farming for the benefit of all under Heaven expresses a gentleman's public-minded concern: the wording about praising this is doubtful [?]. To learn farming for one's own benefit expresses a petty man's selfish concern: the wording about censuring this is doubtful [?]. That he invariably exhausted both ends of a question for an unlearned man shows that he himself never tired of teaching. That he did not repeat his instruction for someone unable to infer the other three corners shows that the other person ultimately lacked the capacity to receive instruction. Regarding the land of one's parents, the Way allows one to remain long: what fault, then, was there in his lingering in Lu, where for three days court was not held? Regarding a ruler without the Way, the Way allows one to leave: thus his haste upon a single question…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
軍旅之衛何遽耶孔圉勤學好問是好善
而忘己之勢公叔錫氏爵位是好善而忘
人之勢此皆合乎謚法之公者烏得不同
許其可以為文乎子貢因論學而知詩子
夏因論詩而知學是皆得於言意之表者
烏得不同許其可以言詩乎由是而觀則
知孔子之體即道而用即義聲為律而身
為度舉一身之言行誠萬世之標準也又
何彼此異同之可議哉愚生管窺蠡測不
能盡摹寫之詳惟執事其進教之謹對
===
汪偉
第四問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔五策皆善發答而此篇尤有見故錄之〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔壽孔學者切務當求學古人賞博而約而有自得之趣此篇深究古書與夫運用之法盡實留心於書學而有所得者也宜錄之以為學書者式〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔觀此條答必其能游于藝者〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔有筆手〕
punctuated:
軍旅之衛，何遽耶？孔圉勤學好問，是好善而忘己之勢；公叔錫氏爵位，是好善而忘人之勢。此皆合乎謚法之公者，烏得不同許其可以為文乎？子貢因論學而知詩，子夏因論詩而知學，是皆得於言意之表者，烏得不同許其可以言詩乎？由是而觀，則知孔子之體即道而用即義，聲為律而身為度，舉一身之言行，誠萬世之標準也。又何彼此異同之可議哉？愚生管窺蠡測，不能盡摹寫之詳，惟執事其進教之。謹對。

汪偉
第四問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔五策皆善發答，而此篇尤有見，故錄之。〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔壽孔學者切務，當求學古人，賞博而約，而有自得之趣。此篇深究古書與夫運用之法，盡實留心於書學而有所得者也。宜錄之，以為學書者式。〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔觀此條答，必其能游于藝者。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔有筆手。〕
translation_en:
…military affairs in Wei—how could his departure have been too hasty? Kong Yu studied diligently and delighted in asking questions: he loved goodness and disregarded his own high standing. Gongshu bestowed rank and office upon his retainer [?]: he loved goodness and disregarded the other man's low standing. Both accorded with the impartial principles governing posthumous names; how could Confucius fail to approve equally of their being called Wen, “Cultured”? Zigong came to understand the Odes through discussing learning; Zixia came to understand learning through discussing the Odes. Both grasped something beyond the expressed words and meanings; how could Confucius fail to approve equally of their fitness to discuss the Odes? Viewed in this light, Confucius embodied the Way in his substance and righteousness in his actions; his voice served as the pitch standard and his person as the measure. All his words and deeds truly constitute a standard for ten thousand generations. What grounds, then, are there for disputing the similarities and differences between these cases? This foolish student, peering through a tube and measuring with a ladle, cannot describe everything in full detail. I ask only that you, honored examiner, offer further instruction. Respectfully submitted.

Wang Wei
Fourth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor: 〔All five policy essays develop their answers well, but this one displays particular insight; therefore it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: 〔[The opening characters are garbled: 壽孔, ?] An urgent task for students is to seek to learn from the ancients, attaining breadth and then concision [?], with the pleasure of understanding gained for oneself. This essay probes deeply into ancient calligraphy and the methods of putting it into practice. Its author truly attends to the study of calligraphy and has gained something from it. It should be included as a model for students of calligraphy.〕

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: 〔Judging from this answer, its author must be someone capable of finding recreation in the arts.〕

Comment by Examiner Ke, Instructor: 〔An accomplished hand with the brush.〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對字書作而變化之體滋學書精而運用
之法密蓋書為六藝之一所以宣人文敷
治化紀六經應萬事經天而緯地皆有賴
於此者也豈他技藝之比哉誠不可以不
講也請因明問而陳其槩夫字書之作其
來尚矣自伏羲畫八卦而書契攸與蒼頡
觀鳥跡而字文以製以體天地之撰以類
萬物之情其圓應規其方應矩轉筆為圓
摺筆為方方之平為準圓之直為繩陰陽
===
五行所以成象成形者也書以方圓平直
為之主而輕重大小低昂長短斜正寓其
變焉六書之義至矣盡矣然其迭更迭變
伏羲氏有龍書神農氏有穗書軒轅氏有
垂雲書因所見而創也太昊氏為鸞書放
勳氏為龜書夏后氏為鍾鼎書隨所見而
製也自是而後史籀作大篆李斯作小篆
而隸則出於程邈焉史游作章草蔡邕作
飛白而楷則出於鍾繇焉乃若霧卷雲收
punctuated:
對：字書作，而變化之體滋；學書精，而運用之法密。蓋書為六藝之一，所以宣人文、敷治化、紀六經、應萬事，經天而緯地，皆有賴於此者也。豈他技藝之比哉？誠不可以不講也。請因明問而陳其槩。
夫字書之作，其來尚矣。自伏羲畫八卦，而書契攸與；蒼頡觀鳥跡，而字文以製。以體天地之撰，以類萬物之情。其圓應規，其方應矩；轉筆為圓，摺筆為方；方之平為準，圓之直為繩。陰陽五行，所以成象成形者也。書以方圓平直為之主，而輕重、大小、低昂、長短、斜正寓其變焉。六書之義，至矣，盡矣！然其迭更迭變，伏羲氏有龍書，神農氏有穗書，軒轅氏有垂雲書，因所見而創也；太昊氏為鸞書，放勳氏為龜書，夏后氏為鍾鼎書，隨所見而製也。自是而後，史籀作大篆，李斯作小篆，而隸則出於程邈焉；史游作章草，蔡邕作飛白，而楷則出於鍾繇焉。乃若霧卷雲收
translation_en:
In reply: As writing developed, its changing forms multiplied; as the study of calligraphy became more refined, the methods of its practice became more exact. Writing is one of the Six Arts. It makes human culture manifest, spreads the transforming influence of government, records the Six Classics, and serves the myriad affairs of life. Ordering heaven and earth depends upon it. How could it be compared with other skills and crafts? It certainly cannot go unexamined. Allow me to respond to your illuminating question by setting out its broad outlines.
The origins of writing reach far back into antiquity. When Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams, written records arose [?]; when Cangjie observed the tracks of birds, written characters were fashioned. These embodied the workings of heaven and earth and represented the nature of the myriad things. Their roundness conformed to the compass and their squareness to the carpenter’s square. Turning the brush produced roundness; folding its movement produced squareness. The level aspect of squareness served as a leveling instrument, and the straight aspect of roundness as a marking cord. Yin and yang and the Five Phases are what bring forth images and forms. Writing takes squareness, roundness, levelness, and straightness as its fundamentals, while its variations reside in lightness and heaviness, largeness and smallness, lowness and height, length and shortness, and slant and uprightness. The principles of the Six Categories of Characters are consummate and exhaustive!
Yet scripts changed and transformed in succession. Fuxi had dragon script; Shennong had grain-ear script; Xuanyuan had hanging-cloud script: they created these from what they saw. Taihao made luan-bird script; Fangxun made tortoise script; the rulers of Xia made bell-and-cauldron script: they fashioned these in accordance with what they observed. Thereafter, Shi Zhou created large-seal script and Li Si created small-seal script, while clerical script originated with Cheng Miao. Shi You created draft cursive script, Cai Yong created flying-white script, and regular script originated with Zhong Yao. As for mist rolling up and clouds drawing away…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
狀若踈而復密鳳翥龍翔勢若斜而反正
鍾王之筆妙矣然視顏魯公之雄秀獨出
有如杜詩者是其精神形於以死赴國之
時則顏之書尤濟於用也虞世南之所稱
五絕詞翰居一薛稷之筆力遒麗當時莫
及虞稷之書善矣然較之柳公拳之心正
筆正由中見外者是有得於虛靜精忠之
間則柳之書尤有所本也且古人之書逸
少嘗云得法於白雲子蔡邕嘗云得神人
===
所授八角垂芒之書人皆信其有異傳也
殊不知白雲子即心也神人亦心也心有
所契而寓言耳古人執筆逸少得其法於
羣鵞之運頸懷素得其妙於夏雲之迴風
人皆議其為好事也殊不知鵞之運頸周
回而容與也雲之迴風變幻而悠揚也曰
有所擊而心悟耳夫書札於儒事最近不
可以不學也學書之法當以執筆為先用
筆次之執筆之法所謂虛拳實腕指齊掌
punctuated: 狀若踈而復密，鳳翥龍翔，勢若斜而反正。鍾王之筆妙矣，然視顏魯公之雄秀獨出，有如杜詩者，是其精神形於以死赴國之時，則顏之書尤濟於用也。虞世南之所稱五絕，詞翰居一；薛稷之筆力遒麗，當時莫及。虞稷之書善矣，然較之柳公拳之心正筆正、由中見外者，是有得於虛靜精忠之間，則柳之書尤有所本也。且古人之書，逸少嘗云得法於白雲子，蔡邕嘗云得神人所授八角垂芒之書，人皆信其有異傳也。殊不知白雲子即心也，神人亦心也，心有所契而寓言耳。古人執筆，逸少得其法於羣鵞之運頸，懷素得其妙於夏雲之迴風，人皆議其為好事也。殊不知鵞之運頸，周回而容與也；雲之迴風，變幻而悠揚也。曰有所擊而心悟耳。夫書札於儒事最近，不可以不學也。學書之法，當以執筆為先，用筆次之。執筆之法，所謂虛拳實腕、指齊掌
translation_en:
…their forms seem open yet are dense; like phoenixes soaring and dragons flying, their disposition seems oblique yet returns to uprightness. The brushwork of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi is marvelous. Yet consider the uniquely powerful elegance of Yan Lugong (Yan Zhenqing), resembling the poetry of Du Fu: this was his spirit taking visible form when he went to his death in service to the state. Thus Yan’s calligraphy was especially effective in practical service.

Among Yu Shinan’s celebrated five excellences, literary composition and calligraphy held one place; the vigorous elegance of Xue Ji’s brushwork was unmatched in his time. Yu’s and Xue’s calligraphy was fine. Yet compare it with Liu Gongquan’s [?]: when the heart is upright, the brush is upright, and what is within manifests itself outwardly. This reflects an attainment arising from inward emptiness and stillness, and from wholehearted loyalty. Thus Liu’s calligraphy had an especially firm foundation.

Moreover, concerning the calligraphy of the ancients, Yishao (Wang Xizhi) once said that he obtained his method from Baiyunzi, and Cai Yong once said that he received from a divine being a script with eight corners and drooping points. People all believed that they had received extraordinary transmissions. They failed to understand that Baiyunzi was simply the mind, and that the divine being was also the mind. Their minds had apprehended something, and they merely expressed it through allegory.

As for how the ancients held the brush, Yishao obtained his method from the movements of a flock of geese’s necks, and Huaisu grasped its subtleties from summer clouds swirling in the wind. People all regarded these as instances of a fondness for curious pursuits. They failed to understand that geese move their necks in rounded, leisurely motions, while clouds swirling in the wind transform and drift freely. Something struck [the senses?], and the mind attained understanding—that was all.

Calligraphy is very closely related to the pursuits of a Confucian scholar and must be studied. In learning calligraphy, holding the brush should come first, and wielding it second. The method of holding the brush is what is called keeping the fist hollow and the wrist firm, the fingers aligned and the palm…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
空者執筆之際使虎口寬可容彈掌中虛
可容卵指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也所謂壓
捺鉤抉抵拒導送者壓用大指捺用食指
鉤抉用中指抵拒用無名指導送用小指
是也用筆之精鋒之或藏或出或正或側
與左用者藏則鋒藏晝中出則芒刃在外
正則鋒不偏露側則轉側取妍而左則弩
力過勁如反竹為弓者矣筆之有引有屻
有縱有複與舞動者引則引短為長屻則
===
屻長為短縱則送之欲迅複則重覆其晝
而舞則欲下不下如景山與雲者矣夫執
筆既熟用筆既精則其為書也可以追倣
古人而傳後世者矣抑豈徒為人觀美哉
蓋天文地文人文一也景星卿雲人共觀
之精金美玉人共寶之書人之心畫也人
之文也烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉愚也
行而不著習而不察姑揣摩以對未知是
否惟進而教之幸甚
punctuated:
空者，執筆之際，使虎口寬可容彈，掌中虛可容卵，指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也。所謂壓捺鉤抉抵拒導送者，壓用大指，捺用食指，鉤抉用中指，抵拒用無名指，導送用小指是也。用筆之精，鋒之或藏或出、或正或側與左用者，藏則鋒藏晝中，出則芒刃在外，正則鋒不偏露，側則轉側取妍，而左則弩力過勁，如反竹為弓者矣。筆之有引、有屻、有縱、有複與舞動者，引則引短為長，屻則屻長為短，縱則送之欲迅，複則重覆其晝，而舞則欲下不下，如景山與雲者矣。
夫執筆既熟，用筆既精，則其為書也，可以追倣古人而傳後世者矣。抑豈徒為人觀美哉？蓋天文、地文、人文一也。景星卿雲，人共觀之；精金美玉，人共寶之。書，人之心畫也，人之文也，烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉？愚也行而不著，習而不察，姑揣摩以對，未知是否，惟進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…“hollow” means that, when holding the brush, the space between thumb and forefinger should be wide enough to contain a pellet, and the hollow of the palm large enough to contain an egg; the fingers should clasp the brush lightly, while the wrist remains firm. As for the techniques called pressing, bearing down, hooking, drawing out, supporting, resisting, guiding, and sending: pressing uses the thumb; bearing down uses the forefinger; hooking and drawing out use the middle finger; supporting and resisting use the ring finger; and guiding and sending use the little finger. Refinement in handling the brush involves concealing or exposing its tip, keeping it upright or inclined, and using it toward the left. When concealed, the tip remains within the stroke [?]; when exposed, its sharp point appears outside. When upright, the tip does not protrude to either side; when inclined, it turns sideways to achieve beauty. In working toward the left, force is exerted with exceptional strength [?], like bending bamboo backward to make a bow. The brush also has movements called drawing out, shortening [?], releasing, retracing, and dancing. Drawing out extends a short stroke into a long one; shortening [?] contracts a long stroke into a short one. Releasing sends the brush onward swiftly; retracing goes back over the stroke [?]. Dancing means being about to descend yet not descending, like “Jingshan and clouds” [?].
Once one is practiced in holding the brush and accomplished in using it, one’s calligraphy can emulate the ancients and be transmitted to later generations. Surely it is not merely intended to offer others a beautiful spectacle! The patterns of Heaven, Earth, and humanity are fundamentally one. Auspicious stars and felicitous clouds are admired by all; refined gold and beautiful jade are treasured by all. Writing is the delineation of a person’s heart and the expression of that person’s refinement. How could one treat it carelessly, without seeking to attain its utmost subtlety? In my ignorance, I act without understanding and practice without examining. I have merely ventured to ponder these matters in making my reply, and do not know whether it is correct. I would be most fortunate if you would advance me with your instruction.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第五問
同考試官教諭劉　批〔斷制養士詰兵之道明確詳悉〕
范希淹
〔編故錄之〕
同考試官教諭俞　批〔處置養士詰兵之事允當無遺〕
〔無如此篇是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔時務所論鑿鑿可行有安邦之才〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔正行問意可取〕
論養士詰兵之法行於古者有優劣不能
===
不隨時以為興衰行於今者雖盡善不可
不因時而為損益蓋歷代養士詰兵之法
迄今凡幾變大率皆隨其優劣以為興衰
耳為治者欲使之常興而不衰可不因時
損益而求以盡其善哉請詳言之自古君
天下者固必資文德以致太平亦必資武
功以戡禍亂文武並用誠長治久安之計
也然而欲興文教必在於設學以養士致
成周之時遐不作人詠歌於棫樸薪槱之
punctuated:
第五問

同考試官教諭劉　批〔斷制養士詰兵之道，明確詳悉。〕
范希淹
〔編故錄之。〕
同考試官教諭俞　批〔處置養士詰兵之事，允當無遺。〕〔無如此篇，是宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔時務所論，鑿鑿可行，有安邦之才。〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔正行問意，可取。〕

論養士詰兵之法，行於古者有優劣，不能不隨時以為興衰；行於今者雖盡善，不可不因時而為損益。蓋歷代養士詰兵之法，迄今凡幾變，大率皆隨其優劣以為興衰耳。為治者欲使之常興而不衰，可不因時損益而求以盡其善哉？請詳言之。自古君天下者，固必資文德以致太平，亦必資武功以戡禍亂。文武並用，誠長治久安之計也。然而欲興文教，必在於設學以養士。致成周之時，遐不作人，詠歌於《棫樸》薪槱之
translation_en:
Fifth Question

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The judgments concerning the methods of nurturing scholars and putting the troops in order are clear, precise, detailed, and comprehensive.〕
Fan Xiyan
〔Compiled, therefore recorded here [?].〕
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔The handling of matters concerning the nurturing of scholars and the ordering of troops is appropriate and leaves nothing out.〕〔None equals this essay; it deserves to be selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔Its arguments on current affairs are sound and practicable; the author has the talent to bring stability to the state.〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It directly follows the purport of the question [?] and is worthy of selection.〕

As for methods of nurturing scholars and putting the troops in order, those practiced in antiquity had strengths and weaknesses and inevitably flourished or declined with the times. Those practiced today, even if wholly good, must undergo reductions and additions as circumstances require. Indeed, how many changes have the successive dynasties’ methods of nurturing scholars and ordering troops undergone down to the present? Broadly speaking, their flourishing or decline has followed their respective strengths and weaknesses. If those who govern wish these methods always to flourish and never to decline, can they fail to adjust them to the times and seek to perfect their merits? Allow me to explain in detail.

From antiquity, those who ruled All-under-Heaven necessarily relied on civil virtue to bring about peace, but also on military achievements to quell calamity and disorder. Employing both civil and military means is indeed the plan for lasting order and enduring peace. Yet promoting civil instruction necessarily depends upon establishing schools to nurture scholars. By the time of the Zhou at its height, “How could they fail to cultivate men?” was sung in the song of stacked firewood, The Oak and the Shrub (Yupu) …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
繇鎬京辟雍揄揚於豊芑有事之際養士
之美無以加矣自是而後若漢武帝為博
士而置弟子員明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮
唐太宗徵天下名儒增廣生員玄宗令天
下州縣里皆置學宋初既設太學武學以
教天下之士其後復設宗學以教宗室之
士漢唐宋之養士大槩如此而永平貞觀
為最盛惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以為
教耳我
===
太祖高皇帝既定天下乃設學校以養士其始
也士有定額而選之也精學有常規而教
之也嚴斥異端而以正道淑人黜詞賦而
以經術取士其法美矣漸涵既久秀民日
多遂因而漸變至于今名州大邑增至數
倍司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中或
䠊於逸樂而挑達城闕或急於進取而貪
緣攀貴至壓
宸慮特
punctuated:
繇，鎬京辟雍揄揚於豊芑有事之際，養士之美無以加矣。自是而後，若漢武帝為博士而置弟子員，明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮；唐太宗徵天下名儒，增廣生員，玄宗令天下州縣里皆置學；宋初既設太學、武學以教天下之士，其後復設宗學以教宗室之士。漢唐宋之養士大槩如此，而永平、貞觀為最盛，惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以為教耳。
我太祖高皇帝既定天下，乃設學校以養士。其始也，士有定額，而選之也精；學有常規，而教之也嚴。斥異端而以正道淑人，黜詞賦而以經術取士，其法美矣。漸涵既久，秀民日多，遂因而漸變。至于今，名州大邑增至數倍。司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中，或䠊於逸樂而挑達城闕，或急於進取而貪緣攀貴，至壓宸慮，特
translation_en:
…song; Haojing and its Biyong ceremonial academy were celebrated in verses concerning luxuriant millet and ceremonial affairs [?]. Nothing could surpass this excellence in nurturing scholars. Thereafter, Emperor Wu of the Han established student places under the Erudites, and Emperor Ming visited the Biyong and performed the ceremony honoring the aged. Emperor Taizong of the Tang summoned eminent Confucian scholars from throughout the realm and increased student enrollment; Emperor Xuanzong ordered schools established in every prefecture, county, and village throughout the realm. Early in the Song, the Imperial University and the Military School were established to educate the scholars of the realm; later, schools for the imperial clan were also established to educate its members. Such, in broad outline, was the nurturing of scholars under the Han, Tang, and Song. It flourished most during the Yongping and Zhenguan eras. Regrettably, they could not emulate the Zhou at its height by personally practicing benevolence and righteousness as the basis of instruction.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had pacified the realm, he established schools to nurture scholars. At first, student numbers were fixed and selection was exacting; schools had standing regulations and instruction was strict. Heterodox teachings were rejected, and people were improved through the correct Way; lyric poetry and rhapsodies were set aside, and scholars were selected through their learning in the Classics. These arrangements were excellent. After prolonged cultivation, talented people grew daily more numerous, and the arrangements gradually changed accordingly. By now, enrollment in prominent prefectures and large counties has increased severalfold. Those responsible for governance and education have proved unable to keep the students within the bounds of the rules. Some stray into idle pleasures [?], idly roaming the city towers; others, impatient for advancement, greedily cultivate connections and attach themselves to the powerful. Matters have reached the point of weighing upon the imperial mind, and a special…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
勑憲臣以提督之猶不能盡弭其弊也爲今
之計竊以爲宜沙之汰之使玉石不得以
兼收艾之鋤之使苗莠不得以雜植仍愼
擇有德行道藝者以爲之帥躬廉恥以正
其行明義理以澤其文尊其賢以激其不
及嘉其善而矜其不能則養士之法其庶
幾乎欲奮武備又在於講武以詰兵故成
周之時居則爲比閭族黨州鄉之民行則
爲伍兩卒旅軍師之衆其詰兵之法無以
===
尚矣自是而後南軍主守衛王宮北軍主
巡徼京城此漢之兵也諸府六百三十四
所關中三百六十一所得強榦弱枝之法
有居重馭輕之勢其後一變而爲彍騎其
制遂壞再變而爲方鎭其制大壞此唐之
兵也以五代之摳家偏重則以文臣爲之
以五代之藩鎭太横則以文臣任之禁將
之責者爲三衙禁旅之要者爲四廂諸司
募者曰役兵諸州募者曰廂兵什伍其民
punctuated:
勑憲臣以提督之，猶不能盡弭其弊也。爲今之計，竊以爲宜沙之汰之，使玉石不得以兼收；艾之鋤之，使苗莠不得以雜植。仍愼擇有德行道藝者以爲之帥，躬廉恥以正其行，明義理以澤其文，尊其賢以激其不及，嘉其善而矜其不能，則養士之法其庶幾乎！
欲奮武備，又在於講武以詰兵。故成周之時，居則爲比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則爲伍兩卒旅軍師之衆，其詰兵之法無以尚矣。自是而後，南軍主守衛王宮，北軍主巡徼京城，此漢之兵也。諸府六百三十四所，關中三百六十一所，得強榦弱枝之法，有居重馭輕之勢。其後一變而爲彍騎，其制遂壞；再變而爲方鎭，其制大壞，此唐之兵也。以五代之摳家偏重，則以文臣爲之；以五代之藩鎭太横，則以文臣任之。禁將之責者爲三衙，禁旅之要者爲四廂。諸司募者曰役兵，諸州募者曰廂兵，什伍其民
translation_en:
…ordered the censorial officials to supervise them, yet even this could not entirely eliminate the abuses. As a plan for the present, I humbly believe that they should be sifted and culled, so that jade and common stones are not accepted together; cut back and weeded out, so that grain and weeds are not planted together. Furthermore, men of virtuous conduct, understanding of the Way, and cultivated accomplishments should be carefully selected to lead them. They should embody integrity and a sense of shame to rectify the students’ conduct, elucidate moral principles to enrich their writing, honor the worthy among them to spur on those who fall short, commend their good qualities, and show compassion for their shortcomings. Would this not bring the methods of nurturing scholars close to the ideal?
To strengthen military preparedness likewise requires military training to put the armed forces in order. Thus, in the flourishing age of Zhou, at home the people belonged to neighborhood and territorial groupings—bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; on campaign they formed military units—wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. No method of ordering the armed forces could surpass this. Thereafter, the Southern Army was chiefly responsible for guarding the imperial palace, and the Northern Army for patrolling the capital: these were the forces of Han. There were 634 military headquarters, of which 361 were in Guanzhong. This achieved the method of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, establishing a configuration in which the weight concentrated at the center controlled the lighter forces elsewhere. Subsequently, a first transformation produced the Expanded Cavalry (Guoqi), and the system deteriorated; a second transformation produced regional military commands, and the system deteriorated gravely. These were the forces of Tang. Because the ‘koujia’ [?] of the Five Dynasties had held disproportionate power, civil officials were appointed to perform those functions; because the regional military commands of the Five Dynasties had been excessively overbearing, civil officials were appointed to take charge of them. Responsibility for commanding the palace armies lay with the Three Commands, while the principal divisions of the palace forces were the Four Wings. Those recruited by the various government offices were called service troops; those recruited by the prefectures were called prefectural troops. The people were organized into groups of ten and five…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
而教之曰民兵籓民內附而用之曰籓兵此
宋之兵也漢唐宋之詰兵大槩如此而唐
之府兵則為最優以其有成周寓兵於農
之遺意耳我
太祖高皇帝既一宇內乃設衛所以詰兵其始
也軍數盈而行伍以飭師律嚴而訓練以
時以戰則勝以攻則克其法善矣承平既
久文恬武嬉遂因而漸弊亡絕者無日而
續逃避者莫從而稽名數雖存在任無幾
===
國無捕者恒無以遏亂於緩急之際無事
則催備差遣有事則借募民兵至座
宸慮特
勑御史以清理之終亦不能悉復其舊也為
今之計竊以為宜復
祖宗官吏枉法受財之典以補其亡絕之數復
祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律以警其脫放之弊其
於清理之際則審閱其版籍以清其源及
其發遣之時則嚴切其文移以防其欺仍
punctuated:
而教之，曰民兵；籓民內附而用之，曰籓兵。此宋之兵也。漢唐宋之詰兵，大槩如此，而唐之府兵則為最優，以其有成周寓兵於農之遺意耳。我太祖高皇帝既一宇內，乃設衛所以詰兵。其始也，軍數盈而行伍以飭，師律嚴而訓練以時，以戰則勝，以攻則克，其法善矣。承平既久，文恬武嬉，遂因而漸弊。亡絕者無日而續，逃避者莫從而稽，名數雖存，在任無幾。國無捕者，恒無以遏亂於緩急之際。無事則催備差遣，有事則借募民兵，至座宸慮，特勑御史以清理之，終亦不能悉復其舊也。
為今之計，竊以為宜復祖宗官吏枉法受財之典，以補其亡絕之數；復祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律，以警其脫放之弊。其於清理之際，則審閱其版籍以清其源；及其發遣之時，則嚴切其文移以防其欺，仍
translation_en:
…and train them, calling them militia; when people of the frontier submit to imperial authority and are employed as soldiers, they are called frontier troops. Such were the forces of the Song. These, broadly, were the military arrangements of the Han, Tang, and Song. The Tang regimental militia system was the best, because it preserved something of the flourishing Zhou practice of embedding soldiers among the farming population. After our Emperor Taizu Gao unified the realm, he established guards and battalions to organize the armed forces. At first, troop strength was full and the ranks orderly; military discipline was strict and training conducted at the proper times. They won in battle and prevailed in assaults: the system was sound. But after a long peace, civil officials grew complacent and military officers indolent, and the system gradually deteriorated. Those who died or whose households became extinct were never replaced [?], and there was no means of tracking down those who fled or evaded service. Though their names remained on the rolls, few were actually serving. The state had no one to apprehend offenders [?] and was continually unable to suppress disorder in emergencies. In quiet times, troops were pressed to prepare for assigned duties; when trouble arose, recourse was made to recruiting militia. This came to trouble the imperial mind [?], and a special order directed investigating censors to inspect and rectify the rolls. Yet even then the original establishment could not be fully restored.
As for present measures, I humbly believe that the ancestral emperors’ provision concerning officials and clerks who accept payment to pervert the law should be reinstated, to replenish the numbers lost through death and household extinction. Their statute concerning military officers who commit private offenses should also be reinstated, to deter abuses involving unauthorized release from service. During the inspection and rectification, the registers should be carefully examined to put the underlying records in order; when men are dispatched, official correspondence should be handled with strict care to prevent deception. Furthermore, …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
申嚴衛所尅減月粮之罪痛革官吏侵漁
朘剝之暴使各遂事育之願而不動懷土
之思則詰兵之法其庶幾乎夫養士詰兵
二者皆
國家之大政而九有志於學古入官者誠不
可以不究心也然管見如斯未知是否惟
執事進而教之
punctuated: 申嚴衛所尅減月粮之罪，痛革官吏侵漁朘剝之暴，使各遂事育之願，而不動懷土之思，則詰兵之法，其庶幾乎？夫養士、詰兵二者，皆國家之大政，而九有志於學古入官者，誠不可以不究心也。然管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事進而教之。
translation_en:
…reinforce the penalties for withholding portions of the monthly grain rations in the guards and battalions, and rigorously eliminate the brutal exploitation and extortion practiced by officials and clerks. Let each man fulfill his wish to support his parents and provide for his children, without stirring thoughts of his native place. Would this not bring the system of military administration close to its proper standard?
Nurturing scholars and putting the military in order are both major affairs of state. Those [?] who aspire to study antiquity and enter official service must indeed give them careful consideration. Such, however, are my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I ask only that you, honored examiners, grant me further instruction.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
弘治壬子秋
今聖天子取士第二科也江西試
事畢將錄所得士以
獻鑰當序其後竊惟科目以文
章校士蓋欲於言語文字之
間以觀人耳非徒以其辭而
===
已也士患不深於道爾深於
道將自裕於言以是觀人其
庶幾哉若乃移舊繡之曲折
於短褐而謂世方無華裾取
殘餕而飣餖爲華饌而謂世
方無正味若此者吾不知其
於道何如耶如是而欲觀其
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

弘治壬子秋，今聖天子取士第二科也。江西試事畢，將錄所得士以獻，鑰當序其後。竊惟科目以文章校士，蓋欲於言語文字之間以觀人耳，非徒以其辭而已也。士患不深於道爾，深於道，將自裕於言。以是觀人，其庶幾哉！若乃移舊繡之曲折於短褐，而謂世方無華裾；取殘餕而飣餖爲華饌，而謂世方無正味。若此者，吾不知其於道何如耶？如是而欲觀其
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The autumn of the renzi year of Hongzhi [1492] marked the second examination cycle for selecting scholars under our present sagely Son of Heaven. With the Jiangxi examination concluded, a record of the scholars selected was to be compiled and presented to the throne. It fell to me, Yue 鑰, to write its postface.

I venture to reflect that the examination system assesses scholars through their compositions because it seeks to discern the person through language and writing, not merely to judge his phrasing. What a scholar should fear is insufficient depth in the Way. With depth in the Way, he will naturally possess ample resources for expression. By this means, might we come close to discerning the person?

But suppose someone transfers the intricate patterns of old embroidery onto a short garment of coarse cloth, claiming that the world now has no splendid robes; or arranges leftovers into an elaborate feast, claiming that the world now has no true flavors. Of such a person, I cannot tell how he stands in relation to the Way. Under these circumstances, to seek to discern his…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
人不亦難乎此擇士者所以
怵心駭目不敢以易視也粥
爲
國家得一天下士則異時亦足
以爲天下重然舉者非私黨
舉之者非私恩此翟璜所以
不敢與魏成比而李克所以
不敢比周翟璜也或曰燕得
樂毅亦自隗起駿骨不遺則
千里之材自至於乎緋細熟
視於沙丘之野尚恐或失之
牝牡驪黃之外敢謂吾能得
其內而忘其外哉尚敢爲消
人之獻哉
punctuated: 人，不亦難乎？此擇士者所以怵心駭目，不敢以易視也。粥爲國家得一天下士，則異時亦足以爲天下重。然舉者非私黨，舉之者非私恩，此翟璜所以不敢與魏成比，而李克所以不敢比周翟璜也。或曰：「燕得樂毅，亦自隗起；駿骨不遺，則千里之材自至。」於乎！緋細熟視於沙丘之野，尚恐或失之牝牡驪黃之外，敢謂吾能得其內而忘其外哉？尚敢爲消人之獻哉？
translation_en:
…would it not also be difficult to discern the man? This is why those who select scholars are apprehensive and alarmed, and dare not regard the task lightly. If [?] one secures for the state a single scholar of outstanding talent in all the realm, he may in time carry weight throughout the realm. Yet those recommended are not private partisans, nor do those recommending them confer private favors. This is why Zhai Huang did not dare compare himself with Wei Cheng, and why Li Ke did not dare form a partisan alliance with Zhai Huang.

Someone says: “Yan’s acquisition of Yue Yi also began with [Guo] Wei. If even the bones of a fine horse are not spurned, talent capable of traveling a thousand li will come of itself.” Alas! Even when scrutinizing closely [?] in the open country of Shaqiu, one still fears failing to discern what lies beyond whether a horse is female or male, black or yellow. Dare I claim that I can grasp what is within and disregard what is without? Dare I further make the offering of a ‘xiao person’ [消人, unclear]?

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓
導孫鑰謹序
punctuated: 直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓導孫鑰謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully written by Sun Yue, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text: □序
punctuated: □序
translation_en: [Illegible character] Preface [?]

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
江西爲東南大藩自昔賢才
之盛甲於天下至我
朝而尤盛
聖天子嗣大歷服改元弘治之五
年適當大比
詔兩畿十三省如制舉行廵按
===
監察御史韓明暨藩臬重臣
仰體
德意預謀聘儒碩以典文衡而
鎮守太監鄧原雅重斯文清
戎御史魏英所至激勸工部
員外郎臧麟主事張瑞適以
事來亦皆同心協贊期得真
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

江西爲東南大藩，自昔賢才之盛甲於天下，至我朝而尤盛。聖天子嗣大歷服，改元弘治之五年，適當大比，詔兩畿十三省如制舉行。廵按監察御史韓明暨藩臬重臣，仰體德意，預謀聘儒碩以典文衡。而鎮守太監鄧原雅重斯文，清戎御史魏英所至激勸，工部員外郎臧麟、主事張瑞適以事來，亦皆同心協贊，期得真
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Jiangxi is a great province of the southeast. Since ancient times, its abundance of worthy and talented men has ranked foremost in the realm; under our dynasty, it has flourished still more. The sagely Son of Heaven succeeded to the imperial throne, and the fifth year of his Hongzhi reign coincided with the triennial examination. He commanded the two metropolitan regions and the thirteen provinces to conduct it according to the established regulations. Han Ming, the Regional Inspector serving as an Investigating Censor, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, respectfully carrying out the emperor’s benevolent intentions, planned in advance to engage eminent scholars to preside over the literary assessment.

Deng Yuan, the Grand Defender serving as a eunuch Director, had long held literary learning in high esteem. Wei Ying, the censor charged with rectifying military affairs, encouraged learning wherever he went. Zang Lin, an Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works, and Zhang Rui, a Secretary in that ministry, happened to arrive on official business. They too joined wholeheartedly in supporting the undertaking, hoping to obtain true…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
才以充實用而提學僉事黃
〔仲昭〕簡自詞垣舊僚作興士
類惟公惟嚴肆人材之成視
昔益盛士之抱藝就試者雲
蒸霧滃至四千有奇巡按御
史乃會藩臬嚴加覆試汰黜
過半至期鎖院而三試之內
===
而提督則左布政使沈〔暉〕按
察使魏〔富〕副使洪〔鍾〕左參議
張〔以弘〕外而防範則右布政
使韓〔邦問〕左參政陳〔瑗〕副使
張璁吳〔璸〕左參議潘〔祺〕右參
議李〔魁〕僉事江〔源〕羅〔九鼎〕陳
〔祥〕趙〔良〕汪〔舜民〕張〔源潔〕洎〔民〕
punctuated: 才，以充實用。而提學僉事黃〔仲昭〕簡自詞垣舊僚，作興士類，惟公惟嚴，肆人材之成，視昔益盛。士之抱藝就試者，雲蒸霧滃，至四千有奇。巡按御史乃會藩臬，嚴加覆試，汰黜過半。至期，鎖院而三試之。內而提督，則左布政使沈〔暉〕、按察使魏〔富〕、副使洪〔鍾〕、左參議張〔以弘〕；外而防範，則右布政使韓〔邦問〕、左參政陳〔瑗〕、副使張璁、吳〔璸〕、左參議潘〔祺〕、右參議李〔魁〕、僉事江〔源〕、羅〔九鼎〕、陳〔祥〕、趙〔良〕、汪〔舜民〕、張〔源潔〕，洎〔民〕
translation_en:
…talent to meet practical needs. Huang Zhongzhao, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner overseeing education, had been selected from among former Hanlin Academy colleagues. He fostered the scholars with impartiality and strictness, so that the cultivation of talent flourished more than before. Scholars bringing their learning to the examination gathered like rising clouds and billowing mist, numbering over four thousand. The Regional Inspector then convened the provincial administration and surveillance officials and subjected the candidates to a rigorous further examination, eliminating more than half. At the appointed time, the examination compound was sealed, and the candidates were examined in three sessions.

Within the compound, supervision was undertaken by Shen Hui, Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Left; Wei Fu, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; Hong Zhong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Zhang Yihong, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left. Outside, security was undertaken by Han Bangwen, Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Right; Chen Yuan, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left; Zhang Cong and Wu Bin, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Pan Qi, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Left; Li Kui, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right; and Jiang Yuan, Luo Jiuding, Chen Xiang, Zhao Liang, Wang Shunmin, and Zhang Yuanjie, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; as well as Min [?] …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
百執事皆極一時之選而綜
理綱維則御史明寔監臨之
矢心協力罔有怠忽乃去乃
取僅遵
制額得中式者九十有五人固
不敢自謂如鑑之明妍媸畢
見如衡之平重輕適當然所
===
以去取一出於至公未始敢
有毫髮容心於其間也宋歐
陽子有曰科目取士無情如
造化至公如權衡諒哉不誣
雖然
天佑國家必生賢才以遺之豈
無意哉人君養士以學校取
punctuated:
百執事皆極一時之選，而綜理綱維，則御史明寔監臨之。矢心協力，罔有怠忽。乃去乃取，僅遵制額，得中式者九十有五人。固不敢自謂如鑑之明，妍媸畢見；如衡之平，重輕適當。然所以去取，一出於至公，未始敢有毫髮容心於其間也。宋歐陽子有曰：「科目取士，無情如造化，至公如權衡。」諒哉，不誣！
雖然，天佑國家，必生賢才以遺之，豈無意哉？人君養士以學校，取
translation_en:
…All the functionaries were among the finest men of their time; overall direction and supervision rested with the Censor Ming Shi, who served as Supervising Official. They pledged their wholehearted cooperation, with no negligence or inattention. In rejecting some candidates and accepting others, they strictly observed the prescribed quota, selecting ninety-five successful candidates. We certainly dare not claim that our judgment was like a bright mirror, revealing every beauty and blemish, or like an evenly balanced scale, weighing heavy and light with perfect accuracy. Yet our decisions to reject or accept proceeded entirely from the utmost impartiality; we never dared allow the slightest personal inclination to intrude. Master Ouyang of the Song once said: “Selecting men through the examinations is without partiality, like the workings of creation, and utterly impartial, like a balance.” True indeed, and no empty assertion!
Nevertheless, when Heaven blesses the state, it surely brings forth worthy and talented men to bestow upon it. Could this be without purpose? The ruler nurtures scholars through schools and selects…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
士以科目而付拳衡責公當
於有司亦惟體天意務得人
以致理耳書曰惟天純佑命
則商實曰顲俊尊上帝皆此
意也恭惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺天眷奄有寰區
文命誕敷聲教四訖
===
列聖繼作百二十餘年造就簡拔
恩意愈厚譽髦魁傑彙興輩出
翼維太平熙洽之運於億萬
斯年之永殆逈軼於前古未
可謂無意而可致也凡茲俊
造登名賢錄毋曰所業自中
於程度主司一出於無情遂
punctuated:
士以科目，而付拳衡，責公當於有司，亦惟體天意，務得人以致理耳。《書》曰：「惟天純佑命，則商實。」曰：「顲俊尊上帝。」皆此意也。恭惟我太祖高皇帝誕膺天眷，奄有寰區，文命誕敷，聲教四訖。
列聖繼作，百二十餘年，造就簡拔，恩意愈厚。譽髦魁傑，彙興輩出，翼維太平熙洽之運，於億萬斯年之永，殆逈軼於前古，未可謂無意而可致也。凡茲俊造，登名賢錄，毋曰所業自中於程度，主司一出於無情，遂
translation_en:
…men through the examinations, entrusting the balance of judgment [?] to the responsible officials and requiring fairness and sound judgment from them. This, too, is simply to embody Heaven’s intent and strive to obtain worthy men so as to achieve good government. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven generously protected the mandate, and thus Shang flourished.” It also says: “[?] outstanding men, honoring the Lord on High.” Both express this intention. Reverently we consider how our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s favor in full measure and possessed the entire realm. His civil ordinances spread far and wide, and his civilizing influence reached all four quarters.
Successive sage emperors have carried on his work. For more than one hundred and twenty years, their gracious concern for nurturing and selecting men of talent has grown ever greater. Eminent talents [?] and outstanding men have arisen in multitudes, generation after generation, sustaining an age of peace, prosperity, and harmony for countless years to come. This surely far surpasses antiquity; it cannot be said that such results could have been achieved without deliberate intent. All you accomplished men whose names are entered in this record of the worthy must not say that your work naturally met the prescribed standards and that the presiding examiners acted wholly without personal feeling, and consequently …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
翛然自得無意於圖報行將
進春官對
大廷服官援政尚思天之所以生
乎我
朝家所以造就乎我有司所以
奉持鑑衡以鑒別稱量乎我
式克至于今日果何爲哉毋
===
亦爲國爲民而已必勉圖報
稱奮庸勵翼匪躬匪懈如先
正所謂主爾忘身國爾忘家
公爾忘私以期無負於天意
無負於
國恩無負於有司薦賢爲國之
公斯有光於科目否則非所
punctuated: 翛然自得，無意於圖報。行將進春官，對大廷，服官援政，尚思天之所以生乎我，朝家所以造就乎我，有司所以奉持鑑衡以鑒別稱量乎我，式克至于今日，果何爲哉？毋亦爲國爲民而已！必勉圖報稱，奮庸勵翼，匪躬匪懈，如先正所謂「主爾忘身，國爾忘家，公爾忘私」，以期無負於天意，無負於國恩，無負於有司薦賢爲國之公，斯有光於科目。否則非所
translation_en: …carefree and self-satisfied, with no thought of repaying what you have received. Soon you will advance to the Ministry of Rites for examination, answer before the imperial court, take office, and assist in governance. You should still reflect: Heaven brought me into being; the dynasty nurtured me; and the responsible officials upheld the mirror and scales by which they discerned and weighed my worth, enabling me to reach this day—for what purpose, after all? Is it not simply to serve the state and the people? You must strive to repay these favors fittingly, exert yourselves in service, and diligently render assistance, neither considering yourselves nor growing lax. As a worthy predecessor said: “Think of your ruler and forget yourself; think of the state and forget your family; think of the public good and forget private interests.” Thus may you prove worthy of Heaven’s intent, of the dynasty’s grace, and of the impartial spirit in which the responsible officials recommend worthy men for the state. Only then will you bring honor to the examination system. Otherwise, this is not what…

昔所自期待意故事鄉試有
錄進
御僉謂〔德贊〕宜序首簡於是乎書
直隸淮安府山陽縣儒學教
諭柯〔德贊〕謹序
punctuated:
期望於諸士，而亦非諸士平昔所自期待意。故事，鄉試有錄進御，僉謂〔德贊〕宜序首簡，於是乎書。
直隸淮安府山陽縣儒學教諭柯〔德贊〕謹序。
translation_en:
…what is expected of you scholars, nor would it accord with the aspirations you have always held for yourselves. By established practice, a record of the Provincial Examination is presented to the Emperor. All agreed that I, 〔Dezan〕, should compose a preface for its opening pages; hence I have written this.
Respectfully prefaced by Ke 〔Dezan〕, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shanyang County, Huai’an Prefecture, in the directly administered region (Zhili).
