title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舉直錯諸枉能使枉者直
所求乎子以事父未能也所求乎臣以事
君未能也所求乎弟以事兄未能也所
求乎朋友先施之未能也
君子所性仁義禮智根於心其生色也睟
然見於面盎於背施於四體四體不言
而喻
===
易
盥而不薦有孚顒若
恒亨无咎利貞久於其道也天地之道恒
久而不已也利有攸往終則有始也
範圍天地之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺
通乎晝夜之道而知故神无方而易无
體
夫易彰往而察來而微顯闡幽
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。

所求乎子，以事父，未能也；所求乎臣，以事君，未能也；所求乎弟，以事兄，未能也；所求乎朋友，先施之，未能也。

君子所性，仁義禮智根於心。其生色也，睟然見於面，盎於背，施於四體；四體不言而喻。

易

盥而不薦，有孚顒若。

恒，亨，无咎，利貞，久於其道也。天地之道，恒久而不已也。利有攸往，終則有始也。

範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，故神无方而易无體。

夫易，彰往而察來，而微顯闡幽。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Raise up the upright and place them over the crooked: this can make the crooked upright.

What I require of a son, I have not yet been able to practice in serving my father; what I require of a minister, I have not yet been able to practice in serving my ruler; what I require of a younger brother, I have not yet been able to practice in serving my elder brother; what I require of friends, I have not yet been able to take the initiative in doing for them.

What the gentleman possesses by nature—benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom—is rooted in his heart. Its expression appears as a pure radiance in his face, fills his back, and extends through his four limbs. His four limbs convey it without words.

Book of Changes

The ritual washing has been performed, but the offering has not yet been presented; there is sincerity and an air of reverence.

“Constancy brings success, with no blame; perseverance is beneficial”: this means enduring in one's way. The way of Heaven and Earth endures without ceasing. “It is beneficial to have somewhere to go”: an ending is followed by a beginning.

It encompasses the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding them, brings the myriad things to completion in all their particulars without omission, and comprehends the way of day and night. Thus the numinous has no fixed location, and change has no fixed form.

The Changes makes the past manifest and examines what is to come; it brings the subtle to light and reveals the hidden.

Book of Documents

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
九州攸同四隩既宅九山刊旅九川滌源
九澤既陂四海會同
協于克一俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一
哉王心
是之謂大同身其康彊子孫其逢吉
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
彼有不穫穉此有不歛穧彼有遺秉此
===
有滯穗伊寡婦之利
肆不殄厥愠亦不隕厥問柞棫拔矣行道
兑矣混夷駾矣維其喙矣虞芮質厥成
文王蹶厥生予曰有疏附予曰有先後
予曰有奔奏予曰有禦侮
昭茲來許繩其祖武於萬斯年受天之祜
儀式刑文王之典日靖四方伊嘏文王既
右享之
春秋
punctuated:
咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。
九州攸同，四隩既宅，九山刊旅，九川滌源，九澤既陂，四海會同。
協于克一，俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」
是之謂大同，身其康彊，子孫其逢吉。

詩
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。彼有不穫穉，此有不歛穧；彼有遺秉，此有滯穗：伊寡婦之利。
肆不殄厥愠，亦不隕厥問。柞棫拔矣，行道兑矣。混夷駾矣，維其喙矣。虞芮質厥成，文王蹶厥生。予曰有疏附，予曰有先後，予曰有奔奏，予曰有禦侮。
昭茲來許，繩其祖武。於萬斯年，受天之祜。
儀式刑文王之典，日靖四方。伊嘏文王，既右享之。

春秋
translation_en:
Ah! You twenty-two men, be reverent! Assist in accomplishing Heaven’s work.

The nine provinces were brought into accord. The habitable lands in all four quarters were settled; the nine mountains had their trees cleared and their sacrifices performed; the nine rivers were cleared to their sources; the nine marshes were embanked; and all within the four seas came together in unity.

Be united in attaining singleness of purpose, so that all the people say, “Great are the king’s words!” and also say, “Single is the king’s heart!”

This is called the Great Accord. You yourself will enjoy health and strength, and your descendants will meet with good fortune.

Book of Odes

Dense clouds gather, bringing plentiful rain. Rain upon our public fields, and then reach our private fields. There is late-ripening grain left unreaped; here are cut stalks left ungathered. There are handfuls left behind; here are ears that remain: these are for the benefit of widows.

Thus he did not put an end to his indignation, nor did he let his good repute fall. The oaks and white oaks were cleared away, and the roads were opened. The Kunyi fled headlong, gasping for breath. Yu and Rui submitted their dispute for settlement, and King Wen awakened their good nature. I say he had men who brought the distant into close allegiance; I say he had men who guided and assisted him; I say he had men who hastened in his service; I say he had men who resisted aggression.

Enlighten these generations to come, that they may follow their ancestors’ footsteps. For ten thousand years, may they receive Heaven’s blessings.

Take King Wen’s statutes as your model and pattern; daily bring peace to the four quarters. Then great King Wen will graciously accept and enjoy these offerings.

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
會王世子于首止〔僖公五年〕
初稅畆〔宣公十五年〕作丘甲〔成公元年〕用田賦〔哀公
十二年〕
二月辛巳立武宮〔成公六年〕
遂城虎牢〔襄公二年〕戍鄭虎牢楚公子貞帥
師救鄭〔襄公十年〕
禮記
太傅審父子君臣之道以示之少傅奉世
===
子以觀太傅之德行而審喻之
禮器是故大備大備盛德也禮釋回增美
質措則正施則行其在人也如竹箭之
有筠也如松栢之有心也二者居天下
之大端矣故貫四時而不改柯易葉故
君子有禮則外諧而內無怨故物無不
懷仁鬼神饗德
山立時行盛氣顛實揚休玉色
樂著太始而禮居成物
punctuated:
公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王世子于首止。〔僖公五年〕
初稅畆。〔宣公十五年〕作丘甲。〔成公元年〕用田賦。〔哀公十二年〕
二月辛巳，立武宮。〔成公六年〕
遂城虎牢。〔襄公二年〕戍鄭虎牢，楚公子貞帥師救鄭。〔襄公十年〕
禮記
太傅審父子、君臣之道以示之，少傅奉世子以觀太傅之德行而審喻之。
禮器，是故大備。大備，盛德也。禮釋回，增美質，措則正，施則行。其在人也，如竹箭之有筠也，如松栢之有心也。二者居天下之大端矣，故貫四時而不改柯易葉。故君子有禮，則外諧而內無怨，故物無不懷仁，鬼神饗德。
山立，時行，盛氣顛實，揚休，玉色。
樂著太始，而禮居成物。
translation_en:
The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi.〕
For the first time, a tax was levied on fields by the mu. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕 Military levies were imposed on the qiu land units. 〔First year of Duke Cheng.〕 A military levy based on farmland was introduced. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Ai.〕
In the second month, on the xinsi day, the temple of Duke Wu was established. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng.〕
They then fortified Hulao. 〔Second year of Duke Xiang.〕 A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng; Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕
Record of Rites
The Grand Preceptor carefully examines the Way governing fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, and demonstrates it to the heir apparent. The Junior Preceptor accompanies the heir apparent to observe the Grand Preceptor’s virtuous conduct and explains it thoroughly to him.
Ritual is an instrument and is therefore all-encompassing. Such completeness constitutes flourishing virtue. Ritual dispels perversity and enhances fine natural qualities; established, it brings correctness; put into practice, it takes effect. In a person, it is like the outer skin of bamboo or the heartwood of pine and cypress. These plants embody great principles of the world: through all four seasons, they neither alter their branches nor change their leaves. Thus, when a gentleman possesses ritual propriety, he is harmonious outwardly and free of resentment inwardly. Hence all beings cherish his benevolence, and ghosts and spirits accept the offerings made through his virtue.
He stands like a mountain and moves in accordance with the seasons; his vital energy is abundant, his bearing full and substantial; he displays gracious beauty, and his complexion is like jade.
Music manifests the primordial beginning, while ritual resides in things brought to completion.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第貳塲
論
萬世大君
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正能直言極諫詔〔文帝二年〕
擬宋以司馬光為尚書左僕射兼門下侍
郎誥〔元祐元年〕
擬賀
冊立
===
皇太子表
判語五條
講讀律令
荒蕪田土
孳生馬疋
恐嚇取財
侵占街道
第叄塲
策五道
punctuated:
第貳塲。
論：萬世大君。
詔誥表〔內科壹道〕：擬漢舉賢良方正能直言極諫詔〔文帝二年〕；擬宋以司馬光為尚書左僕射兼門下侍郎誥〔元祐元年〕；擬賀冊立皇太子表。
判語五條：講讀律令；荒蕪田土；孳生馬疋；恐嚇取財；侵占街道。
第叄塲。
策五道。
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse: “The Great Ruler for Myriad Generations.”

Imperial edict, appointment proclamation, and memorial [one topic in this category [?]]:
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor calling for the recommendation of worthy, upright men capable of speaking frankly and remonstrating unreservedly [second year of Emperor Wen’s reign].
Compose a Song appointment proclamation making Sima Guang Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Chancellery [first year of the Yuanyou era].
Compose a memorial congratulating the emperor on the formal investiture of the Crown Prince.

Five legal judgments:
Lecturing on and studying the statutes and ordinances.
Farmland left uncultivated.
Breeding horses.
Extorting property through intimidation.
Encroaching upon streets.

Third Session

Five policy questions.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
問孔子論居上必以寬爲本答問政亦以
寬爲言是則寬之云者誠居上爲政之
先務也我
太祖高皇帝奉
天出治創制立法
大誥三編深嚴懲惡之典似與孔子之言異
矣然而
御宇建極餘三十年興道致治之隆足以匹
休於殷湯周武其故何歟伊尹訓太甲
有曰率乃祖攸行傳說告高宗亦曰監
先王成憲是則法祖之云者誠繼體守
文之先務也我
太祖高皇帝創業垂統佑啓後人
祖訓一書深戒用法之嚴又似與伊傅之言
殊矣然而
聖子神孫傳六七世
重熙累洽之盛足以邁跡於太甲高宗其故
又何歟夫
punctuated: 問：孔子論居上，必以寬爲本；答問政，亦以寬爲言。是則寬之云者，誠居上爲政之先務也。我太祖高皇帝奉天出治，創制立法，《大誥》三編，深嚴懲惡之典，似與孔子之言異矣。然而御宇建極餘三十年，興道致治之隆，足以匹休於殷湯、周武，其故何歟？伊尹訓太甲有曰：「率乃祖攸行。」傳說告高宗亦曰：「監先王成憲。」是則法祖之云者，誠繼體守文之先務也。我太祖高皇帝創業垂統，佑啓後人，《祖訓》一書，深戒用法之嚴，又似與伊傅之言殊矣。然而聖子神孫傳六七世，重熙累洽之盛，足以邁跡於太甲、高宗，其故又何歟？夫
translation_en:
Question: When Confucius discussed occupying a position above others, he invariably made generosity its foundation; when answering questions about government, he likewise spoke of generosity. Thus generosity is indeed the foremost concern of those who occupy high positions and administer government. Our Emperor Taizu Gao, acting in obedience to Heaven, undertook governance, established institutions, and enacted laws. The three compilations of the Great Pronouncements (Da Gao) set forth exceedingly stern provisions for punishing evil, seemingly at variance with Confucius’s words. Yet during more than thirty years of ruling the realm and establishing the supreme standard, his magnificent achievements in promoting the Way and bringing about good government were sufficient to equal the glory of Tang of Yin and Wu of Zhou. Why was this so?

In instructing Tai Jia, Yi Yin said: “Follow what your ancestor practiced.” Fu Yue likewise told Gaozong: “Take the established statutes of the former kings as your model.” Thus taking one’s ancestors as models is indeed the foremost concern of those who succeed to the throne and preserve inherited institutions. Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty and handed down its succession, protecting and guiding those who came after him. His Ancestral Instructions (Zu Xun) earnestly warned against severity in applying the law, again seemingly differing from the words of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Yet his sagely sons and divine grandsons have succeeded through six or seven generations, and the flourishing of ever-renewed prosperity and cumulative good government has been sufficient to surpass the achievements of Tai Jia and Gaozong. Why, again, was this so? Now, …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之所以行於身而傳於後者皆自我作則
不師古訓而各臻
盛效如此
神謨睿筭蓋必有所主而非苟然也然竊聞之
記曰異世殊時不相沿襲
列聖繼統迄今百二十餘年矣因俗為政其於
寬嚴二者不知尚可以相濟而行之否
歟諸士子欽誦
聖訓于茲有年其尚推
聖祖用心之所極因時損益以著于篇他日躋
===
獻
九重仰塵
乙夜之覽庶幾於
聖明之政萬一有助焉
問濂溪周子祖先天之易作太極之書然
其立象為說之意果皆本於易歟通書
之作又與此圖相為表裏然其發明圖
意之說果可得而聞歟太極圖自一而
punctuated:
聖祖之所以行於身而傳於後者，皆自我作則，不師古訓，而各臻盛效如此。神謨睿筭，蓋必有所主，而非苟然也。然竊聞之，《記》曰：「異世殊時，不相沿襲。」列聖繼統，迄今百二十餘年矣。因俗為政，其於寬嚴二者，不知尚可以相濟而行之否歟？諸士子欽誦聖訓，于茲有年，其尚推聖祖用心之所極，因時損益，以著于篇。他日躋獻九重，仰塵乙夜之覽，庶幾於聖明之政，萬一有助焉。

問：濂溪周子祖先天之《易》，作《太極》之書，然其立象為說之意，果皆本於《易》歟？《通書》之作，又與此圖相為表裏，然其發明圖意之說，果可得而聞歟？太極圖自一而
translation_en:
… What the sagely ancestor put into practice himself and transmitted to posterity established precedents of his own, without taking ancient teachings as his model; yet each measure achieved such splendid results. His divine plans and sagacious calculations surely rested on guiding principles and were no mere happenstance. Yet I have heard that the Record of Rites says: “Different ages and different times do not simply follow one another’s practices.” Successive sage emperors have inherited the imperial succession for more than 120 years now. In governing according to prevailing customs, might leniency and severity still be employed so as to complement one another? You examination candidates have reverently recited the imperial teachings for years. You should explore the ultimate intentions of the sagely ancestor and set forth in your essays how measures may be modified to suit the times. Should these essays one day be presented within the innermost palace and receive the honor of imperial perusal during the second watch of the night, perhaps they may offer some small assistance to His Sagacious Majesty’s government.

Question: Master Zhou of Lianxi took the Changes of Prior Heaven as his foundation and composed his work on the Supreme Ultimate. But were his intentions in establishing images and providing explanations indeed all grounded in the Changes? His Comprehensive Writings (Tongshu), moreover, and this diagram illuminate one another. Can you explain how that work elucidates the meaning of the diagram? The Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate proceeds from one to …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
二自二而五即推至於萬物易則自一
而二自二而四自四而八自八而十六
自十六而三十二自三十二而六十四
然後萬物之理備何歟通書一篇本名
易通則六十四卦宜皆有其說今考其
書獨有乾損益家人睽復无妄蒙艮等
說何歟先天太極二圖同一發明造化
之妙也然格局則太極不如先天之大
而詳義理則先天不如太極之精而約
===
何歟太極西銘二書同一開示學者之
言也然程子於西銘則屢言以示門人
而太極未嘗一言及之何歟劉子所謂
天地之中即濂溪所言太極乎橫渠太
虛之說即濂溪無極之意乎諸士子樂
菁莪之敎育究道學之淵源而於先天
太極通書西銘必深有所得焉願詳言
之以觀性理之學
問孔子萬代之師凡一言一行傳諸後世
punctuated:
二，自二而五，即推至於萬物。《易》則自一而二，自二而四，自四而八，自八而十六，自十六而三十二，自三十二而六十四，然後萬物之理備，何歟？《通書》一篇，本名《易通》，則六十四卦宜皆有其說。今考其書，獨有乾、損、益、家人、睽、復、无妄、蒙、艮等說，何歟？先天、太極二圖，同一發明造化之妙也。然格局則太極不如先天之大而詳，義理則先天不如太極之精而約，何歟？太極、西銘二書，同一開示學者之言也。然程子於《西銘》則屢言以示門人，而太極未嘗一言及之，何歟？劉子所謂天地之中，即濂溪所言太極乎？橫渠太虛之說，即濂溪無極之意乎？諸士子樂菁莪之敎育，究道學之淵源，而於先天、太極、通書、西銘必深有所得焉。願詳言之，以觀性理之學。

問：孔子萬代之師，凡一言一行傳諸後世，
translation_en:
…to two, and from two to five, then extends directly to the myriad things. The Changes, however, proceeds from one to two, from two to four, from four to eight, from eight to sixteen, from sixteen to thirty-two, and from thirty-two to sixty-four; only then are the principles of the myriad things fully encompassed. Why is this? The work Penetrating the Book (Tongshu) was originally entitled Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), so it ought to contain explanations of all sixty-four hexagrams. Yet when we examine it, we find discussions only of such hexagrams as Qian, Sun, Yi, Jiaren, Kui, Fu, Wuwang, Meng, and Gen. Why is this? The Diagram of the Prior Heaven and the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate both elucidate the subtleties of cosmic transformation. Yet in arrangement, the Supreme Ultimate diagram is less extensive and detailed than the Prior Heaven diagram, while in principles and meaning, the Prior Heaven diagram is less refined and concise than the Supreme Ultimate diagram. Why is this? The Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription are both writings that offer instruction to students. Yet Master Cheng repeatedly discussed the Western Inscription to instruct his disciples, while he never said a word about the Supreme Ultimate. Why is this? Is what Master Liu called the centrality of Heaven and Earth precisely what Lianxi called the Supreme Ultimate? Is Hengqu’s explanation of the Great Vacuity precisely what Lianxi meant by the Limitless? You candidates have enjoyed the nurturing education celebrated in the “Luxuriant Southernwood” ode and investigated the origins of the Learning of the Way. You must therefore have gained a profound understanding of the Prior Heaven diagram, the Supreme Ultimate diagram, Penetrating the Book, and the Western Inscription. Please discuss these in detail, so that we may assess your learning concerning human nature and principle.

Question: Confucius is the teacher of ten thousand generations. Every word and deed of his transmitted to later ages…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者皆吾儒所當誦習而取法焉者也今
考諸經傳所載夫子言行之詳其間或
不能無彼此小異者試舉一二與諸士
子商確之可乎里仁為美當知所處也
何以欲居九夷亂邦不居當知所避也
何以欲往公山既曰吾從先進何以又
欲從周既曰有教無類何以有下愚不
移文行忠信文若先於行矣然以餘力
學文為弟子職行又何先於文民無信
===
不立人固貴於信矣然以言必信為小
人信又何不貴耶魯之火則知其為桓
僖廟之焚則不知其人馬豈料遠反易
於料近耶稽首再拜不惜於招搖之行
時亡往拜反惜於歸豚之人豈大夫反
下於小君耶箕子比干微子異行何同
謂之仁太伯文王殊事何同謂之至德
殷夏之禮則知其損益之所宜杞宋之
禮則嘆其文獻之不足豈明於大而不
punctuated: 者，皆吾儒所當誦習而取法焉者也。今考諸經傳所載夫子言行之詳，其間或不能無彼此小異者，試舉一二，與諸士子商確之，可乎？里仁為美，當知所處也，何以欲居九夷？亂邦不居，當知所避也，何以欲往公山？既曰「吾從先進」，何以又欲從周？既曰「有教無類」，何以有「下愚不移」？文行忠信，文若先於行矣，然以餘力學文為弟子職，行又何先於文？民無信不立，人固貴於信矣，然以言必信為小人，信又何不貴耶？魯之火，則知其為桓僖；廟之焚，則不知其人馬，豈料遠反易於料近耶？稽首再拜，不惜於招搖之行；時亡往拜，反惜於歸豚之人，豈大夫反下於小君耶？箕子、比干、微子異行，何同謂之仁？太伯、文王殊事，何同謂之至德？殷夏之禮，則知其損益之所宜；杞宋之禮，則嘆其文獻之不足，豈明於大而不
translation_en:
…are all things that we Confucian scholars should recite, study, and take as models. Now, when we examine the detailed accounts of the Master's words and deeds recorded in the classics and their commentaries, there seem to be some minor discrepancies among them. May we raise one or two for discussion with you candidates?

He said, “To dwell among the humane is best,” and thus must have known where one should live. Why, then, did he wish to live among the Nine Yi peoples? He said that one should not dwell in a disorderly state, and thus must have known what to avoid. Why, then, did he wish to go to Gongshan? Having said, “I follow those of earlier times,” why did he also wish to follow the Zhou? Having said, “In teaching there are no distinctions of kind,” why did he also say that “the lowest fools do not change”? In “cultural learning, conduct, loyalty, and trustworthiness,” learning seems to precede conduct. Yet he made studying cultural learning with one's remaining strength a duty of the young. Why, in this case, does conduct precede learning? “Without trust, the people cannot stand”: trustworthiness is surely something people should value. Yet he deemed someone whose words are invariably trustworthy a petty man. Why, in this case, is trustworthiness not valued?

When there was a fire in Lu, he knew that it involved the temples of Huan and Xi; yet when the temple burned, he did not know about its people and horses [?]. Could judging what is distant actually be easier than judging what is near? He did not withhold two bows with his forehead to the ground on the occasion of an ostentatious outing; yet, by choosing a time when the recipient was away to pay his respects, he withheld an audience from the man who had sent him a pig. Could a grand master actually rank below a ruler's consort?

Jizi, Bigan, and Weizi acted differently: why did he call them all humane? Taibo and King Wen undertook different affairs: why did he describe both as possessing the highest virtue? Concerning the rites of the Yin and Xia, he knew what should properly be omitted or added; concerning the rites of Qi and Song, he lamented the insufficiency of records and learned men. Could he have understood great matters but failed to…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
明於小歟儻知仲由之不得其死不知
顏淵之不幸短命豈知於此而不知於
彼歟昭公管仲其慾禮一也何一以知禮
答一以不知禮斥南容樊遲其言稼一
也何一褒為君子一貶為小人兩端之
教尚竭於空空之鄙夫何獨靳於三隅
之不反三日不朝尚稽於遲遲之魯國
何獨急於明日之遂行孔圉公叔事不
同也胡皆許其可以為文子貢子夏論
===
各異也胡同許其可以言詩夫孔子之
道辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬辟
如四時之錯行日月之代明按其跡似
有可疑原其心豈無所謂願為我一一
言之以示學聖人者
問書之為藝所以宣人文敷治化經綸乎
天地自古聖賢皆重焉者也摉其所自
肇於庖羲之卦畫成於蒼頡之鳥跡六
書之義備矣然其更變不一有龍書有
punctuated:
明於小歟？儻知仲由之不得其死，不知顏淵之不幸短命，豈知於此而不知於彼歟？昭公、管仲，其慾禮一也，何一以知禮答，一以不知禮斥？南容、樊遲，其言稼一也，何一褒為君子，一貶為小人？兩端之教，尚竭於空空之鄙夫，何獨靳於三隅之不反？三日不朝，尚稽於遲遲之魯國，何獨急於明日之遂行？孔圉、公叔，事不同也，胡皆許其可以為文？子貢、子夏，論各異也，胡同許其可以言詩？夫孔子之道，辟如天地之無不持載、無不覆幬，辟如四時之錯行、日月之代明。按其跡，似有可疑；原其心，豈無所謂？願為我一一言之，以示學聖人者。
問：書之為藝，所以宣人文、敷治化、經綸乎天地，自古聖賢皆重焉者也。摉其所自，肇於庖羲之卦畫，成於蒼頡之鳥跡，六書之義備矣。然其更變不一，有龍書，有
translation_en:
…yet not understand the small? If he knew that Zhong You would not meet a natural death, but did not know that Yan Yuan would unfortunately die young, did he know the one but not the other? Duke Zhao and Guan Zhong were alike in their desire for ritual propriety [?]; why did he answer that one understood ritual, yet rebuke the other for not understanding it? Nan Rong and Fan Chi were alike in speaking of farming [?]; why did he praise one as a gentleman and disparage the other as a petty man? He would exhaust both ends of a question in teaching even an ignorant fellow whose mind was empty; why, then, withhold instruction specifically from someone unable to infer the other three corners? When the ruler failed to hold court for three days, he still lingered in the state of Lu, slow to depart; why, in another instance, was he so quick to leave the very next day? Kong Yu and Gongshu differed in their deeds; why did he acknowledge that both could receive the posthumous title Wen, “Cultured”? Zigong and Zixia differed in their discussions; why did he acknowledge that both could discuss the Book of Odes? The Way of Confucius is like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and cover all things; it is like the four seasons proceeding in turn, and the sun and moon shining in succession. Examining his actions, one may find apparent grounds for doubt; tracing his intentions, could there be no underlying meaning? Please explain these matters to me one by one, to instruct those who seek to learn from the sage.
Question: Writing as an art serves to manifest human culture, extend the transforming influence of good government, and bring order to Heaven and Earth. Sages and worthies have valued it since antiquity. Tracing its origins, it began with the hexagram lines of Pao Xi and reached completion in Cang Jie’s bird-track writing, with the principles of the six categories of writing fully established. Yet its subsequent transformations have been manifold: there is dragon script, and there is…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
穗書有垂雲書者孰創之有〔鸞鳥□有〕〔□□□〕
書有鍾鼎書者孰爲之曰篆曰隸體頗
殊也何人所製曰楷曰草體大異也何
人所吏烟霏霧結鳳翥龍翔筆固妙矣
較之雄秀獨出者孰爲工拙五絶居一
筆態迺羆書固善矣視之心正筆正者
孰爲失得古人於書有云得法於白雲
子者有云得神人所授八角垂芒之書
者誣歟信歟古人執筆有見羣鵝運頸
而悟者有觀夏雲迴風之變而悟者然
歟否歟夫書之資於人切矣學書者當
以執筆爲先用筆次之執筆之法曰虛
拳實腕指齊掌空其說傳之遠矣近代
又演爲擫捺鉤抉抵拒導送八字口訣
可悉繹其義歟用筆之精有藏鋒出鋒
正鋒側鋒左鋒者矣然又有衄筆引筆
縱筆複筆舞筆之屬可歷陳其說歟諸
士子游心文苑染翰操觚日有賴於書
punctuated: 穗書、有垂雲書者，孰創之？有〔鸞鳥□有〕〔□□□〕書、有鍾鼎書者，孰爲之？曰篆曰隸，體頗殊也，何人所製？曰楷曰草，體大異也，何人所吏？烟霏霧結，鳳翥龍翔，筆固妙矣；較之雄秀獨出者，孰爲工拙？五絶居一，筆態迺羆，書固善矣；視之心正筆正者，孰爲失得？古人於書，有云得法於白雲子者，有云得神人所授八角垂芒之書者，誣歟信歟？古人執筆，有見羣鵝運頸而悟者，有觀夏雲迴風之變而悟者，然歟否歟？夫書之資於人切矣！學書者當以執筆爲先，用筆次之。執筆之法，曰虛拳實腕，指齊掌空，其說傳之遠矣。近代又演爲擫捺鉤抉抵拒導送八字口訣，可悉繹其義歟？用筆之精，有藏鋒、出鋒、正鋒、側鋒、左鋒者矣，然又有衄筆、引筆、縱筆、複筆、舞筆之屬，可歷陳其說歟？諸士子游心文苑，染翰操觚，日有賴於書
translation_en:
…grain-ear script and hanging-cloud script: who invented them? There are 〔luan-bird … there are [?]〕〔three illegible characters〕 script and bell-and-cauldron script: who made them? Seal script and clerical script differ considerably in form: who devised them? Regular script and cursive script differ greatly in form: who [devised them? — text corrupt]? Like drifting haze and gathering mist, like phoenixes soaring and dragons flying—the brushwork is certainly marvelous. Compared with work outstanding for its vigor and elegance, which is skillful and which inferior? With calligraphy ranking as one of the five supreme accomplishments, and with brushwork described as “nai pi” [?], the writing is certainly fine. Yet compared with the principle that when the heart is upright the brush is upright, which succeeds and which fails?

Among the ancients, some are said to have learned the methods of calligraphy from Baiyunzi; others are said to have received from a divine being a script with eight corners and pendent rays. Are these stories false or trustworthy? Among ancient wielders of the brush, some attained insight by watching a flock of geese turn their necks, and others by observing the transformations of summer clouds and swirling winds. Is this true or not?

Calligraphy is indeed of immediate use to people. Those who study it should first learn to hold the brush, and then to wield it. The method of holding it is described as keeping the fist loose and the wrist firm, the fingers aligned and the palm hollow. This teaching has long been transmitted. In more recent times it has been further developed into an eight-character oral formula: ye, na, gou, jue, di, ju, dao, and song—pressing, bearing down, hooking, drawing out, supporting, resisting, guiding, and sending forth. Can you fully explain their meanings? Refined brush technique includes concealing the tip, exposing the tip, using the tip upright, using it obliquely, and using it to the left. There are also such techniques as reversing, drawing, releasing, repeating, and dancing the brush. Can you set out their explanations one by one? You candidates, whose minds roam the garden of letters, who dip your brushes and take up your writing tablets, daily depend upon calligraphy…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
者也必習察之願詳著于篇毋隱
問國家所以為長治久安之計者不外乎
文武兩途而已文在養士武在詰兵古
今不能易也試以養士言之成周棫樸
之化豐芑之澤無以尚矣若漢之置弟
子員行養老禮唐之增廣生員徧置學
校宋之太學宗學武學之類其法孰為
最優以詰兵言之成周居則為農行則
為兵無以加矣若漢之南北軍唐之府
===
兵彍騎方鎮宋之班直屯駐廂兵民兵
之類其法孰為最善我
朝學校之設周遍海宇厥初士有定額教有
常規其法良矣涵濡既久秀民日多至
于今名州大邑增至數倍司政教者遂
不能約之於規矩之中居常或挑達城
闕而不事學業取應或夤緣攀貴而不
安義命
朝廷因是特
punctuated:
者也，必習察之，願詳著于篇，毋隱。

問：國家所以為長治久安之計者，不外乎文武兩途而已。文在養士，武在詰兵，古今不能易也。試以養士言之，成周棫樸之化、豐芑之澤，無以尚矣。若漢之置弟子員、行養老禮，唐之增廣生員、徧置學校，宋之太學、宗學、武學之類，其法孰為最優？以詰兵言之，成周居則為農，行則為兵，無以加矣。若漢之南北軍，唐之府兵、彍騎、方鎮，宋之班直、屯駐、廂兵、民兵之類，其法孰為最善？我朝學校之設，周遍海宇。厥初士有定額，教有常規，其法良矣。涵濡既久，秀民日多，至于今名州大邑，增至數倍。司政教者遂不能約之於規矩之中。居常或挑達城闕，而不事學業；取應或夤緣攀貴，而不安義命。朝廷因是特
translation_en:
…who depend upon calligraphy must surely have studied and examined it closely. Please set out your knowledge fully in your essay, withholding nothing.

Question: The state's plans for enduring order and lasting peace extend no further than the two paths of civil and military affairs. Civil affairs depend on nurturing scholars; military affairs depend on putting the troops in order. This has remained unchanged from antiquity to the present. Consider first the nurturing of scholars. Nothing could surpass the transforming influence celebrated in the Zhou poem “Luxuriant Oaks” (Yupu) or the beneficence figured by its flourishing millet (feng qi). As for the Han establishment of student places and performance of ceremonies honoring the aged, the Tang expansion of student numbers and establishment of schools everywhere, and the Song institutions such as the Imperial University, schools for the imperial clan, and military schools—which system was best? As for putting troops in order, nothing could improve upon the Zhou arrangement whereby men were farmers at home and soldiers on campaign. Among such institutions as the Han Southern and Northern Armies; the Tang militia system (fubing), Expanded Cavalry (guangqi), and regional military commands; and the Song palace guard units, stationed troops, prefectural troops, and local militias—which system was best?

Our dynasty has established schools throughout the realm. At the outset, student numbers had fixed quotas and instruction followed standing regulations: the system was sound. After long cultivation, talented men among the people grew daily more numerous, so that today, in prominent prefectures and large counties, their numbers have increased severalfold. Those responsible for administration and instruction have consequently become unable to keep them within the prescribed rules. In ordinary times, some saunter about the city gates and towers instead of attending to their studies; when seeking admission to the examinations, some cultivate connections and attach themselves to powerful men instead of resting content with what righteousness and their allotted lot permit. For this reason, the imperial court has specially …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
敕憲臣以提督之尚不能悉祛其弊也請言
其所以救之之術安在我
朝衛所之設布滿寰區厥初軍無缺伍練不
失時其制善矣承平既久弊端百出至
于今名數雖存在伍無幾司兵柄者恒
無以趨辦於緩急之際無事則僅備差
遣有事則借募民兵
朝廷因是特
敕御史以清理之終不能悉復其舊也請言
===
其所以極之之法何居夫政事之弊所
當究心者多矣而斯二者其所關係尤
重也諸士子學古將以入官願酌其可
行於今日者以對
punctuated: 敕憲臣以提督之，尚不能悉祛其弊也。請言其所以救之之術安在？我朝衛所之設，布滿寰區。厥初軍無缺伍，練不失時，其制善矣。承平既久，弊端百出。至于今，名數雖存，在伍無幾。司兵柄者恒無以趨辦於緩急之際，無事則僅備差遣，有事則借募民兵。朝廷因是特敕御史以清理之，終不能悉復其舊也。請言其所以極之之法何居？夫政事之弊，所當究心者多矣，而斯二者，其所關係尤重也。諸士子學古，將以入官，願酌其可行於今日者以對。
translation_en:
…ordered censorial officials to supervise them, yet they have still been unable to eliminate all these abuses. Explain what methods might remedy them.

Our dynasty’s guards and battalions extend throughout the realm. At their establishment, the military ranks had no vacancies, and training took place at the prescribed times: the system was sound. After a long period of peace, however, abuses have proliferated. Today, although names and numerical strengths remain on the registers, few men are actually in the ranks. Those holding military command are consequently often unable to meet demands as circumstances require. In quiet times, the troops barely suffice for routine assignments; when trouble arises, commanders resort to recruiting civilian militia. For this reason, the court specially ordered investigating censors to scrutinize and rectify the situation, yet they have ultimately been unable to restore the former arrangements in full. Explain what methods could bring this matter to a complete resolution [?].

There are many abuses in government that deserve careful attention, but these two matters have particularly weighty implications. You candidates study antiquity in preparation for entering office. In your answers, weigh what could practicably be carried out today.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人九十五名
第一名羅欽順　泰和縣儒士　書
第二名汪偉　弋陽縣學增廣生　易
第三名陳嬰　撫州府學生　詩
第四名范希淹　弋陽縣學增廣生　禮記
第五名阮芳　安福縣學增廣生　春秋
第六名楊廷用　撫州府學增廣生　詩
第七名徐威　泰和縣學生　書
===
第八名熊吉　臨川縣學生　易
第九名王潮　南昌縣學生　春秋
第十名楊二和　進賢縣學增廣生　詩
第十一名鄒璀　樂安縣儒士　書
第十二名黄黼　宜春縣學生　易
第十三名黄洪　貴溪縣學增廣生　禮記

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導孫　批〔典雅〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔表有忠愛實心〕
臣某等伏覩弘治五年某月某日
冊立
皇太子
詔諭天下謹奉
表稱
賀者臣某誠歡誠忭稽首頓首
上言伏以
===
聖主御天普
仁恩於四海
儲皇正位定
國本於萬年夷夏交歡
神人胥慶茲盖伏遇
○○○
聰明
天錫
聖敬日躋嗣
punctuated:
考試官訓導孫，批〔典雅〕。
考試官教諭柯，批〔表有忠愛實心〕。
臣某等伏覩弘治五年某月某日冊立皇太子，詔諭天下，謹奉表稱賀者。臣某誠歡誠忭，稽首頓首，上言：伏以聖主御天，普仁恩於四海；儲皇正位，定國本於萬年。夷夏交歡，神人胥慶。茲盖伏遇○○○，聰明天錫，聖敬日躋，嗣
translation_en:
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Refined and elegant.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔The memorial expresses a sincere heart of loyalty and devotion.〕
We, your servants So-and-so and others, humbly observe that on a certain day of a certain month in the fifth year of Hongzhi, the Imperial Heir Apparent was formally invested and an edict proclaimed this throughout the realm. We respectfully submit this memorial to offer congratulations. Your servant So-and-so, truly joyful and truly delighted, bows his head to the ground and repeatedly kowtows, submitting these words:
We humbly reflect that the sage sovereign rules under Heaven, extending benevolent favor throughout the Four Seas; the Imperial Heir Apparent assumes his proper position, securing the foundation of the state for ten thousand years. The peoples beyond and within the Chinese realm rejoice together; spirits and men alike celebrate. This is because we have the good fortune to serve ○○○ [?], whose intelligence is bestowed by Heaven and whose sagely reverence increases daily, succeeding to…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗列聖之丕圖荷
天地百神之眷佑奉明禋於
九廟穆若高宗遏至養於
兩宮孝同虞舜正家以化天下綽有關雎之風
垂統以裕
後昆遂致麟趾之應黃河清而
聖人出式協昌期鸑鳳下而
渙詔頒肇建
儲位前星拱極而耀三垣
===
離照繼明而光八表信
天生之不偶知
神器之有歸文丕顯而武丕承華夏蠻貊之
率俾禹克勤而啓克敬謳歌獄訟之皆歸
此誠
宗社無疆之休臣民莫大之慶也〔臣欣逢〕
盛典叨列清班馳遥
賀於
九重效嵩呼之三祝伏願
punctuated: 祖宗列聖之丕圖，荷天地百神之眷佑，奉明禋於九廟，穆若高宗；遏至養於兩宮，孝同虞舜。正家以化天下，綽有關雎之風；垂統以裕後昆，遂致麟趾之應。黃河清而聖人出，式協昌期；鸑鳳下而渙詔頒，肇建儲位。前星拱極而耀三垣，離照繼明而光八表。信天生之不偶，知神器之有歸。文丕顯而武丕承，華夏蠻貊之率俾；禹克勤而啓克敬，謳歌獄訟之皆歸。此誠宗社無疆之休、臣民莫大之慶也。〔臣欣逢〕盛典，叨列清班，馳遥賀於九重，效嵩呼之三祝。伏願
translation_en:
…the grand enterprise of the ancestors and successive sage emperors, receiving the gracious protection of Heaven, Earth, and the hundred spirits. You offer pure sacrifices at the nine ancestral temples, reverent as Gaozong; in tending the two palaces with utmost devotion [?], your filial piety equals that of Shun of Yu. You set your household in order to transform all under Heaven, abundantly displaying the spirit of “The Ospreys”; you transmit the succession to enrich your descendants, thereby bringing forth the auspicious fulfillment of “The Qilin’s Hoofs.” The Yellow River runs clear and a sage appears, fitting this age of flourishing fortune; the phoenix descends and an imperial edict goes forth, establishing the position of heir apparent. The Foremost Star attends the celestial pole and shines upon the Three Enclosures; the radiance of Li continues the light and illuminates the eight outermost regions.

Truly, Heaven’s bringing forth such a person is no coincidence; we know that the sacred vessel of sovereignty has its rightful successor. As King Wen was greatly illustrious and King Wu greatly carried on his work, so the peoples of Huaxia and the Man and Mo all submit. As Yu was diligent and Qi reverent, so those singing praises and those seeking judgment in lawsuits all turn toward the successor. This is indeed a boundless blessing for the dynastic ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain, and the greatest joy for your subjects. [Your servant, joyfully encountering] this grand occasion and unworthily holding a place among the distinguished officials, hastens to convey congratulations from afar to the ninefold palace, emulating the acclamations at Mount Song with three blessings. I humbly pray that…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
重華協
帝揭
日月而同明
聖壽齊天保山河而永固臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
===
第叄場
策
第一問
阮芳
同考試官學正毛　批我
聖祖立法垂訓之善暨
列聖因時致治之隆孰能鋪張揚厲如此策者乎是用錄出
考試官訓導孫　批〔荅契問意〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔有考據有斷制〕
punctuated:
重華協帝，揭日月而同明；聖壽齊天，保山河而永固。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第叄場
策
第一問
阮芳

同考試官學正毛　批：我聖祖立法垂訓之善，暨列聖因時致治之隆，孰能鋪張揚厲如此策者乎？是用錄出。

考試官訓導孫　批：〔荅契問意〕

考試官教諭柯　批：〔有考據，有斷制〕
translation_en:
…may renewed splendor accord with the Emperor, shining aloft with the sun and moon; may Your Majesty’s longevity equal Heaven’s, keeping the realm forever secure. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Ruan Fang

Comment by Associate Examiner Mao, School Instructor: Who could expound and extol the excellence of our Sagely Founder’s establishment of laws and transmission of instructions, and the flourishing government achieved by successive sage emperors in accordance with the needs of their times, as this policy essay does? For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: 〔The answer accords with the intent of the question.〕

Comment by Examiner Ke, Instructor: 〔It offers both substantiation from sources and decisive judgments.〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
大對寬猛因時而不泥乎古此
聖祖拯世救時之卓見寬猛相濟而必酌其宜
此
聖世長治久安之良圖蓋易亂為治固不得不
施之以猛而貽謀燕翼又不得不示之以
寬寬猛因時神矣哉
聖祖卓越之見也政猛則必節之以寬政寬則
必振之以猛寬猛相濟允矣哉
聖世致治之法也請因執事之問而陳其槩昔
===
孔子論居上為政而必有取於寬者所以
示人為政之常道也伊尹傅說之告其君
而皆欲其法祖者亦示之以法其常道而
已洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺
天眷命為生民主丁元政縱弛之餘遭華風淪
沒之際教化陵夷人紀廢墜思欲示國法
於臣民乃作
大誥三編鋤凶芟惡之典凜乎秋霜之肅殺
punctuated:
大對：寬猛因時而不泥乎古，此聖祖拯世救時之卓見；寬猛相濟而必酌其宜，此聖世長治久安之良圖。蓋易亂為治，固不得不施之以猛；而貽謀燕翼，又不得不示之以寬。寬猛因時，神矣哉，聖祖卓越之見也！政猛則必節之以寬，政寬則必振之以猛。寬猛相濟，允矣哉，聖世致治之法也！請因執事之問而陳其槩。
昔孔子論居上為政，而必有取於寬者，所以示人為政之常道也。伊尹、傅說之告其君，而皆欲其法祖者，亦示之以法其常道而已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天眷命，為生民主，丁元政縱弛之餘，遭華風淪沒之際，教化陵夷，人紀廢墜。思欲示國法於臣民，乃作《大誥》三編，鋤凶芟惡之典，凜乎秋霜之肅殺
translation_en:
In reply: Adapting leniency and severity to the times without rigidly adhering to antiquity—this was the sagacious founding emperor’s outstanding insight into delivering the world and remedying the troubles of his age. Making leniency and severity complement one another, while always weighing what is appropriate—this is the excellent plan for enduring order and lasting peace in our sagely age. To turn disorder into order, severity was indeed indispensable; yet to leave plans that would secure the welfare of his descendants, he also had to show leniency. How inspired was the sagacious founding emperor’s exceptional insight in adapting leniency and severity to the times! When government is severe, it must be moderated with leniency; when government is lenient, it must be invigorated with severity. How sound is the method of achieving order in our sagely age by making leniency and severity complement one another! Allow me to set forth its broad outlines in response to your question.
In former times, when Kongzi discussed governing from a position of authority, he invariably commended leniency, thereby showing people the constant way of government. When Yi Yin and Fu Yue advised their rulers, both wished them to emulate their ancestors; they too were simply showing them how to follow that constant way. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s favor and mandate and became lord of the people. He came in the aftermath of lax and undisciplined Yuan government, at a time when Chinese cultural traditions had fallen into oblivion, moral instruction was declining, and the norms of human relationships had been abandoned. Wishing to make the laws of the realm manifest to his officials and people, he composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao). Their provisions for rooting out the violent and cutting down the wicked were as fearsome as the killing force of autumn frost…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也戢姦剔蠹之法肅乎雷霆之威斷也若
是者似異於孔子之言矣然而
御宇建極餘三十年教化已晦而復明人紀
已墜而復立
盛德大業視殷湯周武而無愧者蓋以其用
法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳及其
駿命已凝大統已定思欲示家法於子孫乃
作
祖訓一書論用法特以前日之嚴為戒論致
===
治惟於先王之道是程若是者又似異於
伊傅之言矣然而
聖子神孫傳六七世九有奠安而至治益隆四
夷賓服而
鴻業益固
重熙累洽視太甲高宗而有光者以其垂訓
有合於孔子論為政之道故耳夫猛於立
國之初者一時之用也寬於繼統之後者
萬世之常也寬猛各因其時而效驗彰
punctuated: 也。戢姦剔蠹之法，肅乎雷霆之威斷也。若是者，似異於孔子之言矣。然而御宇建極餘三十年，教化已晦而復明，人紀已墜而復立，盛德大業視殷湯周武而無愧者，蓋以其用法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳。及其駿命已凝，大統已定，思欲示家法於子孫，乃作《祖訓》一書。論用法，特以前日之嚴為戒；論致治，惟於先王之道是程。若是者，又似異於伊傅之言矣。然而聖子神孫傳六七世，九有奠安而至治益隆，四夷賓服而鴻業益固，重熙累洽，視太甲高宗而有光者，以其垂訓有合於孔子論為政之道故耳。夫猛於立國之初者，一時之用也；寬於繼統之後者，萬世之常也。寬猛各因其時，而效驗彰
translation_en:
… His laws for restraining evildoers and rooting out pernicious elements were as awe-inspiring as the thunderbolt’s decisive might. Such measures seem to differ from Confucius’s words. Yet, during more than thirty years of ruling the realm and establishing the supreme standard, moral instruction, once obscured, shone forth again, and the bonds of human relations, once fallen into ruin, were reestablished. His splendid virtue and great achievements bore comparison without shame with those of Tang of Shang and Wu of Zhou. This was simply because his application of the law accorded with the prescriptions in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) for punishing a disordered state.

Once his great mandate was firmly secured and the imperial succession settled, he wished to set forth his family’s rules for his descendants, and so composed the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun). In discussing the application of law, he expressly warned against the severity of earlier days; in discussing how to achieve good government, he took only the Way of the former kings as his standard. Such teachings again seem to differ from the words of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Yet his sagely sons and divinely wise grandsons have transmitted the throne through six or seven generations: the nine regions are secure, and excellent government flourishes ever more; the peoples of the four quarters submit, and the great imperial enterprise grows ever firmer. Successive reigns have brought accumulating prosperity and harmony, shining in comparison with those of Tai Jia and Gaozong. This is simply because the instructions he bequeathed accord with Confucius’s account of the Way of government.

Severity at the founding of a state is a measure for a particular time; leniency after succession to the throne is the enduring norm for myriad generations. Leniency and severity each suit their respective times, and their efficacy becomes manifest …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
其撫非
聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古曷能然哉雖然嘗
聞之孔子有曰政寬則民慢慢則糾之以
猛猛則民殘殘則施之以寬寬以濟猛猛
以濟寬政是以和
列聖相承迄今百二十餘年矣記不云乎異世
殊時不相沿襲愚竊以為因俗為政尚當
以孔子之言為法因時制宜隨事取中猛
以警之使頹靡之綱無不振寬以行之使
===
仁厚之意無不存則唐虞三代之治無以
易此而其所以垂裕於
後昆者將億萬斯世而無窮矣謹因明問所
及而述其管見如此他日倘得徹聽
九重亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也
第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林　批〔究道學之淵源探先儒之閫〕
奧無如此篇
punctuated:
其撫，非聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古，曷能然哉？雖然，嘗聞之，孔子有曰：「政寬則民慢，慢則糾之以猛；猛則民殘，殘則施之以寬。寬以濟猛，猛以濟寬，政是以和。」列聖相承，迄今百二十餘年矣。《記》不云乎：「異世殊時，不相沿襲。」愚竊以為，因俗為政，尚當以孔子之言為法，因時制宜，隨事取中。猛以警之，使頹靡之綱無不振；寬以行之，使仁厚之意無不存。則唐虞三代之治無以易此，而其所以垂裕於後昆者，將億萬斯世而無窮矣。謹因明問所及，而述其管見如此。他日倘得徹聽九重，亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也。
第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林　批〔究道學之淵源，探先儒之閫〕奧，無如此篇。
translation_en:
…its pacification [?]. Had the sagely founder’s profound intentions and discerning wisdom not surpassed those of all preceding ages, how could this have been achieved? Nevertheless, I have heard these words of Confucius: “When government is lenient, the people become lax; when they become lax, correct them with severity. When government is severe, the people suffer; when they suffer, apply leniency. Temper severity with leniency and leniency with severity: through this, government achieves harmony.”
Successive sage sovereigns have inherited the throne for more than 120 years now. Does not the Record of Rites say, “Different ages and different times do not simply follow one another’s practices”? In my humble opinion, governing in accordance with local customs still requires taking Confucius’s words as the standard, adapting measures to the times, and finding the proper balance in each affair. Use severity to admonish, so that every weakened principle of order is restored; exercise leniency, so that the spirit of benevolence and generosity is everywhere preserved. Then even the government of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties could offer no improvement upon this, and the blessings thereby bequeathed to future descendants would endure for countless generations without end. In respectful response to the matters raised by your illuminating question, I have thus set forth my limited views. Should they someday reach the imperial hearing within the ninefold palace gates, perhaps they might offer some small assistance, like the humble gifts of cress and the sun’s warmth.
Second Policy Question
Chen Ying
Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor, comments: “For investigating the origins of the Learning of the Way and probing the innermost profundities of earlier Confucian scholars, no essay equals this one.”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭王 批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人盖慮其未有能受之者此策於先天太極通書西銘諸書同異條答無遺其亦深有所得而可受之者耶〕
考試官訓導孫 批〔精粹〕
考試官教諭柯 批〔策能答所問足見學識〕
對濂溪未作而千聖相傳之道學晦而不
明濂溪既作而千聖相傳之道統斷而復
續夫道之大原出於天而具於人心盖混
然一太極也濂溪周子手爲圖筆爲書使斯
===
道已晦而復明已斷而復續是其生乎千
載之下而有以接道統於千載之上奮乎
百世之上而有以啓道學於百世之下也
先生之學其粹矣哉愚顧何人而能發其
精蘊乎巖陳大義以復明問之萬一且夫
伏羲先天之易備天地鬼神之奧萬事萬
物之理誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也堯舜湯武
之相禪繼以治天下者以是孔曾思孟之
相傳授以淑天下者以是孟子既歿聖學
punctuated:
同考試官教諭王批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人，盖慮其未有能受之者。此策於先天、太極、通書、西銘諸書同異，條答無遺，其亦深有所得而可受之者耶？〕
考試官訓導孫批〔精粹。〕
考試官教諭柯批〔策能答所問，足見學識。〕
對：濂溪未作，而千聖相傳之道學晦而不明；濂溪既作，而千聖相傳之道統斷而復續。夫道之大原出於天，而具於人心，盖混然一太極也。濂溪周子手爲圖，筆爲書，使斯道已晦而復明，已斷而復續。是其生乎千載之下，而有以接道統於千載之上；奮乎百世之上，而有以啓道學於百世之下也。先生之學，其粹矣哉！愚顧何人，而能發其精蘊乎？巖陳大義，以復明問之萬一。且夫伏羲先天之易，備天地鬼神之奧、萬事萬物之理，誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也。堯舜湯武之相禪繼以治天下者，以是；孔曾思孟之相傳授以淑天下者，以是。孟子既歿，聖學
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Cheng never showed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate to others, presumably fearing that none could receive its teaching. This policy essay answers point by point, without omission, concerning the similarities and differences among the works on the Prior-to-Heaven Changes and the Supreme Ultimate, the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), and the Western Inscription (Ximing). Might its author likewise have attained a deep understanding and be capable of receiving that teaching?〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Refined and pure.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay answers what was asked, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.〕
Response: Before Lianxi arose, the learning of the Way transmitted by the sages through the ages had grown obscure and was no longer clear. Once Lianxi arose, the succession of the Way transmitted by those sages, though broken, was renewed. The great source of the Way issues from Heaven and is fully present in the human heart; it is, indeed, one undifferentiated Supreme Ultimate. Master Zhou of Lianxi drew a diagram with his own hand and composed a book with his brush, making this Way clear again after it had become obscure and renewing its succession after it had been broken. Thus, born a thousand years later, he could reconnect with the succession of the Way a thousand years before; rising to prominence a hundred generations earlier, he could open the learning of the Way to the hundred generations that followed. How pure was the Master’s learning! Who am I, in my ignorance, to expound its essential depths? I shall set forth its principal meaning [?], to answer even a fraction of your discerning question.
Now Fuxi’s Prior-to-Heaven Changes encompasses the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, and the principles of all affairs and all things. It is truly the founding source of this cultural tradition for all ages. It was through this that Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, yielding the throne or succeeding one another, governed all under Heaven; it was through this that Confucius, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mencius, transmitting their teaching from one to another, brought goodness to all under Heaven. Once Mencius had died, the learning of the sages…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不傳先生崛起千載之後獨得不傳之秘
祖先天之易作太極之書所謂太極云者
蓋本於易有太極而陰陽五行人物由此
而生即太極生兩儀兩儀生四象四象生
八卦之謂也自太極之在造化者言之則
即天地可以推太極動靜之妙所謂立天
之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛也自
太極之在品彙者言之惟聖人會太極動
靜之全所謂立人之道曰仁與義也至於
===
易通之書又與此圖相為表裏所謂誠者
即圖之言太極而大哉乾元萬物資始乾
道變化各正性命即圖之陽動而陰靜也
所謂五殊二實二本則一此自末以緣本
萬物統體一太極也所謂一實萬分萬一
各正此自本而之末一物各具一太極也
太極之書祖先天之易則其象數宜無不
同今觀太極自一而二自二而五即推至
於萬物其則自一而二自二而四自四而
punctuated:
不傳。先生崛起千載之後，獨得不傳之秘，祖先天之易，作太極之書。所謂太極云者，蓋本於「易有太極」，而陰陽五行人物由此而生，即「太極生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦」之謂也。自太極之在造化者言之，則即天地可以推太極動靜之妙，所謂「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛」也。自太極之在品彙者言之，惟聖人會太極動靜之全，所謂「立人之道曰仁與義」也。至於《易通》之書，又與此圖相為表裏。所謂誠者，即圖之言太極；而「大哉乾元，萬物資始」，「乾道變化，各正性命」，即圖之陽動而陰靜也。所謂「五殊二實，二本則一」，此自末以緣本，萬物統體一太極也。所謂「一實萬分，萬一各正」，此自本而之末，一物各具一太極也。

太極之書祖先天之易，則其象數宜無不同。今觀太極，自一而二，自二而五，即推至於萬物；其則自一而二，自二而四，自四而
translation_en:
…was no longer transmitted. The Master arose a thousand years later and alone grasped the secrets that had ceased to be transmitted. Taking the Before-Heaven Changes as his foundation, he composed his work on the Supreme Ultimate. What he calls the Supreme Ultimate is based on the statement, “In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate.” Yin and yang, the five phases, human beings, and other things arise from it. This is precisely what is meant by “The Supreme Ultimate generates the two modes; the two modes generate the four images; the four images generate the eight trigrams.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate within the processes of creation and transformation, one can infer from Heaven and Earth the subtle workings of its activity and stillness. This is what is meant by “Establishing the Way of Heaven, we speak of yin and yang; establishing the Way of Earth, we speak of yielding and firmness.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate within the various categories of beings, only the sage comprehends the entirety of its activity and stillness. This is what is meant by “Establishing the Way of humanity, we speak of benevolence and righteousness.” As for the book Comprehending the Changes (Yitong), it and this diagram mutually elucidate one another as inner substance and outward expression. What the book calls sincerity is what the diagram calls the Supreme Ultimate. “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian: the myriad things draw upon it for their beginnings” and “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, each thing attaining its proper nature and allotted destiny” correspond to the diagram’s active yang and still yin. The statement “The five are distinct, yet their realities are two; the two are rooted in one” traces the branches back to their root: the myriad things, taken as a whole, are one Supreme Ultimate. The statement “The one reality differentiates into the myriad, and each of the myriad attains its proper state” proceeds from the root to the branches: each individual thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

Since the work on the Supreme Ultimate takes the Before-Heaven Changes as its foundation, their images and numbers ought to agree in every respect. Yet, examining the Supreme Ultimate, we see a progression from one to two, from two to five, and thence directly to the myriad things; the other sequence [?] proceeds from one to two, from two to four, and from four to …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
八自八而十六自十六而三十二自三十
二而六十四然後萬物之理備誠若有可
疑者然物理本同而象數亦無二致但推
得有詳畧耳通書一篇本名易通則六十
四卦疑皆有其說今考其書獨有乾損益
家人睽復無妄蒙艮等說則亦有未安者
然先生之書散逸頗多葢本有而今亡矣
先天太極二圖雖同一發明造化之妙也
然先天乃伏羲本圖非康節所自作雖無
===
言語而所該甚廣太極却是濂溪自作發
明易中大槩綱領意思而已故格局則太
極不如先天之大而詳義理則先天不如
太極之精而約也太極西銘二書雖同一
開示學者之言也然西銘則推人以之天
即近以明遠於學者日用最為親切太極
則詳於性命之原而畧於進為之目有不
可以驟而語者故程子於西銘嘗屢言以
示門人而太極未嘗一言及之也至若劉
punctuated:
八，自八而十六，自十六而三十二，自三十二而六十四，然後萬物之理備，誠若有可疑者。然物理本同，而象數亦無二致，但推得有詳畧耳。《通書》一篇，本名《易通》，則六十四卦疑皆有其說。今考其書，獨有乾、損、益、家人、睽、復、無妄、蒙、艮等說，則亦有未安者。然先生之書散逸頗多，葢本有而今亡矣。
先天、太極二圖，雖同一發明造化之妙也，然先天乃伏羲本圖，非康節所自作，雖無言語，而所該甚廣。太極却是濂溪自作，發明《易》中大槩綱領意思而已。故格局則太極不如先天之大而詳，義理則先天不如太極之精而約也。
太極、西銘二書，雖同一開示學者之言也，然西銘則推人以之天，即近以明遠，於學者日用最為親切。太極則詳於性命之原，而畧於進為之目，有不可以驟而語者。故程子於西銘，嘗屢言以示門人，而太極未嘗一言及之也。至若劉
translation_en:
…eight, from eight to sixteen, from sixteen to thirty-two, and from thirty-two to sixty-four; only then are the principles of the myriad things fully encompassed. There does indeed seem to be something questionable here. Yet the principles of things are fundamentally the same, and their images and numbers likewise admit of no discrepancy; the deductions merely differ in their degree of detail. The work entitled Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu) was originally called Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), so presumably it contained explanations of all sixty-four hexagrams. Examining the work now, however, we find explanations only of such hexagrams as Qian, Sun, Yi, Jiaren, Kui, Fu, Wuwang, Meng, and Gen. This, too, leaves something unsettled. Yet many of the Master's writings have been scattered and lost; these explanations probably once existed but are now lost.
Although the diagrams of the Prior Heaven and the Supreme Ultimate both elucidate the wonders of creation and transformation, the Prior Heaven is Fuxi's original diagram, not something Kangjie himself devised. Though it contains no words, its scope is very broad. The Supreme Ultimate, by contrast, was devised by Lianxi himself, merely to elucidate the general framework and purport of the Book of Changes. Thus, in structure, the Supreme Ultimate is less comprehensive and detailed than the Prior Heaven; in its exposition of principles, however, the Prior Heaven is less refined and concise than the Supreme Ultimate.
Although the two works, the Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription, both offer instruction to learners, the Western Inscription proceeds from humanity to Heaven, illuminating what is distant through what is near, and is especially immediate and pertinent to learners' daily lives. The Supreme Ultimate treats the source of human nature and Heaven's mandate in detail, but gives only a brief account of the specific steps for advancing in self-cultivation; it contains matters that cannot be discussed with learners hastily. Thus Master Cheng repeatedly spoke of the Western Inscription to instruct his disciples, but never said a word about the Supreme Ultimate. As for Liu…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
子所謂天地之中即濂溪太極之謂蓋中
只是恰好處極是在中至極之理也橫渠
太虛之說本為無極之意殊不知無極是
該虛實清濁而言太虛只說得清虛一邊
耳嗟夫伊洛道喪寖失其真賴有考亭朱
夫子上接聖賢相傳之道統著書立言私
淑後人其本義啓蒙諸書皆所以闡揚乎
太極之理也噫道學得濂溪而始傳濂溪
得朱子而益明朱子實有大造於萬世學
===
者矣謹對
第三問
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批場中答此策者多不能以其迹
而原其心惟此作稍推原聖心步步著實無異當時親炙者高
薦何疑
同考試官教諭陸　批隨問隨答略無蹇詞策場中作者
考試官訓導孫　批延見用心希聖之學
考試官教諭柯　批三場多可錄錄此以例其餘
punctuated:
子所謂天地之中，即濂溪太極之謂。蓋中只是恰好處，極是在中至極之理也。橫渠太虛之說，本為無極之意，殊不知無極是該虛實清濁而言，太虛只說得清虛一邊耳。嗟夫！伊洛道喪，寖失其真，賴有考亭朱夫子，上接聖賢相傳之道統，著書立言，私淑後人。其本義、啓蒙諸書，皆所以闡揚乎太極之理也。噫！道學得濂溪而始傳，濂溪得朱子而益明，朱子實有大造於萬世學者矣。謹對。
第三問
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李批：場中答此策者，多不能以其迹而原其心。惟此作稍推原聖心，步步著實，無異當時親炙者，高薦何疑？
同考試官教諭陸批：隨問隨答，略無蹇詞，策場中作者。
考試官訓導孫批：延見用心希聖之學。
考試官教諭柯批：三場多可錄，錄此以例其餘。
translation_en:
…what Master Liu called “the mean of Heaven and Earth” is precisely what Lianxi called the Supreme Ultimate. The mean is simply the point of perfect appropriateness; the ultimate is the principle within the mean carried to its utmost perfection. Hengqu’s explanation of the Great Void was originally intended to express the meaning of the Non-Ultimate. He failed to understand, however, that the Non-Ultimate encompasses both emptiness and substantiality, clarity and turbidity, whereas the Great Void speaks only of the clear and empty side. Alas! The Way of the masters of the Yi and Luo rivers fell into decline and gradually lost its true character. Fortunately, Master Zhu of Kaoting carried forward the orthodox succession of the Way transmitted by the sages and worthies, composing books and setting forth teachings through which later generations could learn from him. His Original Meaning, Introduction to the Study of the Changes, and other works all elucidate the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. Ah! The learning of the Way began to be transmitted through Lianxi, and Lianxi’s teachings became still clearer through Master Zhu. Master Zhu truly rendered an immense service to learners for all generations. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Third Question
Luo Qinshun
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Most candidates answering this policy question could not trace the sage’s intentions through his deeds. This essay alone goes some way toward investigating the sage’s mind. Every step is firmly grounded, as though its author had personally studied under him in his own day. What doubt can there be about recommending it highly?
Comment by Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor: Each question receives its answer, without the slightest awkwardness of expression. An accomplished writer among the candidates composing policy essays.
Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: This reveals [?] a learning that applies the mind to aspiring to sagehood.
Comment by Examiner Ke, Instructor: Much from all three sessions merits selection. This piece is selected to exemplify the rest.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對欲觀聖人之迹當知聖人之道欲知聖
人之道當原聖人之心盖聖人之心一道
之所寓而言行之迹一道之所形也得其
心則可以知其道知其道則凡跡之同異
皆可以會而通之合而一之而無所疑矣
苟徒泥其跡而不原其心明其道以會其
同異惡足以知聖人也哉嗟夫尼丘毓秀
孔聖肇生廓宇宙而一人亘古今而獨盛
道參乎兩間法垂於萬世誠非後人所敢
===
妄議也然其言行之載諸經傳者似有小
異不能無疑愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸
矣姑即其一二而論之如里必擇乎仁厚
較之居不陋乎九夷者若戾矣殊不知化
於人者常人之事固當擇化人者聖人之
事不必擇也亂邦不居比之公山欲往者
似背矣殊不知遷善避惡固君子潔身之
常道而化惡為善又聖人誨人之本心也
從先進以示損過就中之意從周制以盡
punctuated: 對：欲觀聖人之迹，當知聖人之道；欲知聖人之道，當原聖人之心。盖聖人之心，一道之所寓；而言行之迹，一道之所形也。得其心，則可以知其道；知其道，則凡跡之同異，皆可以會而通之，合而一之，而無所疑矣。苟徒泥其跡，而不原其心、明其道，以會其同異，惡足以知聖人也哉！嗟夫！尼丘毓秀，孔聖肇生，廓宇宙而一人，亘古今而獨盛。道參乎兩間，法垂於萬世，誠非後人所敢妄議也。然其言行之載諸經傳者，似有小異，不能無疑。愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸矣。姑即其一二而論之。如里必擇乎仁厚，較之居不陋乎九夷者，若戾矣。殊不知，化於人者，常人之事，固當擇；化人者，聖人之事，不必擇也。亂邦不居，比之公山欲往者，似背矣。殊不知，遷善避惡，固君子潔身之常道；而化惡為善，又聖人誨人之本心也。從先進，以示損過就中之意；從周制，以盡
translation_en:
In reply: To examine the sage’s deeds, one must understand his Way; to understand his Way, one must trace it to his heart. For the sage’s heart is where the one Way resides, while the outward traces of his words and actions are where that Way takes form. Grasp his heart, and one can understand his Way; understand his Way, and all the similarities and differences in his deeds can be comprehended together and reconciled into a unity, leaving no room for doubt. If one merely clings to his outward deeds without tracing them to his heart and clarifying his Way so as to reconcile their similarities and differences, how could one adequately understand the sage?

Ah! Niqiu nurtured its finest essence, and the sage Confucius was born. In the vast universe he stood alone; throughout antiquity and the present his excellence was unrivaled. His Way ranked alongside Heaven and Earth, and his example was handed down for ten thousand generations. He is certainly not someone whom later men would dare discuss recklessly. Yet his words and actions as recorded in the classics and their commentaries seem to contain minor discrepancies, which cannot but give rise to doubts. I, this humble student, have also recited and studied them and grasped their purport.

Let me discuss just one or two examples. His insistence that one choose a neighborhood marked by benevolence and generosity seems at odds with his view that dwelling among the Nine Yi would involve no uncouthness. What this overlooks is that being transformed by others is the lot of ordinary people, who certainly must choose their surroundings; transforming others is the work of the sage, who need not choose. His refusal to reside in a disorderly state seems inconsistent with his wish to go to Gongshan. What this overlooks is that turning toward goodness and avoiding evil is indeed the gentleman’s usual way of preserving his own integrity, while transforming evil into goodness is also the sage’s fundamental intention in instructing others. He followed the earlier practitioners to show his intention of reducing excess and attaining the mean; he followed the institutions of Zhou to fulfill…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
為下不倍之道從夫先進非即所以從周
乎言無類是我之教化有善反之功云不
移乃彼之暴棄無自反之道教雖無類豈
能移其下愚乎大學之道自致知始此聖
人文行忠信之先夫文小學之事自力行
始此弟子餘力學文之先夫行民無信不
立者全體之大信故為為政之先必信於
言者一事之小信故為為士之次知魯火
而不知廐焚非明於遠而暗於近也蓋桓
===
僖之廟功德不足以存火之者天道之必
然也廐牧之地人馬之所兩集焚之者人
事之偶然也拜南子而不拜陽貨非重於
此而輕於彼也古者仕於其國有見小君
之禮彼須見而吾則往見非行其禮之當
然乎大夫有賜於士雖有往拜之禮彼瞯
亡而吾亦瞯亡非欲其禮之相稱乎箕子
比干微子也觀其行雖有死生去就之殊
原其心同一至誠惻怛之意所以同謂之
punctuated: 為下不倍之道。從夫先進，非即所以從周乎？言無類，是我之教化有善反之功；云不移，乃彼之暴棄無自反之道。教雖無類，豈能移其下愚乎？大學之道自致知始，此聖人文行忠信之先夫文；小學之事自力行始，此弟子餘力學文之先夫行。民無信不立者，全體之大信，故為為政之先；必信於言者，一事之小信，故為為士之次。知魯火而不知廐焚，非明於遠而暗於近也。蓋桓僖之廟，功德不足以存，火之者，天道之必然也；廐牧之地，人馬之所兩集，焚之者，人事之偶然也。拜南子而不拜陽貨，非重於此而輕於彼也。古者仕於其國，有見小君之禮；彼須見，而吾則往見，非行其禮之當然乎？大夫有賜於士，雖有往拜之禮，彼瞯亡，而吾亦瞯亡，非欲其禮之相稱乎？箕子、比干、微子也，觀其行，雖有死生去就之殊；原其心，同一至誠惻怛之意，所以同謂之
translation_en:
…the principle that one in a subordinate position must not be disloyal. Is following the earlier practitioners not precisely the means of following Zhou? When Confucius says that teaching recognizes no distinctions of kind, he means that his instruction has the power to bring people back to goodness; when he says that some cannot be changed, this is because they have cast themselves away and lack the means to turn back of their own accord. Though teaching recognizes no distinctions of kind, how could it change the most foolish?

The Way of the Great Learning begins with extending knowledge: this is why, among cultural learning, conduct, loyalty, and trustworthiness, the sage placed cultural learning first. Elementary learning begins with vigorous practice: this is why, in saying that disciples should study cultural learning when they have energy to spare, he placed conduct first. The saying that the people cannot stand without trust concerns trust in its comprehensive, greater sense; thus it takes precedence in governing. Being invariably true to one’s word concerns the lesser trustworthiness of an individual matter; thus it occupies a secondary place in qualifying as a gentleman.

Knowing of the fire in Lu but not knowing that his own stable was burning does not mean that he understood distant things but was ignorant of what was nearby. The merits and virtues of Dukes Huan and Xi were insufficient to warrant the preservation of their temples; that fire should consume them was an inevitable consequence of the Way of Heaven. A stable, however, is a place where people and horses gather together; its burning was a chance occurrence in human affairs.

Paying respects to Nanzi but not to Yang Huo did not mean that he esteemed the former and slighted the latter. In antiquity, those serving in a state were ritually obliged to have an audience with the ruler’s consort. When she requested an audience and he went to see her, was this not performing what ritual properly required? When a grand master bestowed a gift upon a gentleman, ritual did require the recipient to go and offer thanks. Yet the other had watched for his absence, and he likewise watched for the other’s absence: was this not intended to make their ritual courtesies correspond?

As for Jizi, Bi Gan, and Weizi, their actions differed in dying or surviving, withdrawing or remaining in service. But if we examine their hearts, all shared the same utmost sincerity and compassionate concern. This is why all were called…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
三仁大伯文王也或當為而不欲為以全
人子之孝或可為而不忍為以盡人臣之
忠所以同謂之至德殷夏之後尚有杞宋
之所存也故有據而可考杞宋之後無復
杞宋之所存矣此無徵而不信其於孔子
之知何所損不待結纓之日而豫知子路
之死人事之可必也不能於終日之頃而
先知顏淵之夭天命之不幸也其於孔子
之知何所虧荅昭公以為知禮所以諱其
===
君之過以存吾之忠厚斥管仲以不知禮
所以暴其人之罪以著彼之僭竊勸農事
以利天下者君子之公心也不适之褒而
誰褒學農事以利一已者小人之私心也
不遲之貶而誰貶必竭其兩端於鄙夫者
是我固無倦教之心不復於三隅之不反
者是彼終無受教之地論父母之國道在
可久也則遲遲於三日不朝之魯何過耶
論無道之君道在可去也則急急於一問
punctuated: 三仁。大伯、文王也，或當為而不欲為，以全人子之孝；或可為而不忍為，以盡人臣之忠，所以同謂之至德。殷夏之後，尚有杞宋之所存也，故有據而可考；杞宋之後，無復杞宋之所存矣，此無徵而不信，其於孔子之知何所損？不待結纓之日而豫知子路之死，人事之可必也；不能於終日之頃而先知顏淵之夭，天命之不幸也，其於孔子之知何所虧？荅昭公以為知禮，所以諱其君之過，以存吾之忠厚；斥管仲以不知禮，所以暴其人之罪，以著彼之僭竊。勸農事以利天下者，君子之公心也，不适之褒而誰褒？學農事以利一已者，小人之私心也，不遲之貶而誰貶？必竭其兩端於鄙夫者，是我固無倦教之心；不復於三隅之不反者，是彼終無受教之地。論父母之國，道在可久也，則遲遲於三日不朝之魯，何過耶？論無道之君，道在可去也，則急急於一問
translation_en:
…the three benevolent men. As for Taibo and King Wen, one was due to assume the throne but did not wish to do so, thereby fulfilling a son's filial devotion; the other could have assumed it but could not bear to do so, thereby fulfilling a subject's loyalty. Thus both were said to possess consummate virtue. After the Yin and Xia dynasties, there were still things preserved in Qi and Song, providing evidence that could be examined. After Qi and Song, there would no longer be what those states had preserved: without corroboration, such matters could not command belief. How does this diminish Confucius's knowledge?

That he foresaw Zilu's death before the day when Zilu tied his cap strings was because human affairs can have inevitable outcomes. That he could not foresee Yan Yuan's premature death even within the span of a day was because this was a misfortune ordained by Heaven. How does this detract from Confucius's knowledge? In answering that Duke Zhao understood ritual, he concealed his ruler's fault, thereby preserving his own loyalty and generosity. In rebuking Guan Zhong for not understanding ritual, he exposed that man's offenses, making manifest his usurpation of privileges above his station.

To commend agriculture for benefiting all under Heaven expresses the gentleman's concern for the common good: whom should he praise if not Kuo [Nangong Kuo]? To study agriculture for one's own benefit expresses the petty man's selfish concern: whom should he criticize if not Chi [Fan Chi]? That he invariably explored both ends of a question fully for an unlearned man shows that he himself was never weary of teaching. That he did not repeat his instruction for someone unable to infer the other three corners shows that the other person ultimately lacked the capacity to receive instruction.

When considering the land of one's parents, the Way permits one to remain: what fault, then, was there in his lingering in Lu, where there had been no court audience for three days [?]? When considering a ruler without the Way, the Way permits departure: thus his haste upon a single question…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
軍旅之衛何遽耶孔圉勤學好問是好善
而忘己之勢公叔錫氏爵祉是好善而忘
人之勢此皆合乎謚法之公者烏得不同
許其可以為文乎子貢因論學而知詩子
夏因論詩而知學是皆得於言意之表者
烏得不同許其可以言詩乎由是而觀則
知孔子之體即道而用即義聲為律而身
為度舉一身之言行誠萬世之標準也又
何彼此異同之可議哉愚生管窺蠡測不
能盡摹寫之詳惟執事其進教之謹對
===
第四問
汪□
同考試官教諭馮 批〔五策皆善此卷而此篇尤有見故錄之〕
同考試官教諭黃 批〔書孔學者切務當求學古人書博而約而有自得之趣此篇深究古書與夫運用之法 □□留心〕
〔於書學而有所得者也宜錄之以為學書者式〕
考試官訓導孫 批〔觀此卷必其能游于藝者〕
考試官教諭柯 批〔有筆手〕
punctuated:
軍旅之衛，何遽耶？孔圉勤學好問，是好善而忘己之勢；公叔錫氏爵祉，是好善而忘人之勢。此皆合乎謚法之公者，烏得不同許其可以為文乎？子貢因論學而知詩，子夏因論詩而知學，是皆得於言意之表者，烏得不同許其可以言詩乎？由是而觀，則知孔子之體即道而用即義，聲為律而身為度，舉一身之言行，誠萬世之標準也。又何彼此異同之可議哉？愚生管窺蠡測，不能盡摹寫之詳，惟執事其進教之。謹對。

第四問

汪□

同考試官教諭馮批〔五策皆善，此卷而此篇尤有見，故錄之。〕

同考試官教諭黃批〔書孔學者切務，當求學古人書，博而約，而有自得之趣。此篇深究古書與夫運用之法，□□留心〕〔於書學而有所得者也。宜錄之，以為學書者式。〕

考試官訓導孫批〔觀此卷，必其能游于藝者。〕

考試官教諭柯批〔有筆手。〕
translation_en:
…military affairs in Wei—how was his departure unduly hasty? Kong Yu studied diligently and readily asked questions: this was loving goodness and forgetting his own standing. Gongshu received a clan name, rank, and blessings [?]: this was loving goodness and forgetting another’s standing. Both accorded with the impartial principles governing posthumous titles. How could Confucius fail to acknowledge alike that they deserved the title Wen, “Cultured”? Zigong came to understand the Poetry through discussing learning; Zixia came to understand learning through discussing the Poetry. Both grasped what lay beyond the explicit words and their meaning. How could Confucius fail to acknowledge alike that they could discuss the Poetry? Viewed in this light, Confucius embodied the Way in his fundamental being and righteousness in his actions. His voice was the pitch standard; his person, the measure. All his words and deeds truly provided a standard for ten thousand generations. What grounds, then, are there for disputing their similarities and differences in one instance or another? This ignorant student peers through a tube and measures with a ladle; I cannot fully portray every detail. I ask only that you, honored examiners, grant me further instruction. Respectfully submitted.

Fourth Question

Wang □

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔All five policy essays in this script are good, but this particular essay shows exceptional insight; hence its inclusion.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Calligraphy [?] is an urgent concern for scholars. One should seek to study the calligraphy of the ancients, ranging widely and then distilling its essentials, with the delight of attaining one’s own understanding. This essay thoroughly investigates ancient calligraphy and the methods of putting it into practice. [Two illegible characters] applies himself〕〔to the study of calligraphy and has attained something in it. It should be included as a model for students of calligraphy.〕

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Judging from this script, its author must be someone capable of finding recreation in the arts.〕

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔A skilled hand with the brush.〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對字書作而變化之體滋學書精而運用
之法密蓋書為六藝之一所以宣人文敷
治化紀六經應萬事經天而緯地皆有賴
於此者也豈他技藝之比哉誠不可以不
講也請因明問而陳其槩夫字書之作其
來尚矣自伏羲畫八卦而書契攸與蒼頡
觀鳥跡而字文以製以體天地之撰以類
萬物之情其圓應規其方應矩轉筆為圓
摺筆為方方之平為準圓之直為繩陰陽
===
五行所以成象成形者也書以方圓平直
為之主而輕重大小低昂長短斜正寓其
變焉六書之義至矣盡矣然其迭更迭變
伏羲氏有龍書神農氏有穗書軒轅氏有
垂雲書因所見而創也太昊氏為鸞書放
勲氏為龜書夏后氏為鍾鼎書隨所見而
製也自是而後史籀作大篆李斯作小篆
而隸則出於程邈焉史游作章草蔡邕作
飛白而楷則出於鍾繇焉乃若雲霧卷雲收
punctuated:
對：字書作，而變化之體滋；學書精，而運用之法密。蓋書為六藝之一，所以宣人文、敷治化、紀六經、應萬事，經天而緯地，皆有賴於此者也。豈他技藝之比哉？誠不可以不講也。請因明問而陳其槩。
夫字書之作，其來尚矣。自伏羲畫八卦，而書契攸與；蒼頡觀鳥跡，而字文以製。以體天地之撰，以類萬物之情。其圓應規，其方應矩。轉筆為圓，摺筆為方；方之平為準，圓之直為繩。陰陽五行，所以成象成形者也。書以方圓平直為之主，而輕重、大小、低昂、長短、斜正寓其變焉。六書之義，至矣，盡矣！然其迭更迭變，伏羲氏有龍書，神農氏有穗書，軒轅氏有垂雲書，因所見而創也；太昊氏為鸞書，放勲氏為龜書，夏后氏為鍾鼎書，隨所見而製也。自是而後，史籀作大篆，李斯作小篆，而隸則出於程邈焉；史游作章草，蔡邕作飛白，而楷則出於鍾繇焉。乃若雲霧卷雲收
translation_en:
In reply: As writing was created, its variant forms multiplied; as the study of calligraphy became more refined, the methods of wielding the brush became more exact. Writing is one of the Six Arts. It serves to manifest human culture, spread the transforming influence of government, record the Six Classics, and meet the needs of all affairs. The ordering of heaven and earth alike depends upon it. How could it be compared with other technical arts? It certainly cannot be left unexamined. Allow me to set out its general principles in response to your discerning question.
The creation of writing reaches far back into antiquity. When Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams, written records arose; when Cangjie observed birds’ tracks, written characters were fashioned. These embodied the workings of heaven and earth and represented the dispositions of the myriad things. Their roundness conformed to the compass, their squareness to the carpenter’s square. Turning the brush produced roundness; folding its movement produced squareness. The levelness of the square served as a leveling instrument, and the straightness of the round as a marking cord [?]. Yin and yang and the Five Phases are what produce images and give things form. Writing takes squareness, roundness, levelness, and straightness as its governing principles, while its variations reside in lightness and heaviness, size, lowness and height, length, and obliqueness and uprightness. The principles of the Six Categories of Characters are consummate and exhaustive!
Yet scripts successively changed and developed. Fuxi had dragon script, Shennong had grain-ear script, and Xuanyuan had hanging-cloud script: these were inventions inspired by what they saw. Taihao made luan-bird script, Fangxun made tortoise script, and the ruler of Xia made bell-and-tripod script: these too were fashioned after what they observed. Thereafter, Shi Zhou created large-seal script, and Li Si created small-seal script, while clerical script originated with Cheng Miao. Shi You created chapter-cursive script, and Cai Yong created flying-white script, while regular script originated with Zhong Yao. As for clouds and mist, clouds curling and gathering [?]…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
鍾王之筆妙矣然視顏魯公之雄秀獨出
有如杜詩者是其精神形於以死赴國之
時則顏之書尤濟於用也虞世南之所稱
五絕詞翰居一薛稷之筆力遒麗當時莫
及虞稷之書善矣然較之柳公拳之心正
筆正由中見外者是有得於虛靜精忠之
間則柳之書尤有所本也且古人之書逸
少嘗云得法於白雲子蔡邕嘗云得神人
===
所授八角垂芒之書人皆信其有異傳也
殊不知白雲子即心也神人亦心也心有
所契而寓言耳古人執筆逸少得其法於
羣鵞之運頸懷素得其妙於夏雲之迴風
人皆議其為好事也殊不知鵞之運頸周
回而容與也雲之迴風變幻而悠揚也目
有所擊而心悟耳夫書札於儒事最近不
可以不學也學書之法當以執筆為先用
筆次之執筆之法所謂虛拳實腕指齊掌
punctuated: 鍾王之筆妙矣，然視顏魯公之雄秀獨出，有如杜詩者，是其精神形於以死赴國之時，則顏之書尤濟於用也。虞世南之所稱五絕，詞翰居一；薛稷之筆力遒麗，當時莫及。虞稷之書善矣，然較之柳公拳之心正筆正，由中見外者，是有得於虛靜精忠之間，則柳之書尤有所本也。且古人之書，逸少嘗云得法於白雲子，蔡邕嘗云得神人所授八角垂芒之書，人皆信其有異傳也。殊不知白雲子即心也，神人亦心也，心有所契而寓言耳。古人執筆，逸少得其法於羣鵞之運頸，懷素得其妙於夏雲之迴風，人皆議其為好事也。殊不知鵞之運頸，周回而容與也；雲之迴風，變幻而悠揚也。目有所擊而心悟耳。夫書札於儒事最近，不可以不學也。學書之法，當以執筆為先，用筆次之。執筆之法，所謂虛拳實腕，指齊掌
translation_en:
…The brushwork of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi is marvelous. Yet consider the uniquely vigorous and elegant calligraphy of Yan Lugong (Yan Zhenqing), comparable to Du Fu’s poetry: it manifests the spirit he displayed when he went to his death in service to the state. Thus Yan’s calligraphy was especially effective in practical service. Among the celebrated five excellences of Yu Shinan, literary and calligraphic accomplishment held one place; the vigorous beauty of Xue Ji’s brushwork was unmatched in his day. The calligraphy of Yu and Xue is fine. Yet compare it with Liu Gongquan’s [?; transcribed as 柳公拳] principle that when the heart is upright, the brush is upright: the inner self becomes visible outwardly. This reflects an attainment grounded in inner emptiness and stillness, wholehearted loyalty and devotion. Thus Liu’s calligraphy had an especially firm foundation.

Furthermore, concerning the calligraphy of the ancients, Yishao (Wang Xizhi) once said that he learned his method from Baiyunzi, the Master of White Clouds. Cai Yong once said that a divine being bestowed upon him a script with eight corners and trailing points. Everyone believes that they received extraordinary transmissions. They fail to understand that Baiyunzi is simply the heart, and the divine being is also the heart: the heart apprehended something, and they merely expressed it allegorically. As for how the ancients held the brush, Yishao learned his method from the movements of a flock of geese’s necks, while Huaisu grasped its subtleties from summer clouds swirling in the wind. Everyone regards these accounts as a fondness for curiosities. They fail to understand that the geese’s necks turn with unhurried ease, while clouds swirling in the wind transform and drift freely. Something strikes the eye, and the heart understands: that is all.

Now, writing is closely connected with the affairs of a Confucian scholar and must be studied. In learning calligraphy, holding the brush should come first, and wielding it second. The method of holding the brush is expressed in the saying: “Keep the fist hollow and the wrist firm, the fingers aligned and the palm…”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
空者執筆之際使虎口寬可容彈掌中虛
可容卵指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也所謂擫
捺鉤抉抵拒導送者擫用大指捺用食指
鉤抉用中指抵拒用無名指導送用小指
是也用筆之精鋒之或藏或出或正或側
與左用者藏則鋒藏畫中出則芒刃在外
正則鋒不偏露側則轉側取妍而左則弩
力過勁如反竹為弓者矣筆之有引有屻
有縱有複與舞動者引則引短為長屻則
===
屻長為短縱則送之欲迅複則重覆其畫
而舞則欲下不下如景山興雲者矣夫執
筆既熟用筆既精則其為書也可以追倣
古人而傳後世者矣抑豈徒為人觀美哉
蓋天文地文人文一也景星卿雲人共觀
之精金美玉人共寶之書人之心畫也人
之文也烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉愚也
行而不著習而不察姑揣摩以對未知是
否惟進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 空者，執筆之際，使虎口寬可容彈，掌中虛可容卵，指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也。所謂擫、捺、鉤、抉、抵、拒、導、送者，擫用大指，捺用食指，鉤、抉用中指，抵、拒用無名指，導、送用小指是也。用筆之精，鋒之或藏、或出、或正、或側與左用者，藏則鋒藏畫中，出則芒刃在外，正則鋒不偏露，側則轉側取妍，而左則弩力過勁，如反竹為弓者矣。筆之有引、有屻、有縱、有複與舞動者，引則引短為長，屻則屻長為短，縱則送之欲迅，複則重覆其畫，而舞則欲下不下，如景山興雲者矣。夫執筆既熟，用筆既精，則其為書也，可以追倣古人而傳後世者矣。抑豈徒為人觀美哉！蓋天文、地文、人文一也。景星卿雲，人共觀之；精金美玉，人共寶之。書，人之心畫也，人之文也，烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉！愚也，行而不著，習而不察，姑揣摩以對，未知是否，惟進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …“hollow” means that, when holding the brush, one leaves the opening between thumb and forefinger wide enough to accommodate a pellet, and the palm hollow enough to accommodate an egg; the fingers clasp the brush lightly, while the wrist remains firm. As for the techniques called pressing, bearing down, hooking, drawing out, supporting, resisting, guiding, and sending: pressing employs the thumb; bearing down, the index finger; hooking and drawing out, the middle finger; supporting and resisting, the ring finger; and guiding and sending, the little finger. Refinement in wielding the brush involves concealing or exposing its tip, keeping it upright or inclined, and using it toward the left [?]. When concealed, the tip remains within the stroke; when exposed, its sharp edge appears outside. When upright, the tip does not protrude to either side; when inclined, it turns sideways to achieve beauty. In leftward use [?], one exerts exceptional force, like bending bamboo backward to make a bow. The brush also has movements called extending, shortening [?], releasing, retracing, and dancing. Extending draws something short out into something long; shortening [?] reduces something long to something short. Releasing sends the brush forward swiftly; retracing goes back over the stroke. Dancing means being about to descend yet not descending, like clouds rising over a great mountain. Once one is practiced in holding the brush and accomplished in wielding it, one’s calligraphy can emulate the ancients and be handed down to later generations. Surely it is not merely intended to give others something beautiful to look at! The patterns of heaven, earth, and human culture are fundamentally one. Auspicious stars and felicitous clouds are admired by all; refined gold and fine jade are treasured by all. Writing depicts a person’s heart and expresses that person’s cultivated pattern. How could one be careless about it and fail to seek its highest excellence? In my ignorance, I act without understanding clearly and practice without examining closely. I have ventured to ponder these matters and offer this reply, not knowing whether it is correct. I would be most grateful if you would guide me further and instruct me.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第五問
范希淹
同考試官教諭劉　批〔斷制養士詰兵之道明晰而〕
〔藴故錄之〕
同考試官教諭俞　批〔處置養士詰兵之事允當無〕
〔如此篇是宜錄出〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔正得問意可取〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔時務所論鑿鑿可行有學者〕
論養士詰兵之法行於古者有優劣不能
===
不隨時以爲興衰行於今者雖盡善不可
不因時而爲損益蓋歷代養士詰兵之法
迄今凡幾變大率皆隨其優劣以爲興衰
耳爲治者欲使之常興而不衰可不因時
損益而求以盡其善哉請詳言之自古君
天下者固必資文德以致太平亦必資武
功以戡禍亂文武並用誠長治久安之計
也然而欲興文教必在於設學以養士故
成周之時遐不作人詠歌於棫樸薪槱之
punctuated:
第五問
范希淹
同考試官教諭劉　批〔斷制養士詰兵之道，明晰而〕〔藴，故錄之。〕
同考試官教諭俞　批〔處置養士詰兵之事，允當無〕〔如此篇，是宜錄出。〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔正得問意，可取。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔時務所論，鑿鑿可行，有學者。〕
論養士詰兵之法，行於古者有優劣，不能不隨時以爲興衰；行於今者雖盡善，不可不因時而爲損益。蓋歷代養士詰兵之法，迄今凡幾變，大率皆隨其優劣以爲興衰耳。爲治者欲使之常興而不衰，可不因時損益而求以盡其善哉？請詳言之。自古君天下者，固必資文德以致太平，亦必資武功以戡禍亂。文武並用，誠長治久安之計也。然而欲興文教，必在於設學以養士。故成周之時，「遐不作人」詠歌於《棫樸》薪槱之
translation_en:
Fifth Question
Fan Xiyan

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔His judgment concerning the principles of nurturing scholars and putting military forces in order is clear and profound [?]; therefore this answer is included.〕
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: 〔His handling of the matters of nurturing scholars and putting military forces in order is sound and appropriate; none is like this essay [?]. It should be selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔It grasps precisely the intent of the question and merits acceptance.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔Its discussion of current affairs offers definite, practicable proposals and shows learning [?].〕
I submit that methods of nurturing scholars and putting military forces in order, as practiced in antiquity, had strengths and weaknesses and inevitably flourished or declined with the times. Even if those practiced today are entirely sound, they must still be curtailed or augmented as circumstances require. Through how many transformations have the methods of successive dynasties passed down to the present? Broadly speaking, they have flourished or declined according to their strengths and weaknesses. If those who govern wish them always to flourish and never to decline, can they fail to adjust them to the times and seek to perfect them? Allow me to explain in detail.
Since antiquity, those who ruled the realm have certainly had to rely on civil virtue to bring about peace, but they have also had to rely on military achievements to quell calamity and disorder. Employing civil and military means together is indeed the way to secure lasting good government and enduring peace. Yet promoting civil instruction necessarily depends on establishing schools to nurture scholars. Thus, in the flourishing Zhou era, “How could he fail to nurture men?” was sung in Dense Oak Clusters (Yupu), amid its account of firewood heaped for burning …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
餘鎬京辟雍揄揚於豐芑有事之際養士
之美無以加矣自是而後若漢武帝爲博
士而置弟子員明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮
唐太宗徵天下名儒增廣生員玄宗令天
下州縣里皆置學宋初旣設太學武學以
教天下之士其後復設宗學以教宗室之
士漢唐宋之養士大槩如此而永平貞觀
爲最盛惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以爲
教耳我
===
太祖高皇帝旣定天下乃設學校以養士其始
也士有定額而選之也精學有常規而教
之也嚴斥異端而以正道淑人黜詞賦而
以經術取士其法美矣漸涵旣久秀民日
多遂因而漸變至于今名州大邑增至數
倍司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中或
䠶於逸樂而挑達城闕或急於進取而貪
緣奔貴至屢
punctuated:
餘，鎬京辟雍揄揚於豐芑有事之際，養士之美無以加矣。自是而後，若漢武帝爲博士而置弟子員，明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮，唐太宗徵天下名儒，增廣生員，玄宗令天下州縣里皆置學，宋初旣設太學、武學以教天下之士，其後復設宗學以教宗室之士。漢唐宋之養士大槩如此，而永平、貞觀爲最盛，惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以爲教耳。
我太祖高皇帝旣定天下，乃設學校以養士。其始也，士有定額，而選之也精；學有常規，而教之也嚴。斥異端而以正道淑人，黜詞賦而以經術取士，其法美矣。漸涵旣久，秀民日多，遂因而漸變。至于今，名州大邑增至數倍。司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中，或䠶於逸樂而挑達城闕，或急於進取而貪緣奔貴，至屢
translation_en:
…and the Biyong ritual academy at Haojing was celebrated in the verses about millet by the Feng River and the undertaking there. Nothing could surpass this excellence in nurturing scholars. Thereafter, Emperor Wu of Han established student places under the Erudites, and Emperor Ming visited the Biyong to perform the ceremony honoring the aged. Emperor Taizong of Tang summoned renowned Confucian scholars from throughout the realm and increased student enrollment; Emperor Xuanzong ordered schools established in every prefecture, county, and village throughout the realm. At the beginning of the Song, the Imperial University and the Military School were established to educate scholars throughout the realm; subsequently, schools for the imperial clan were also established to educate its members. Such, broadly, were the arrangements for nurturing scholars under the Han, Tang, and Song. They flourished most during the Yongping and Zhenguan reign periods. Regrettably, however, these rulers could not emulate the established Zhou order by personally practicing benevolence and righteousness as the basis of their teaching.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had pacified the realm, he established schools to nurture scholars. At first, student places had fixed quotas, and selection was exacting; schools had standing regulations, and instruction was strict. He rejected heterodox teachings and improved people through the correct Way; he set aside lyric poetry and rhapsodies and selected scholars through learning in the classics. These methods were excellent. After prolonged cultivation, talented people became more numerous by the day, and the arrangements gradually changed accordingly. By the present time, enrollment in prominent prefectures and large counties has increased severalfold. Those responsible for administration and education have proved unable to keep the students within the prescribed rules. Some indulge in ease and pleasure [?], roaming frivolously about the city gates; others, impatient for advancement, seek connections greedily and court the powerful. Matters have reached the point of repeated…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
敕憲臣以提督之猶不能盡弭其弊也為今
之計竊以為宜沙汰之使玉石不得以
兼收莠之鋤之使苗莠不得以雜植仍慎
擇有德行道藝者以為之帥躬廉恥以正
其行明義理以澤其文尊其賢以激其不
及嘉其善而矜其不能則養士之法其庶
幾乎欲奮武衛又在於講武以詰兵故成
周之時居則為比閭族黨州鄉之民行則
為伍兩卒旅軍師之衆其詰兵之法無以
===
尚矣自是而後南軍主守衛王宮北軍主
巡徼京城此漢之兵也諸府六百三十四
所關中三百六十一所得強幹弱枝之法
有居重馭輕之勢其後一變而為彍騎其
制遂壞再變而為方鎮其制大壞此唐之
兵也以五代之樞密偏重則以文臣為之
以五代之藩鎮太橫則以文臣任之禁將
之貴者為三衙禁旅之要者為四廂諸司
募者曰役兵諸州募者曰廂兵什伍其民
punctuated:
敕憲臣以提督之，猶不能盡弭其弊也。為今之計，竊以為宜沙汰之，使玉石不得以兼收；莠之鋤之，使苗莠不得以雜植。仍慎擇有德行道藝者以為之帥，躬廉恥以正其行，明義理以澤其文，尊其賢以激其不及，嘉其善而矜其不能，則養士之法其庶幾乎！
欲奮武衛，又在於講武以詰兵。故成周之時，居則為比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則為伍兩卒旅軍師之衆，其詰兵之法無以尚矣。自是而後，南軍主守衛王宮，北軍主巡徼京城，此漢之兵也。諸府六百三十四所，關中三百六十一所，得強幹弱枝之法，有居重馭輕之勢。其後一變而為彍騎，其制遂壞；再變而為方鎮，其制大壞，此唐之兵也。以五代之樞密偏重，則以文臣為之；以五代之藩鎮太橫，則以文臣任之。禁將之貴者為三衙，禁旅之要者為四廂。諸司募者曰役兵，諸州募者曰廂兵，什伍其民
translation_en:
…edicts commanded censorial officials to supervise them, yet even this could not entirely eliminate these abuses. As a plan for the present, I humbly submit that unsuitable students should be weeded out, so that jade and common stone are not accepted together; the weeds should be hoed away, so that crops and weeds are not planted together. Moreover, men possessing virtuous conduct and mastery of the Way and the arts should be carefully selected to lead them. By personally exemplifying integrity and a sense of shame, they would correct the students’ conduct; by elucidating moral principles, they would enrich their writing. They should honor the worthy to spur on those who fall short, commend what is good in them, and show compassion for their shortcomings. Would this not bring the method of nurturing scholars close to the ideal?
