To invigorate the military guards likewise requires practicing military skills to put the troops in order. Thus, in the flourishing Zhou era, when at home the people belonged to neighborhood units called bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang; when on campaign, they formed military units called wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. No method of ordering troops could surpass this. Thereafter, the Southern Army was responsible for guarding the imperial palace, and the Northern Army for patrolling the capital: these were the military arrangements of the Han. There were 634 military headquarters, of which 361 were in Guanzhong. This achieved the method of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, establishing a disposition in which the weight concentrated at the center controlled the lighter forces elsewhere. Subsequently, a change to the Expanded Cavalry (Guangqi) caused the system to deteriorate; a further change to regional military commands brought its thorough collapse. These were the military arrangements of the Tang. Because the Bureau of Military Affairs had held disproportionate power during the Five Dynasties, civil officials were appointed to direct it; because the regional military commands of the Five Dynasties had been excessively overbearing, civil officials were appointed to take charge of them. The highest-ranking commanders of the palace armies headed the Three Commands, while the principal formations of the palace forces constituted the Four Divisions. Those recruited by the various offices were called service troops; those recruited by the various prefectures were called prefectural troops. The common people were organized into groups of ten and five…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
而敎之曰民兵番民内附而用之曰番兵此
宋之兵也漢唐宋之詰兵大槩如此而唐
之府兵則爲最優以其有成周寓兵於農
之遺意耳我
太祖高皇帝旣一宇内乃設衛所以詰兵其法
也軍數盈而行伍以飭師律嚴而訓練以
時以戰則勝以攻則克其兵法善矣承平旣
久文恬武嬉遂因而漸弊至絶者無句而
續逃避者莫從而稽名數雖存在伍無幾
===
司兵柄者恒無以應變紓於緩急之際無事
則僅備差遣有事則借募民兵至屢
宸慮特
勅御史以清理之終亦不能悉復其舊也爲
今之計竊以爲宜復
祖宗官吏枉法受財之典以補其已絶之數復
祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律以警其脫放之弊其
於清理之際則審閱其板籍以清其源及
其發遣之時則嚴切其文移以防其欺仍
punctuated:
而敎之，曰民兵；番民内附而用之，曰番兵。此宋之兵也。漢唐宋之詰兵大槩如此，而唐之府兵則爲最優，以其有成周寓兵於農之遺意耳。
我太祖高皇帝旣一宇内，乃設衛所以詰兵。其法也，軍數盈而行伍以飭，師律嚴而訓練以時，以戰則勝，以攻則克，其兵法善矣。承平旣久，文恬武嬉，遂因而漸弊。至絶者無句而續，逃避者莫從而稽，名數雖存，在伍無幾。司兵柄者恒無以應變，紓於緩急之際。無事則僅備差遣，有事則借募民兵，至屢宸慮，特勅御史以清理之，終亦不能悉復其舊也。
爲今之計，竊以爲宜復祖宗官吏枉法受財之典，以補其已絶之數；復祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律，以警其脫放之弊。其於清理之際，則審閱其板籍以清其源；及其發遣之時，則嚴切其文移以防其欺，仍
translation_en:
…and train them, calling them militia. Non-Han peoples who submitted to the dynasty were employed as tribal troops. These were the military forces of the Song. Such, in broad outline, were the military arrangements of the Han, Tang, and Song. The Tang militia system (fubing) was the best, for it preserved something of the intent of the Zhou practice of embedding soldiers among the farming population.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had unified the realm, he established guards and battalions to organize the armed forces. Under this system, troop quotas were filled and the ranks kept in order; military discipline was strict, and training took place at prescribed times. In battle they prevailed, and in assaults they conquered. His military system was excellent. But after prolonged peace, civil officials grew complacent and military officers idle, and abuses gradually developed. When military households died out, no replacements were conscripted to continue their service; those who fled or evaded service were not investigated. Although names and quotas remained on the registers, few men were actually in the ranks. Those wielding military authority were continually unable to respond to unforeseen developments or provide relief in emergencies [?]. In quiet times, the troops barely sufficed for routine assignments; when trouble arose, officials resorted to recruiting militia. This repeatedly occasioned imperial concern [?], and special orders were issued to investigating censors to rectify the registers. Yet even then, the former establishment could never be fully restored.
As a measure for the present, I humbly believe that the ancestral emperors’ statute concerning officials and clerks who accept bribes and pervert the law should be reinstated, to fill the vacancies left by extinct military households. Their law concerning military officers who commit private offenses should also be reinstated, to deter abuses involving the unauthorized release of soldiers from service. During the rectification process, the registers should be carefully examined to set matters right at their source. When men are dispatched, the official correspondence should be handled with strict care to prevent fraud. Furthermore…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪痛革官吏侵漁
朘剝之暴使各遂事育之願而不動懷土
之思則詰兵之法其庶幾乎夫養士詰兵
二者皆
國家之大政而九有志於學古入官者誠不
可以不究心也然管見如斯未知是否惟
執事進而教之
===
□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□
□□□□□□□□□□
國家之大□□□□□□□□
祖宗之意者皆□□□□□□
祖宗之□則詰兵之法其庶幾乎夫養士詰兵
朘剝之暴使各遂事育之願而不動懷土
中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪痛革官吏侵漁
punctuated:
中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪，痛革官吏侵漁朘剝之暴，使各遂事育之願，而不動懷土之思，則詰兵之法其庶幾乎！夫養士詰兵二者，皆國家之大政，而九有志於學古入官者，誠不可以不究心也。然管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事進而教之。

□□□□□□□□□，□□□□□□□□□□，□□□□□□□□□□。國家之大□□□□□□□□，祖宗之意者皆□□□□□□。祖宗之□，則詰兵之法其庶幾乎！夫養士詰兵，朘剝之暴，使各遂事育之願，而不動懷土，中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪，痛革官吏侵漁。
translation_en:
…strictly punish [?] the offense of withholding portions of the monthly grain rations in the guards and battalions, and resolutely eradicate the violent exploitation and extortion practiced by officials and clerks. Let each man fulfill his wish to support his parents and nurture his family, without stirring thoughts of his native place: would this not come close to a proper method of putting the military in order? Nurturing scholars and putting the military in order are both major affairs of state. Those [?] who aspire to study antiquity and enter official service truly cannot neglect to examine them carefully. Such, however, are my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I ask you, sir, to guide and instruct me further.

[Three illegible passages.] The state's great… [illegible]. Those who… the intentions of the imperial ancestors all… [illegible]. The imperial ancestors'… [illegible]: would this not come close to a proper method of putting the military in order? As for nurturing scholars and putting the military in order… the violence of extortion, allowing each man to fulfill his wish to support his parents and nurture his family, without stirring attachment to his native place… strictly punish [?] the offense of withholding portions of the monthly grain rations in the guards and battalions, and resolutely eradicate exploitation by officials and clerks… [The surviving text in this half-leaf is fragmentary and appears out of sequence.]

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
弘治壬子秋
今聖天子取士第二科也江西試
事畢將錄所得士以
獻〔鑰〕當序其後竊惟科目以文
章校士蓋欲於言語文字之
間以觀人耳非徒以其辭而
===
已也士患不深於道爾深於
道將自裕於言以是觀人其
庶幾哉若乃移舊綴之曲折
於短褐而謂世方無華裾取
殘餕而飣餖爲華饌而謂世
方無正味若此者吾不知其
於道何如耶如是而欲觀其
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

弘治壬子秋，今聖天子取士第二科也。江西試事畢，將錄所得士以獻，〔鑰〕當序其後。竊惟科目以文章校士，蓋欲於言語文字之間以觀人耳，非徒以其辭而已也。士患不深於道爾，深於道，將自裕於言。以是觀人，其庶幾哉！若乃移舊綴之曲折於短褐，而謂世方無華裾；取殘餕而飣餖爲華饌，而謂世方無正味。若此者，吾不知其於道何如耶？如是而欲觀其
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The autumn of the renzi year of Hongzhi (1492) marked the second examination for selecting scholars under our present sagely Son of Heaven. With the Jiangxi examination concluded, a record of the scholars selected was to be compiled and presented to the throne. It fell to me (Yue 鑰) to write its postface.

I humbly reflect that the examination system assesses scholars through literary composition because it seeks to discern the person through his words and writing, not merely to judge his phrasing. What scholars should fear is insufficient depth in the Way. With depth in the Way, ease and abundance of expression will follow naturally. To assess people on this basis would surely come close to the aim!

But there are those who transfer the twists and turns of old patchwork onto a coarse hemp jacket [?], then declare that the world now has no splendid robes; who take leftovers and arrange them into a sumptuous feast, then declare that the world now has no true flavors. As for such people, I do not know where they stand in relation to the Way. To seek, under these circumstances, to discern their…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
人不亦難乎此擇士者所以
林心膂目不敢以易視也粵
為
國家得一天下士則異時亦足
以為天下重然舉者非私黨
舉之者非私恩此翟璜所以
不敢與魏成比而李克所以
不敢比周翟璜也或曰燕得
樂毅亦自隗起駿骨不遺則
千里之材自至於乎綳細熟
視於沙丘之野尚恐或失之
牝牡驪黃之外敢謂吾能得
其內而忘其外哉尚敢為循
人之獻哉
punctuated: 人，不亦難乎？此擇士者所以林心膂目，不敢以易視也。粵為國家得一天下士，則異時亦足以為天下重。然舉者非私黨，舉之者非私恩。此翟璜所以不敢與魏成比，而李克所以不敢比周翟璜也。或曰：「燕得樂毅，亦自隗起。駿骨不遺，則千里之材自至。」於乎！綳細熟視於沙丘之野，尚恐或失之牝牡驪黃之外，敢謂吾能得其內而忘其外哉？尚敢為循人之獻哉？
translation_en:
…the person—is this not difficult? This is why those who select scholars strain their hearts and eyes [?], not daring to regard the task lightly. If one obtains for the state a single scholar of outstanding talent in all the realm, he may in time lend weight to the realm itself. Yet those recommended are no private faction, and those recommending them confer no private favor. This is why Zhai Huang did not dare compare himself with Wei Cheng, and why Li Ke did not dare form a partisan alliance with Zhai Huang.

Someone says: “Yan’s acquisition of Yue Yi also began with Guo Wei. If even the bones of a fine horse are not overlooked, horses capable of traveling a thousand li will arrive of themselves.” Alas! Even scrutinizing closely [?] in the wilderness of Shaqiu, I still fear that I may fail to discern what lies beyond whether a horse is mare or stallion, black or yellow. Dare I claim that I can grasp its inner qualities and disregard its outward appearance? Would I still dare offer a recommendation merely to accommodate others [?]?

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓
導孫鑰謹序
punctuated: 直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓導孫鑰謹序。
translation_en: Respectfully prefaced by Sun Yue 孫鑰, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
之基示以仁敬之道太傅之身教也少傅奉世
子以法其所教而為進道之的詳吾啓迪之言
動彼警悟之意務俾心有所得而豁然貫通道
有所契而怡然領會少傅以言教如此則世子
寧不有所曉悟乎吁太傅少傅之所教雖異而
其所以為教則同先王設官養世子之意一何
至哉雖然先王之於世子不特立太傅少傅以
養之而已而又設師保疑丞及四輔三公焉不
特示君臣父子之道而已而又教長幼之義與
詩書禮樂焉養有常職而各惟其人教有常規
而一復其性此所以教喻德成而保有天下之
大也不然何以語曰一有元良萬國以貞有天
下者鑒之
樂著太始而禮居成物
黄洪
同考試官教諭劉　批〔題本平易作者多泛而不切見理　真達詞而無如此篇宜録之以式後學〕
同考試官教諭俞　批〔場中作者有以贊化育言者有〕
punctuated:
之基，示以仁敬之道，太傅之身教也。少傅奉世子以法其所教，而為進道之的，詳吾啓迪之言，動彼警悟之意，務俾心有所得而豁然貫通，道有所契而怡然領會。少傅以言教如此，則世子寧不有所曉悟乎？吁！太傅少傅之所教雖異，而其所以為教則同。先王設官養世子之意，一何至哉！雖然，先王之於世子，不特立太傅少傅以養之而已，而又設師保疑丞及四輔三公焉；不特示君臣父子之道而已，而又教長幼之義與詩書禮樂焉。養有常職而各惟其人，教有常規而一復其性，此所以教喻德成而保有天下之大也。不然，何以語曰：「一有元良，萬國以貞。」有天下者鑒之。

樂著太始而禮居成物
黄洪

同考試官教諭劉　批〔題本平易，作者多泛而不切。見理　真，達詞而無如此篇，宜録之以式後學。〕

同考試官教諭俞　批〔場中作者有以贊化育言者，有〕
translation_en:
…the foundation of it, showing him the way of benevolence and reverence: this is the Grand Preceptor’s teaching by personal example. The Junior Preceptor attends upon the heir apparent, helping him to emulate what has been taught and making it his target for advancing in the Way. He elaborates his words of instruction to awaken the prince’s understanding, striving to ensure that the prince gains insight in his heart and achieves a sudden, comprehensive understanding, and that he finds accord with the Way and grasps it with delight. If the Junior Preceptor teaches through words in this manner, how could the heir apparent fail to attain understanding? Ah! Although what the Grand Preceptor and Junior Preceptor teach differs, their purpose in teaching is the same. How utterly solicitous were the former kings in establishing offices to nurture the heir apparent!

Yet the former kings did not merely appoint a Grand Preceptor and Junior Preceptor to nurture him; they also appointed mentors, guardians, advisers, and assistants, together with the Four Auxiliaries and Three Dukes. Nor did they merely show him the way governing ruler and minister, father and son; they also taught him the proper relations between elder and younger, and the Odes, Documents, rites, and music. His nurture had established offices, each entrusted to the appropriate person; his instruction had established norms, all directed toward restoring his original nature. Through this, instruction brought understanding and virtue reached completion, enabling him to preserve possession of the vast realm. Otherwise, why would the saying declare, “Once there is a supremely worthy heir, the myriad states are set right”? Let those who possess the realm take this as their mirror.

“Music Manifests the Grand Beginning, while Rites Reside in Completed Things”
Huang Hong

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The topic is straightforward, but most writers treat it vaguely and fail to address it closely. This essay perceives the principles truly; the wording that follows is garbled [?]. It should be recorded as a model for later students.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor: 〔Among the writers in the examination hall, some discuss this in terms of assisting the transforming and nurturing processes of Heaven and Earth; others…〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以法造化而制作言者殊戾大旨惟此作體認明白寫出
禮樂功用合造化生成之妙深合本旨故錄之
考試官訓導孫　批〔講禮樂成功合造化處明白可觀〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔聖人制作　功用之大此作得之〕
論禮樂之用而合造化之生成焉蓋禮樂造化
相爲流通者也孰謂禮樂之用有不合造化之
生成哉樂記言禮樂成功之所合而及此意謂
人徒知禮樂制作於聖人而不知功用脗合乎
造化是故由天而作出於自然之和者樂也而
===
樂著太始焉以地而制出於自然之序者禮也
而禮居成物焉彼大哉乾元萬物資始此乾知
太始也乾以陽始萬物氣行而同和則樂情已
與流通無間矣令樂之用峻極于天而發達乎陽
之所生貫通乎神而橐籥乎物之所始無顯不至
無高不届是和之所在即樂之所在所謂敦和
率神而從天者是已非樂著太始而何至哉坤
元萬物資生此坤作成物也坤以陰成萬物質
具而異序則禮制已與契合爲一也令禮之用蟠
punctuated:
以法造化而制作言者，殊戾大旨。惟此作體認明白，寫出禮樂功用合造化生成之妙，深合本旨，故錄之。
考試官訓導孫，批〔講禮樂成功合造化處，明白可觀〕
考試官教諭柯，批〔聖人制作，功用之大，此作得之〕
論禮樂之用，而合造化之生成焉。蓋禮樂、造化相爲流通者也，孰謂禮樂之用有不合造化之生成哉？《樂記》言禮樂成功之所合而及此，意謂人徒知禮樂制作於聖人，而不知功用脗合乎造化。是故由天而作，出於自然之和者，樂也，而樂著太始焉；以地而制，出於自然之序者，禮也，而禮居成物焉。彼「大哉乾元，萬物資始」，此乾知太始也。乾以陽始萬物，氣行而同和，則樂情已與流通無間矣。令樂之用峻極于天，而發達乎陽之所生，貫通乎神，而橐籥乎物之所始，無顯不至，無高不届，是和之所在即樂之所在。所謂「敦和率神而從天」者，是已。非樂著太始而何？「至哉坤元，萬物資生」，此坤作成物也。坤以陰成萬物，質具而異序，則禮制已與契合爲一也。令禮之用蟠
translation_en:
…those who discuss instituting rites and music by taking the creative processes of Heaven and Earth as their model depart markedly from the main purport. This essay alone shows a clear grasp of the subject and expresses the subtle way in which the workings of rites and music accord with those processes of generation and completion. It accords profoundly with the original meaning and has therefore been selected.
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of how the accomplishments of rites and music accord with the creative processes of Heaven and Earth is clear and worthy of attention.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔This essay captures the greatness of the workings of the institutions established by the sages.〕
To discuss the workings of rites and music is to show their accord with the generation and completion of things through the creative processes of Heaven and Earth. Rites and music and these creative processes flow through one another. Who could say that the workings of rites and music fail to accord with such generation and completion? The Record of Music touches on this when explaining what the accomplishments of rites and music accord with. Its meaning is that people know only that rites and music were instituted by the sages, without knowing that their workings accord perfectly with the creative processes of Heaven and Earth. Thus, what is created following Heaven and issues from spontaneous harmony is music: music manifests the Grand Beginning. What is instituted following Earth and issues from spontaneous order is ritual: ritual resides in the completion of things.
The statement, “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian; the myriad things draw upon it for their beginning,” means that Qian presides over the Grand Beginning. Through yang, Qian initiates the myriad things; vital energy circulates, and all share in harmony. The essential nature of music already flows uninterruptedly with this process. Now [?], the workings of music reach to the utmost heights of Heaven and unfold in what yang generates; they penetrate the spirits and act as bellows in the beginnings of things. There is nothing manifest that they do not reach, no height that they do not attain. Wherever harmony is found, music is found. This is what is meant by “fostering harmony, leading the spirits, and following Heaven.” What could this be but music manifesting the Grand Beginning?
The statement, “Utmost indeed is the originating power of Kun; the myriad things draw upon it for their birth,” means that Kun brings things to completion. Through yin, Kun completes the myriad things; their substance takes form, and they are differentiated in an ordered arrangement. The forms of ritual already accord with this process as one. Now [?], the workings of ritual coil…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
委于地而安定乎陰之所成通達乎鬼而凝聚乎
物之所斂無幽不格無深不入是序之所存即
禮之所存所謂別宜居鬼而從地者是已非禮
居成物而何吁樂著太始同一乾德之充同禮
居成物同一坤德之凝寂禮樂功用之妙有如
是夫抑論天地先禮樂而形禮樂後天地而作
天地者禮樂之本原禮樂者天地之妙用禮樂
非天地無以肇其體天地非禮樂無以顯其用
然非聖人心識乎情文之妙身任乎制作之隆
===
孰能興禮樂以贊天地而昭揭以示人哉操制
作之柄者察諸
第貳場
論
萬世大君
羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批　近時作論者多務為新奇
可喜之語殊無古人渾厚意思此作平正溫雅而詞理
俱到故錄之為學者式
punctuated:
委于地，而安定乎陰之所成，通達乎鬼，而凝聚乎物之所斂，無幽不格，無深不入。是序之所存，即禮之所存，所謂別宜居鬼而從地者是已，非禮居成物而何？吁！樂著太始，同一乾德之充同；禮居成物，同一坤德之凝寂。禮樂功用之妙有如是夫！抑論天地先禮樂而形，禮樂後天地而作。天地者，禮樂之本原；禮樂者，天地之妙用。禮樂非天地，無以肇其體；天地非禮樂，無以顯其用。然非聖人心識乎情文之妙，身任乎制作之隆，孰能興禮樂以贊天地，而昭揭以示人哉？操制作之柄者察諸！

第貳場
論
萬世大君
羅欽順

同考試官訓導李批：「近時作論者，多務為新奇可喜之語，殊無古人渾厚意思。此作平正溫雅，而詞理俱到，故錄之為學者式。」
translation_en:
…extending throughout the earth, bringing stability to what yin completes, reaching the spirits of the dead, and gathering together where things contract. There is no obscurity it does not reach, no depth it does not penetrate. Wherever order resides, ritual likewise resides. This is what is meant by distinguishing what is appropriate, providing a dwelling for the spirits of the dead, and following earth. What could this be but ritual abiding in the completion of things? Ah! Music manifests the primordial beginning, sharing the fullness and concord [?] of Qian’s virtue; ritual abides in the completion of things, sharing the settled stillness of Kun’s virtue. Such is the marvelous efficacy of ritual and music!

Yet consider: heaven and earth took form before ritual and music, while ritual and music arose after heaven and earth. Heaven and earth are the source of ritual and music; ritual and music are the wondrous operation of heaven and earth. Without heaven and earth, ritual and music could not originate in their essential form; without ritual and music, heaven and earth could not manifest their operation. But unless a sage understands in his heart the subtleties of inner feeling and outward form, and personally assumes the exalted responsibility of establishing institutions, who can bring forth ritual and music to assist heaven and earth, and clearly display them for humanity? Let those who hold the authority to establish institutions consider this!

Second Session
Discourse
The Great Sovereign for Myriad Ages
Luo Qinshun

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: “Those who compose discourses nowadays mostly strive for novel, surprising, and pleasing expressions, entirely lacking the substantial and generous spirit of the ancients. This composition is balanced, correct, gentle, and elegant, and both its language and reasoning are fully realized. We have therefore included it as a model for students.”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陸　批〔立意正大而措詞簡當真〕
老手筆也
考試官訓導孫　批〔此論歷叙二帝三王所以爲萬〕
世大君及後世諸君之所以不及末乃歸之我
聖祖暨
列聖足以繼往聖之絕迹開萬世之太平旨鑒鑒有據而詞足以發之有學有識之士也
考試官教諭柯　批〔議論得古作者體製〕
人主之所以大過人者無他亦惟盡其道
焉耳夫人主所當盡之道何道也先王之
===
道也先王之道不外乎存其心正其情大
其德新其政光其國而先王於此無一不
盡焉此所以出乎其類拔乎其萃而卓然
爲萬世之大君也後世人主能講明先王
之道而行之使吾之道不異於先王則萬
世之下仰之以爲大君將亦不異於先王
顧不大過於人哉萬世大君請以五峯胡
氏之言而闡其旨人主一身上焉爲天地
之宗子下焉爲生民之父母天地賴我栽
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陸批〔立意正大，而措詞簡當，真〕老手筆也。
考試官訓導孫批〔此論歷叙二帝三王所以爲萬〕世大君，及後世諸君之所以不及，末乃歸之我聖祖暨列聖，足以繼往聖之絕迹，開萬世之太平。旨鑒鑒有據，而詞足以發之，有學有識之士也。
考試官教諭柯批〔議論得古作者體製。〕
人主之所以大過人者，無他，亦惟盡其道焉耳。夫人主所當盡之道，何道也？先王之道也。先王之道，不外乎存其心、正其情、大其德、新其政、光其國，而先王於此無一不盡焉。此所以出乎其類，拔乎其萃，而卓然爲萬世之大君也。後世人主能講明先王之道而行之，使吾之道不異於先王，則萬世之下仰之以爲大君，將亦不異於先王，顧不大過於人哉？萬世大君，請以五峯胡氏之言而闡其旨。人主一身，上焉爲天地之宗子，下焉爲生民之父母。天地賴我栽
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “The conception is upright and elevated, and the wording concise and apt: truly the work of a seasoned hand.”

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This discourse recounts in turn what made the Two Emperors and Three Kings great rulers for all ages, and why subsequent rulers fell short. Finally, it turns to our sagely founding ancestor and the succession of sage emperors, who could carry forward the interrupted achievements of the sages of old and inaugurate peace for all ages. Its purport is well grounded [?], and its language fully expresses it. The author is a man of learning and discernment.”

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: “The argument attains the form and manner of the ancient writers.”

There is no other reason why a ruler greatly surpasses other men: it is simply that he fulfills his Way. What is this Way that a ruler ought to fulfill? It is the Way of the former kings. The Way of the former kings consists in nothing beyond preserving one's mind, rectifying one's feelings, enlarging one's virtue, renewing one's governance, and bringing glory to one's state. In these matters the former kings left nothing unfulfilled. Thus they stood out from their kind and rose above their fellows, becoming outstandingly great rulers for all ages. If rulers of later generations can elucidate the Way of the former kings and put it into practice, making their own Way no different from that of the former kings, then those who look up to them as great rulers through the ages to come will regard them just as they regard the former kings. Would they not indeed greatly surpass other men? As for “great rulers for all ages,” allow me to explain its meaning through the words of Master Hu of Wufeng. In his single person, the ruler is, above, the principal heir of Heaven and Earth, and, below, the father and mother of the people. Heaven and Earth depend upon me to nurture …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
成化育賴我叅賛九州四海之民待我而
子育郊廟百神之祀待我而主宰其責之
重如此吾見君之名未易稱也况天下大
君乎天下大君未易稱也况萬世大君乎
人主欲進於是盖必有其道矣昔者堯德
克明而致黎民之於變萬世之下孰不仰
大哉之堯則堯為萬世大君固有道也舜
德罔愆而致四方之風動萬世之下孰不
仰君哉之舜則舜為萬世大君固有道也
===
以至禹之祗台德先湯之聖敬日躋文之
純亦不已武之建其有極當是時也地平
天成萬世永賴功加于時而德垂後裔永
清四海而永敘萬年則禹湯文武為萬世
大君孰非有道而然耶漢唐以來人主未
甞聞先王之道故天下不得蒙至治之澤
自夫因循自怠之習興而是道壞於宴安
矣自夫沉溺聲色之欲熾而是道壞於淫
泆矣自夫開拓邊境之議起而是道壞於
punctuated:
成，化育賴我叅賛，九州四海之民待我而子育，郊廟百神之祀待我而主宰。其責之重如此，吾見君之名未易稱也，况天下大君乎？天下大君未易稱也，况萬世大君乎？人主欲進於是，盖必有其道矣。
昔者堯德克明，而致黎民之於變。萬世之下，孰不仰大哉之堯？則堯為萬世大君，固有道也。舜德罔愆，而致四方之風動。萬世之下，孰不仰君哉之舜？則舜為萬世大君，固有道也。以至禹之祗台德先，湯之聖敬日躋，文之純亦不已，武之建其有極。當是時也，地平天成，萬世永賴，功加于時而德垂後裔，永清四海而永敘萬年。則禹湯文武為萬世大君，孰非有道而然耶？
漢唐以來，人主未甞聞先王之道，故天下不得蒙至治之澤。自夫因循自怠之習興，而是道壞於宴安矣；自夫沉溺聲色之欲熾，而是道壞於淫泆矣；自夫開拓邊境之議起，而是道壞於
translation_en:
…completion; the transforming and nurturing processes of nature depend on my assistance. The people of the Nine Provinces and Four Seas await my nurturing care as their parent; the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and to the hundred spirits, await my presiding over them. Such is the weight of these responsibilities. I see that even the title of ruler is not easily deserved—how much less that of great ruler of all under Heaven! If the title of great ruler of all under Heaven is not easily deserved, how much less that of great ruler for all ages! A sovereign who wishes to attain this must surely possess the Way.
In antiquity, Yao made his virtue manifest and thereby brought about the transformation of the common people. Through all succeeding ages, who has not looked up to Yao, of whom it was said, “Great indeed!”? Thus Yao became a great ruler for all ages because he possessed the Way. Shun’s virtue was without fault, and his influence stirred the four quarters like the wind. Through all succeeding ages, who has not looked up to Shun, of whom it was said, “What a ruler!”? Thus Shun became a great ruler for all ages because he possessed the Way. So too with Yu’s declaration, “Reverently I put virtue first”; Tang’s sagacity and reverence, which advanced daily; King Wen’s unceasing purity; and King Wu’s establishment of the highest standard. In their time, the earth was brought into order and Heaven’s work accomplished, providing enduring benefits for all ages. Their achievements benefited their own times, while their virtue descended to later generations; they secured lasting peace within the Four Seas and enduring order for ten thousand years. When Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu became great rulers for all ages, was there any whose attainment did not arise from possessing the Way?
Since the Han and Tang dynasties, sovereigns have never heard the Way of the former kings, and thus all under Heaven have been unable to enjoy the blessings of consummate government. Once habits of merely following precedent and lapsing into indolence arose, this Way was ruined by ease and comfort. Once the desire to indulge in music and sensual pleasures blazed up, this Way was ruined by debauchery. Once proposals to expand the frontiers arose, this Way was ruined by…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
窮黷矣自夫崇務虛文之風盛而是道壞
於侈靡矣又其下則有惑於神仙眞空之
說而是道又壞於虛無寂滅渺茫荒誕之
教矣若是者謂之一世之大君且不可又
可謂之萬世之大君乎君焉而欲以大名
大焉而欲以萬世之大名亦在乎講明先
王之道而行之耳吾能敬以直內禮以制
外則心存矣好惡不偏喜怒中節則情正
矣和順積中英華發外則德大矣治教修
===
舉而巍乎成功則政新矣禮樂明備而煥
乎文章則國光矣殆見先王之道自我而
行先王之治自我而臻由一世而百世世
固久矣而凡君天下者莫不仰其道以為
法則百世仰其道豈非百世之大君乎由
百世而萬世世國遠矣而凡御宇內者莫
不慕其道以為儀刑萬世慕其道又非萬
世之大君乎彼君於漢者餘四百年之後
人已不知其為漢漢之君非不能久也特
punctuated:
窮黷矣。自夫崇務虛文之風盛，而是道壞於侈靡矣。又其下，則有惑於神仙眞空之說，而是道又壞於虛無寂滅、渺茫荒誕之教矣。若是者，謂之一世之大君且不可，又可謂之萬世之大君乎？君焉而欲以大名，大焉而欲以萬世之大名，亦在乎講明先王之道而行之耳。
吾能敬以直內，禮以制外，則心存矣；好惡不偏，喜怒中節，則情正矣；和順積中，英華發外，則德大矣；治教修舉，而巍乎成功，則政新矣；禮樂明備，而煥乎文章，則國光矣。殆見先王之道自我而行，先王之治自我而臻。由一世而百世，世固久矣，而凡君天下者莫不仰其道以為法則。百世仰其道，豈非百世之大君乎？由百世而萬世，世國遠矣，而凡御宇內者莫不慕其道以為儀刑。萬世慕其道，又非萬世之大君乎？彼君於漢者，餘四百年之後，人已不知其為漢。漢之君非不能久也，特
translation_en:
…in exhausting resources through relentless warfare. Once the fashion for prizing empty formalities flourished, this Way was ruined by extravagance. Still further down, some were deluded by teachings about immortals and true emptiness, and this Way was again ruined by doctrines of nothingness and extinction, vague and absurd. Such men cannot even be called great rulers of a single age; how could they be called great rulers of ten thousand generations? For a ruler to gain a name for greatness, and, being great, to gain a name for greatness lasting ten thousand generations, depends simply upon elucidating the Way of the former kings and putting it into practice.
If I can use reverence to make my inner self upright and ritual propriety to regulate my outward conduct, then my moral mind will be preserved. If my likes and dislikes are impartial, and my joy and anger remain within their proper bounds, then my feelings will be correct. If harmony and compliance accumulate within and their finest qualities shine forth, then my virtue will be great. If government and moral instruction are cultivated and carried out, achieving towering accomplishments, then my administration will be renewed. If rites and music are clear and complete, resplendent in their cultural forms, then my state will shine. We may then expect to see the Way of the former kings put into practice through me, and their good governance brought to realization through me. From one generation to a hundred generations is certainly a long span; yet if all who rule the world look up to this Way as their standard, and a hundred generations look up to it, am I not a great ruler of a hundred generations? From a hundred generations to ten thousand generations is a far greater span [?]; yet if all who govern the realm admire this Way as their model, and ten thousand generations admire it, am I not also a great ruler of ten thousand generations? As for those who ruled under the Han, after more than four hundred years people no longer even recognized it as the Han. It was not that the rulers of the Han could not endure; it was only…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
以其不知先王之道而自小之耳君於唐
者幾三百年之後人已不知其爲唐唐之
君非不能大也亦以其不知先王之道而
自小之耳吾以是知君之大者道之大大
焉而爲萬世之大者道之冠於萬世孰
謂人君之所以大過於人者不自其道之
盡也耶雖然漢唐之君不知先王之道而
自小者固不足言矣而其英君誼辟之志
趣高邁識量閎達者亦未易及也又况二
帝三王之大道其可以易而及之哉然豈
終不可及耶後世有高於漢唐之賢君必
能行之矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺景命汛掃胡風新一代之制
作正千古之綱常萬世大君莫有加於此
者
太宗文皇帝肅靖家邦纘承
鴻業丕闡君師之道撫私帝王之治萬世大
君莫有尚於此者
punctuated:
以其不知先王之道而自小之耳。君於唐者幾三百年之後，人已不知其爲唐。唐之君非不能大也，亦以其不知先王之道而自小之耳。吾以是知君之大者，道之大；大焉而爲萬世之大者，道之冠於萬世。孰謂人君之所以大過於人者，不自其道之盡也耶？雖然，漢唐之君不知先王之道而自小者，固不足言矣，而其英君誼辟之志趣高邁、識量閎達者，亦未易及也。又况二帝三王之大道，其可以易而及之哉？然豈終不可及耶？後世有高於漢唐之賢君，必能行之矣。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，誕膺景命，汛掃胡風，新一代之制作，正千古之綱常，萬世大君莫有加於此者。太宗文皇帝，肅靖家邦，纘承鴻業，丕闡君師之道，撫私帝王之治，萬世大君莫有尚於此者。
translation_en:
…because they did not understand the Way of the former kings and thus diminished themselves. After nearly three hundred years of Tang rule, people no longer recognized it as Tang. It was not that the rulers of Tang were incapable of greatness; they too diminished themselves because they did not understand the Way of the former kings. From this I know that a ruler’s greatness lies in the greatness of his Way; to attain still greater stature and be great for all ages requires a Way that stands supreme throughout all ages. Who could say that a ruler’s greatness beyond other men does not come from his fully realizing the Way? Nevertheless, those rulers of Han and Tang who diminished themselves through ignorance of the Way of the former kings scarcely merit discussion; yet even their outstanding and righteous sovereigns, with lofty aspirations and broad understanding, are not easily equaled. How much less could the great Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings be attained with ease! But must it remain forever unattainable? If later ages produce a worthy ruler who surpasses those of Han and Tang, he will surely be able to put it into practice.
We reverently reflect upon our Emperor Gao, Taizu, who received Heaven’s glorious mandate, swept away barbarian customs, established anew the institutions of a dynasty, and rectified the cardinal relationships and enduring norms for all time. No great ruler of all ages could exceed him in this. Emperor Wen, Taizong, brought order and peace to the ruling house and realm, continued the grand imperial enterprise, magnificently elucidated the Way of the ruler and teacher, and upheld [?] the governance of the ancient emperors and kings. No great ruler of all ages could surpass him in this.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
列聖繼統奕葉重光君道之大皆視
祖宗而無愧矣方今
聖天子在上心
祖宗之心德
祖宗之德情無不正政是以和是宜其上有以
慰
九廟在天之靈下有以啓
儲皇天縱之聖而益光顯其國家於無窮也歟
天下臣民莫不鼓舞欣忭而相慶曰萬世
大君何幸復見於
今日也猗歟休哉
===
表
擬賀
冊立
皇太子表
一道 汪偉
同考試官教諭馮 批〔嚴而有則〕
同考試官教諭黃 批〔得體〕
punctuated:
列聖繼統，奕葉重光，君道之大，皆視祖宗而無愧矣。方今聖天子在上，心祖宗之心，德祖宗之德，情無不正，政是以和。是宜其上有以慰九廟在天之靈，下有以啓儲皇天縱之聖，而益光顯其國家於無窮也歟！天下臣民莫不鼓舞欣忭而相慶曰：「萬世大君，何幸復見於今日也！」猗歟休哉！

表

擬賀冊立皇太子表

一道，汪偉。

同考試官教諭馮，批〔嚴而有則〕。
同考試官教諭黃，批〔得體〕。
translation_en:
Successive sage sovereigns have inherited the imperial succession, renewing its brilliance generation after generation. In the greatness of their practice of rulership, all can stand comparison with their ancestors without shame. Now the sage Son of Heaven reigns above, taking his ancestors’ heart as his own and embodying their virtue. His sentiments are invariably correct, and his government is therefore harmonious. Surely he can thereby console above the spirits in Heaven honored in the nine ancestral temples, and nurture below the Heaven-endowed sagacity of the Crown Prince, bringing ever greater glory to his dynasty for all eternity! All the subjects of the realm rejoice and congratulate one another, saying: “How fortunate we are to see once again today a great sovereign whose like appears but once in ten thousand generations!” Ah, how splendid!

Memorial

Draft Memorial Congratulating the Emperor on the Formal Investiture of the Crown Prince

One composition, by Wang Wei.

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔Rigorous and guided by proper standards.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Appropriate to the form.〕

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Refined and elegant.〕

We respectfully present this memorial to offer congratulations. Your servant So-and-so, truly joyful and truly delighted, bows his head to the ground and kowtows, submitting these words: We humbly reflect that the sagely sovereign rules by Heaven’s mandate, extending benevolence and grace throughout the Four Seas; the imperial heir assumes his rightful position, securing the foundation of the state for ten thousand years. The peoples beyond and within the Chinese realm rejoice together; spirits and human beings alike celebrate. This is because we have the good fortune to serve ○○○ [?], whose intelligence is bestowed by Heaven, whose sagely reverence increases daily, and who succeeds to …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗列聖之丕圖荷
天地百神之眷佑奉明禋於
九廟穆若高宗竭至養於
兩宮孝同虞舜正家以化天下綽有關雎之風
垂統以裕
後昆遂致麟趾之應黃河清而
聖人出式協昌期鸑鳳下而
渙詔頒肇建
儲位前星拱極而耀三垣
===
離照繼明而光八表信
天生之不偶知
神器之有歸文丕顯而武丕承華夏蠻貊之
率俾禹克勤而啓克敬謳歌獄訟之皆歸
此誠
宗社無疆之休臣民莫大之慶也臣欣逢
盛典叨列清班馳逞
賀於
九重效嵩呼之三祝伏願
punctuated: 祖宗列聖之丕圖，荷天地百神之眷佑，奉明禋於九廟，穆若高宗；竭至養於兩宮，孝同虞舜。正家以化天下，綽有關雎之風；垂統以裕後昆，遂致麟趾之應。黃河清而聖人出，式協昌期；鸑鳳下而渙詔頒，肇建儲位。前星拱極而耀三垣，離照繼明而光八表。信天生之不偶，知神器之有歸。文丕顯而武丕承，華夏蠻貊之率俾；禹克勤而啓克敬，謳歌獄訟之皆歸。此誠宗社無疆之休，臣民莫大之慶也。臣欣逢盛典，叨列清班，馳逞賀於九重，效嵩呼之三祝。伏願
translation_en:
…the grand enterprise of the ancestors and successive sage sovereigns, receiving the solicitous protection of Heaven, Earth, and the hundred spirits. You offer pure sacrifices in the nine ancestral temples, reverent like Gaozong; you devote yourself to the utmost care of the Two Palaces, filial like Shun of Yu. By ordering your household, you transform all under Heaven, abundantly displaying the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guanju); by transmitting the succession to enrich your descendants, you have brought forth the auspicious fulfillment of “The Qilin’s Hoof” (Linzhi). The Yellow River runs clear and a sage appears, fitting this flourishing age; the phoenix descends and an imperial proclamation issues forth, establishing the position of heir apparent. The Foremost Star attends the celestial pole and shines upon the Three Enclosures; the radiance of Li continues the light and illuminates the eight outermost regions. Truly, Heaven’s bringing him forth was no accident; we know that the sacred vessel of sovereignty has its rightful successor. As King Wen was greatly illustrious and King Wu grandly continued his work, the peoples of Huaxia and the Man and Mo all submit; as Yu was diligent and Qi reverent, those singing praises and seeking judgment in lawsuits all turn to the heir. This is indeed boundless blessing for the ancestral temples and altars of state, and the greatest joy for officials and people alike.

Your servant rejoices to encounter this grand ceremony and is privileged, though unworthy, to stand among the honored ranks of court officials. I hasten to convey congratulations [?] to the ninefold palace, emulating the threefold acclamation at Mount Song. I humbly wish that…

天仰

聞

Your servant gazes toward Heaven and looks up to Your Majesty, overcome with fervent emotion and trembling reverence. title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對寬猛因時而不泥乎古此
聖祖撥世救時之卓見寬猛相濟而必酌其宜
此
聖世長治久安之良圖蓋易亂為治固不得不
施之以猛而貽謀燕翼又不得不示之以
寬寬猛因時神矣哉
聖祖卓越之見也政猛則必節之以寬政寬則
必振之以猛寬猛相濟允矣哉
聖世致治之法也請因執事之問而陳其槩昔
===
孔子論居上為政而必有取於寬者所以
示人為政之常道也伊尹傅說之告其君
而皆欲其法祖者亦示之以法其常道而
已洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺
天眷命為生民主丁元政縱弛之餘遭華風淪
沒之際教化陵夷人紀廢墜思欲示國法
於臣民乃作
大誥三編鋤凶芟惡之典凜乎秋霜之肅殺
punctuated:
對：寬猛因時而不泥乎古，此聖祖撥世救時之卓見；寬猛相濟而必酌其宜，此聖世長治久安之良圖。蓋易亂為治，固不得不施之以猛；而貽謀燕翼，又不得不示之以寬。寬猛因時，神矣哉，聖祖卓越之見也！政猛則必節之以寬，政寬則必振之以猛。寬猛相濟，允矣哉，聖世致治之法也！請因執事之問而陳其槩。
昔孔子論居上為政，而必有取於寬者，所以示人為政之常道也。伊尹、傅說之告其君，而皆欲其法祖者，亦示之以法其常道而已。洪惟我太祖高皇帝膺天眷命，為生民主，丁元政縱弛之餘，遭華風淪沒之際，教化陵夷，人紀廢墜。思欲示國法於臣民，乃作《大誥》三編。鋤凶芟惡之典，凜乎秋霜之肅殺
translation_en:
In reply: To employ leniency and severity according to the times, without clinging rigidly to antiquity—this was the sagacious founding emperor’s exceptional insight in restoring order to the world and rescuing his age. To make leniency and severity complement one another, always weighing what is appropriate—this is the excellent plan by which our sagely age achieves lasting order and enduring peace. For in transforming disorder into order, severity was indeed indispensable; yet in bequeathing plans for the security of his descendants, it was likewise indispensable to show leniency. How inspired was the sagacious founding emperor’s extraordinary insight in adapting leniency and severity to the times! When government is severe, it must be tempered with leniency; when government is lenient, it must be invigorated with severity. How fitting is our sagely age’s method of achieving order through the mutual support of leniency and severity! Allow me to respond to your question, honored examiners, by setting out its general principles.
When Confucius discussed occupying a superior position and conducting government, he invariably commended leniency in order to show people the constant Way of government. When Yi Yin and Fu Yue counseled their rulers, both urged them to emulate their ancestors; this too was merely to instruct them to follow that constant Way. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao received Heaven’s gracious mandate and became lord of the people. He came in the aftermath of lax and undisciplined Yuan government, at a time when Chinese civilized customs had fallen into oblivion, moral instruction was declining, and the bonds of human relations had broken down. Wishing to make the laws of the state manifest to his subjects, he composed the three collections of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao). Their statutes for rooting out the violent and cutting down the wicked were as awe-inspiring as the killing frost of autumn…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
也戢姦剔蠹之法肅乎雷霆之威斷也若
是者似異於孔子之言矣然而
御宇建極餘三十年教化已晦而復明人紀
已墜而復立
盛德大業視殷湯周武而無愧者蓋以其用
法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳及其
駿命已凝大統已定思欲示家法於子孫乃
作
祖訓一書論用法特以前日之嚴為戒論致
治惟於先王之道是程若是者又似異於
伊傅之言矣然而
聖子神孫傳六七世九有奠安而至治益隆四
夷賓服而
鴻業益固
重熈累洽視太甲高宗而有光者以其垂訓
有合於孔子論為政之道故耳夫猛於立
國之初者一時之用也寬於繼統之後者
萬世之常也寬猛各因其時而效驗各臻
punctuated: 也。戢姦剔蠹之法，肅乎雷霆之威斷也。若是者，似異於孔子之言矣。然而御宇建極餘三十年，教化已晦而復明，人紀已墜而復立，盛德大業視殷湯、周武而無愧者，蓋以其用法有合於周官刑亂國之典故耳。及其駿命已凝，大統已定，思欲示家法於子孫，乃作《祖訓》一書。論用法，特以前日之嚴為戒；論致治，惟於先王之道是程。若是者，又似異於伊傅之言矣。然而聖子神孫傳六七世，九有奠安而至治益隆，四夷賓服而鴻業益固，重熈累洽，視太甲、高宗而有光者，以其垂訓有合於孔子論為政之道故耳。夫猛於立國之初者，一時之用也；寬於繼統之後者，萬世之常也。寬猛各因其時，而效驗各臻
translation_en:
…indeed. His laws for restraining evildoers and rooting out corruption were as awe-inspiring as the force and decisiveness of thunder. Such measures seem to differ from the words of Confucius. Yet, during more than thirty years of ruling the realm and establishing the supreme standard, he restored to brightness moral instruction that had grown obscure and reestablished the human relationships that had fallen into decay. His splendid virtue and great achievements bore comparison without shame with those of Tang of Yin and Wu of Zhou. This was surely because his application of the law accorded with the provisions in the Offices of Zhou for punishing a disordered state.

Once his august mandate was secure and his imperial succession settled, he wished to set forth his family's rules for his descendants, and so composed the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun). In discussing the application of law, he expressly warned against the severity of his earlier days; in discussing the achievement of good government, he took only the Way of the former kings as his model. This, in turn, seems to differ from the words of Yi Yin and Fu Yue. Yet his sagely sons and divinely endowed grandsons have succeeded him for six or seven generations: the nine regions are secure, and exemplary government flourishes ever more; the peoples of the four quarters submit, and the great imperial enterprise grows ever firmer. With successive reigns of prosperity and enduring peace, their achievements shine in comparison with those of Tai Jia and Gaozong. This is because the instructions he bequeathed accorded with Confucius's account of the Way of governing.

Severity at the founding of a state is a measure suited to a particular time; leniency after succession to the throne is the enduring norm for all ages. Leniency and severity each suit their respective times, and their results each attain…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
其拯非
聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古曷能然哉雖然嘗
聞之孔子有曰政寛則民慢慢則糾之以
猛猛則民殘殘則施之以寛寛以濟猛猛
以濟寛政是以和
列聖相承迄今百二十餘年矣記不云乎異世
殊時不相沿襲愚竊以爲因俗爲政尚當
以孔子之言爲法因時制宜隨事取中猛
以警之使頽靡之綱無不振寛以行之使
===
仁厚之意無不存則唐虞三代之治無以
易此而其所以垂裕於
後昆者將億萬斯世而無窮矣謹因明問所
及而述其管見如此他日倘得徹聽
九重亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也
第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林　批〔究道學之淵源探先儒之閫〕
奥無如此篇
punctuated:
其拯。非聖祖之淵衷睿識卓越千古，曷能然哉？雖然，嘗聞之，孔子有曰：「政寛則民慢，慢則糾之以猛；猛則民殘，殘則施之以寛。寛以濟猛，猛以濟寛，政是以和。」列聖相承，迄今百二十餘年矣。記不云乎：「異世殊時，不相沿襲。」愚竊以爲，因俗爲政，尚當以孔子之言爲法，因時制宜，隨事取中。猛以警之，使頽靡之綱無不振；寛以行之，使仁厚之意無不存。則唐虞三代之治，無以易此，而其所以垂裕於後昆者，將億萬斯世而無窮矣。謹因明問所及，而述其管見如此。他日倘得徹聽九重，亦庶幾乎芹曝之一助也。

第二問
陳嬰
同考試官訓導林　批〔究道學之淵源，探先儒之閫〕奥，無如此篇。
translation_en:
…their saving effects [?]. Had the sagely founder’s profound mind and discerning wisdom not surpassed those of all ages, how could this have been achieved? Nevertheless, I have heard these words of Confucius: “When government is lenient, the people become lax; when they become lax, correct them with severity. When government is severe, the people suffer; when they suffer, extend leniency to them. Let leniency temper severity and severity temper leniency: government thereby achieves harmony.”

The succession of sage sovereigns has now continued for more than 120 years. Does not the Record of Rites say, “Different ages and different times do not simply follow one another’s practices”? In my humble opinion, governing in accordance with prevailing customs still requires taking Confucius’s words as the standard, adapting measures to the times, and finding the proper balance in each affair. Use severity to admonish, so that every weakened bond of order is restored; exercise leniency, so that the spirit of benevolence and generosity is preserved throughout. Then even the government of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties could offer no improvement upon this, and the blessings thereby bequeathed to posterity would endure for countless generations without end. I have respectfully set forth these limited views in response to the matters raised by your discerning question. Should they someday reach the imperial hearing within the ninefold palace gates, they might perhaps offer some small assistance, like the humble gifts of celery and the sun’s warmth.

Second Policy Question
Chen Ying

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: “For investigating the origins of the Learning of the Way and probing the inner mysteries of earlier Confucian scholars, no essay equals this one.”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭王　批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人蓋慮其未有能受之者此策於先天太極通書西銘諸書同異條答無遺其亦深有所得而可受之者耶〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔精粹〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔策能答所問足見學識〕
對濂溪未作而千聖相傳之道學晦而不
明濂溪既作而千聖相傳之道統斷而復
續夫道之大原出於天而具於人心蓋混
然一太極也濂溪周子手為圖筆為書使斯
===
道已晦而復明已斷而復續是其生乎千
載之下而有以接道統於千載之上奮乎
百世之上而有以啓道學於百世之下也
先生之學其粹矣哉愚顧何人而能發其
精藴乎龘陳大義以復明問之萬一且夫
伏羲先天之易備天地鬼神之奥萬事萬
物之理誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也堯舜湯武
之相禪繼以治天下者以是孔曾思孟之
相傳授以淑天下者以是孟子既殁聖學
punctuated:
同考試官教諭王　批〔程子未嘗以太極圖示人，蓋慮其未有能受之者。此策於先天、太極、通書、西銘諸書同異，條答無遺，其亦深有所得而可受之者耶？〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔精粹。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔策能答所問，足見學識。〕
對：濂溪未作，而千聖相傳之道學晦而不明；濂溪既作，而千聖相傳之道統斷而復續。夫道之大原出於天，而具於人心，蓋混然一太極也。濂溪周子手為圖，筆為書，使斯道已晦而復明，已斷而復續。是其生乎千載之下，而有以接道統於千載之上；奮乎百世之上，而有以啓道學於百世之下也。先生之學，其粹矣哉！愚顧何人，而能發其精藴乎？龘陳大義，以復明問之萬一。且夫伏羲先天之易，備天地鬼神之奥、萬事萬物之理，誠萬世斯文之鼻祖也。堯舜湯武之相禪繼，以治天下者以是；孔曾思孟之相傳授，以淑天下者以是。孟子既殁，聖學
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Master Cheng never showed the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate to others, presumably fearing that none could yet receive its teaching. This policy essay answers point by point, without omission, concerning the similarities and differences among the writings on the Prior Heaven and the Supreme Ultimate, the Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu), and the Western Inscription (Ximing). Might its author likewise have gained a profound understanding and be capable of receiving that teaching?〕
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Refined and pure.〕
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔The policy essay answers what was asked, amply demonstrating learning and discernment.〕
In reply: Before Lianxi arose, the Learning of the Way transmitted through a thousand sages had grown obscure and lacked clarity. Once Lianxi arose, the succession of the Way transmitted through a thousand sages, having been broken, was renewed. The great source of the Way issues from Heaven and is fully present in the human mind: it is, indeed, the Supreme Ultimate in its undivided entirety. Master Zhou of Lianxi drew a diagram with his own hand and composed writings with his brush, bringing this Way back to light after its obscuration and restoring its broken succession. Thus, though born a thousand years later, he could connect with the succession of the Way a thousand years before; and, arising a hundred generations before those to come, he could open up the Learning of the Way for a hundred generations afterward. How pure was the Master's learning! Who am I, in my ignorance, to expound its essential depths? I venture [?] to set forth its broad meaning, thereby answering even a ten-thousandth part of your discerning question.
Now, Fuxi's Changes of the Prior Heaven encompasses the mysteries of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits, and the principles of all affairs and things. It is truly the progenitor of this cultural tradition for all ages. It was by this that Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, successively yielding or succeeding to the throne, governed the realm; and it was by this that Kongzi, Zengzi, Zisi, and Mengzi, transmitting and receiving the teaching in succession, brought goodness to the realm. After Mengzi died, the learning of the sages…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
不傳先生崛起千載之後獨得不傳之秘
祖先天之易作太極之書所謂太極云者
蓋本於易有太極而陰陽五行人物由此
而生即太極生兩儀兩儀生四象四象生
八卦之謂也自太極之在造化者言之則
即天地可以推太極動靜之妙所謂立天
之道曰陰與陽立地之道曰柔與剛也自
太極之在品彙者言之惟聖人會太極動
靜之全所謂立人之道曰仁與義也至於
===
易通之書又與此圖相為表裏所謂誠者
即圖之言太極而大哉乾元萬物資始乾
道變化各正性命即圖之陽動而陰靜也
所謂五殊二實二本則一此自末以緣本
萬物統體一太極也所謂一實萬分萬一
各正此自本而之末一物各具一太極也
太極之書祖先天之易則其象數宜無不
同今觀太極自一而二自二而五即推至
於萬物具則自一而二自二而四自四而
punctuated:
不傳，先生崛起千載之後，獨得不傳之秘，祖先天之易，作太極之書。所謂太極云者，蓋本於「易有太極」，而陰陽五行人物由此而生，即「太極生兩儀，兩儀生四象，四象生八卦」之謂也。自太極之在造化者言之，則即天地可以推太極動靜之妙，所謂「立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛」也。自太極之在品彙者言之，惟聖人會太極動靜之全，所謂「立人之道曰仁與義」也。至於《易通》之書，又與此圖相為表裏。所謂誠者，即圖之言太極，而「大哉乾元，萬物資始」「乾道變化，各正性命」，即圖之陽動而陰靜也。所謂「五殊二實，二本則一」，此自末以緣本，萬物統體一太極也。所謂「一實萬分，萬一各正」，此自本而之末，一物各具一太極也。

太極之書祖先天之易，則其象數宜無不同。今觀太極，自一而二，自二而五，即推至於萬物；具則自一而二，自二而四，自四而
translation_en:
…was no longer transmitted. The Master arose a thousand years later and alone grasped the secrets that had ceased to be transmitted. Taking the Before-Heaven system of the Changes as his foundation, he composed his work on the Supreme Ultimate. What he calls the Supreme Ultimate is grounded in the statement, “In the Changes there is the Supreme Ultimate.” Yin and yang, the Five Phases, human beings, and all other things arise from it. This is precisely what is meant by “The Supreme Ultimate generates the Two Modes; the Two Modes generate the Four Images; the Four Images generate the Eight Trigrams.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate as it exists in the processes of creation and transformation, one can infer the wonders of its activity and stillness from Heaven and Earth themselves. This is what is meant by “Establishing the Way of Heaven, they called it yin and yang; establishing the Way of Earth, they called it yielding and firm.” Speaking of the Supreme Ultimate as it exists in the various kinds of beings, only the sage comprehends the entirety of its activity and stillness. This is what is meant by “Establishing the Way of humanity, they called it benevolence and righteousness.” As for the book Penetrating the Changes (Yitong), it and this diagram mutually illuminate one another. What the book calls sincerity is what the diagram calls the Supreme Ultimate. Its statements, “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! The myriad things depend upon it for their beginning,” and “The Way of Qian changes and transforms, and each thing receives its proper nature and allotted destiny,” correspond to the diagram’s activity of yang and stillness of yin. The statement “The five are distinct, but their underlying reality is the two; the two are fundamentally one” traces the branches back to their root: the myriad things, taken as a whole, are one Supreme Ultimate. The statement “The one reality divides into the myriad, and each of the myriad obtains its proper unity” proceeds from the root to the branches: each individual thing possesses a Supreme Ultimate in its entirety.

Since the work on the Supreme Ultimate takes the Before-Heaven system of the Changes as its foundation, its images and numbers ought to agree with that system in every respect. Yet, examining the Supreme Ultimate, we find that it proceeds from one to two and from two to five, and from there extends directly to the myriad things; the following sequence [?], however, proceeds from one to two, from two to four, and from four to…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
八自八而十六自十六而三十二自三十
二而六十四然後萬物之理備誠若有可
疑者然物理本同而象數亦無二致但推
得有詳畧耳通書一篇本名易通則六十
四卦疑皆有其說今考其書獨有乾損益
家人睽復無妄蒙艮等說則亦有未安者
然先生之書散逸頗多蓋本有而今亡矣
先天太極二圖雖同一發明造化之妙也
然先天乃伏羲本圖非康節所自作雖無
===
言語而所該甚廣太極却是濂溪自作發
明易中大槩綱領意思而已故格局則太
極不如先天之大而詳義理則先天不如
太極之精而約也太極西銘二書雖同一
開示學者之言也然西銘則推人以之天
即近以明遠於學者日用最為親切大極
則詳於性命之原而畧於進為之目有不
可以驟而語者故程子於西銘嘗屢言以
示門人而太極未嘗一言及之也至若劉
punctuated:
八，自八而十六，自十六而三十二，自三十二而六十四，然後萬物之理備，誠若有可疑者。然物理本同，而象數亦無二致，但推得有詳畧耳。《通書》一篇，本名《易通》，則六十四卦疑皆有其說。今考其書，獨有乾、損、益、家人、睽、復、無妄、蒙、艮等說，則亦有未安者。然先生之書散逸頗多，蓋本有而今亡矣。
先天、太極二圖，雖同一發明造化之妙也，然先天乃伏羲本圖，非康節所自作，雖無言語，而所該甚廣。太極却是濂溪自作，發明《易》中大槩綱領意思而已。故格局則太極不如先天之大而詳，義理則先天不如太極之精而約也。
《太極》《西銘》二書，雖同一開示學者之言也，然《西銘》則推人以之天，即近以明遠，於學者日用最為親切。《大極》則詳於性命之原，而畧於進為之目，有不可以驟而語者。故程子於《西銘》嘗屢言以示門人，而《太極》未嘗一言及之也。至若劉
translation_en:
…eight, from eight to sixteen, from sixteen to thirty-two, and from thirty-two to sixty-four; only then are the principles of all things fully encompassed. There does indeed seem to be room for doubt. Yet the principles of things are fundamentally the same, and their images and numbers likewise do not diverge; the difference lies merely in how fully or briefly they are developed. The work Penetrating the Changes (Tongshu) was originally entitled Comprehending the Changes (Yitong), so presumably it contained explanations of all sixty-four hexagrams. Upon examining the book now, however, we find only explanations of Qian, Sun, Yi, Jiaren, Kui, Fu, Wuwang, Meng, Gen, and the like. This too leaves something unresolved. Yet many of the Master's writings have been scattered and lost; presumably these explanations once existed but are now gone.
Although the Prior Heaven and Supreme Ultimate diagrams both elucidate the subtleties of creation and transformation, the Prior Heaven diagram is Fuxi's original diagram, not something Kangjie himself devised. Though it contains no words, its scope is exceedingly broad. The Supreme Ultimate diagram, by contrast, was Lianxi's own creation, intended simply to elucidate the broad outlines and guiding ideas of the Book of Changes. Thus, in scope and arrangement, the Supreme Ultimate diagram is less expansive and detailed than the Prior Heaven diagram; in its exposition of principles, however, the Prior Heaven diagram is less refined and concise than the Supreme Ultimate diagram.
Although the two works, Supreme Ultimate and Western Inscription (Ximing), both offer instruction to students, the Western Inscription proceeds from humanity to Heaven and illuminates what is distant through what is near, making it especially immediate and pertinent to students' daily lives. The Supreme Ultimate [written 大極 here, apparently for 太極] treats the origins of human nature and destiny in detail but gives only a brief account of the specific steps for advancing in practice; some of its teachings cannot be conveyed hastily. Thus Master Cheng repeatedly discussed the Western Inscription to instruct his disciples, but never once mentioned the Supreme Ultimate. As for Liu…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
子所謂天地之中即濂溪太極之謂蓋中
只是恰好處極是在中至極之理也橫渠
太虛之說本爲無極之意殊不知無極是
該虛實清濁而言太虛只說得清虛一邊
耳嗟夫伊洛道喪寖失其真賴有考亭朱
夫子上接聖賢相傳之道統著書立言私
淑後人其本義啓蒙諸書皆所以闡揚乎
太極之理也噫道學得濂溪而始傳濂溪
得朱子而益明朱子實有大造於萬世學
===
者矣謹對
第三問　　羅欽順
同考試官訓導李　批〔場中答此策者多不能以其迹而原其心惟此作備推究聖心步步著實無異當時親炙者高〕
薦何疑
同考試官教諭陸　批〔隨問隨答略無襄詞策場中作者〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔足見用心希聖之學〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔三場多可録録此以例其餘〕
punctuated:
子所謂天地之中，即濂溪太極之謂。蓋中只是恰好處，極是在中至極之理也。橫渠太虛之說，本爲無極之意，殊不知無極是該虛實清濁而言，太虛只說得清虛一邊耳。嗟夫！伊洛道喪，寖失其真，賴有考亭朱夫子，上接聖賢相傳之道統，著書立言，私淑後人。其《本義》《啓蒙》諸書，皆所以闡揚乎太極之理也。噫！道學得濂溪而始傳，濂溪得朱子而益明，朱子實有大造於萬世學者矣。謹對。
第三問　　羅欽順
同考試官訓導李，批〔場中答此策者，多不能以其迹而原其心。惟此作備推究聖心，步步著實，無異當時親炙者。高〕薦何疑？
同考試官教諭陸，批〔隨問隨答，略無襄詞，策場中作者。〕
考試官訓導孫，批〔足見用心希聖之學。〕
考試官教諭柯，批〔三場多可録，録此以例其餘。〕
translation_en:
…what Master Liu called “the center of Heaven and Earth” is precisely what Lianxi called the Supreme Ultimate. For “the center” is simply the point of perfect appropriateness, while “the ultimate” is the principle that reaches its utmost within that center. Hengqu’s account of the Great Void was intended to express the meaning of the Non-Ultimate. He failed to realize, however, that the Non-Ultimate encompasses both the empty and the substantial, the clear and the turbid, whereas the Great Void describes only the clear and empty side.
Alas! The Way of the Yi and Luo traditions fell into decline, gradually losing its authentic meaning. Fortunately, Master Zhu of Kaoting took up the orthodox transmission of the Way handed down by the sages and worthies, writing books and expounding teachings through which later generations could learn from him indirectly. His Original Meaning and Introduction to the Study of the Changes, among other works, all elucidate the principle of the Supreme Ultimate. Ah! The learning of the Way began to be transmitted through Lianxi, and Lianxi’s teachings became still clearer through Master Zhu. Master Zhu has indeed rendered an immense service to learners of all ages. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Third Question — Luo Qinshun
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Most candidates answering this policy question could not trace the sage’s outward actions back to his mind. This essay alone thoroughly investigates the sage’s mind, remaining firmly grounded at every step, as though its author had personally received his teaching at the time. What doubt can there be about recommending it highly?”
Associate Examiner Lu, Instructor, comments: “It answers each point as it is asked, with no superfluous wording [?]: an accomplished composition among the policy essays.”
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This amply reveals learning devoted to aspiring to sagehood.”
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: “Much from all three sessions merits inclusion. This piece is included as representative of the rest.”

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對欲觀聖人之迹當知聖人之道欲知聖
人之道當原聖人之心蓋聖人之心一道
之所寓而言行之迹一道之所形也得其
心則可以知其道知其道則凡跡之同異
皆可以會而通之合而一之而無所疑矣
茍徒泥其跡而不原其心明其道以會其
同異惡足以知聖人也哉嗟夫尼丘毓秀
孔聖肇生窮宇宙而一人亙古今而獨盛
道參乎兩間法垂於萬世誠非後人所敢
===
妄議也然其言行之載諸經傳者似有小
異不能無疑愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸
矣姑即其一二而論之如里必擇乎仁厚
較之居不陋乎九夷者若戾矣殊不知化
於人者常人之事固當擇化人者聖人之
事不必擇也亂邦不居比之公山欲往者
似背矣殊不知遷善避惡固君子潔身之
常道而化惡為善又聖人誨人之本心也
從先進以示損過就中之意從周制以盡
punctuated: 對：欲觀聖人之迹，當知聖人之道；欲知聖人之道，當原聖人之心。蓋聖人之心，一道之所寓；而言行之迹，一道之所形也。得其心，則可以知其道；知其道，則凡跡之同異，皆可以會而通之，合而一之，而無所疑矣。茍徒泥其跡，而不原其心、明其道，以會其同異，惡足以知聖人也哉！嗟夫！尼丘毓秀，孔聖肇生，窮宇宙而一人，亙古今而獨盛。道參乎兩間，法垂於萬世，誠非後人所敢妄議也。然其言行之載諸經傳者，似有小異，不能無疑。愚生亦嘗誦習而得其指歸矣。姑即其一二而論之。如里必擇乎仁厚，較之居不陋乎九夷者，若戾矣。殊不知，化於人者，常人之事，固當擇；化人者，聖人之事，不必擇也。亂邦不居，比之公山欲往者，似背矣。殊不知，遷善避惡，固君子潔身之常道；而化惡為善，又聖人誨人之本心也。從先進，以示損過就中之意；從周制，以盡
translation_en:
In reply: To examine the traces of the sage’s conduct, one must understand his Way; to understand his Way, one must investigate his heart. For the sage’s heart is where the single Way resides, while the traces of his words and actions are where that single Way takes form. If one grasps his heart, one can understand his Way. Once one understands his Way, all the similarities and differences in his conduct can be comprehended together and reconciled as one, leaving no grounds for doubt. If one merely clings to the outward traces, without investigating his heart and illuminating his Way in order to reconcile their similarities and differences, how could one adequately understand the sage?

Ah! Niqiu nurtured its finest essence, and the sage Kong was born: unique throughout the universe, unrivalled in excellence across past and present. His Way ranks alongside Heaven and Earth; his example extends to ten thousand generations. Truly, he is not someone whom later generations would dare to discuss presumptuously. Yet his words and actions, as recorded in the classics and their commentaries, seem to contain minor discrepancies that cannot but raise doubts. This humble student has also recited and studied them and has grasped their underlying purport. Let me discuss one or two examples.

His insistence on choosing a humane and generous neighborhood seems at odds with his assertion that dwelling among the Nine Yi would not be uncouth. This overlooks the fact that being influenced by others is the condition of ordinary people, who must therefore choose their surroundings, whereas transforming others is the work of the sage, who need not choose. His refusal to dwell in a disorderly state seems contrary to his wish to go to Gongshan. This overlooks the fact that advancing toward goodness and avoiding evil is indeed the gentleman’s regular way of keeping himself unsullied, while transforming evil into goodness is also the sage’s fundamental intention in instructing others. He followed the earlier practitioners to convey the intention of reducing excess and attaining the mean; he followed the institutions of Zhou to fulfill…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
為下不倍之道從夫先進非即所以從周
乎言無類是我之教化有善反之功云不
移乃彼之暴棄無自反之道教雖無類豈
能移其下愚乎大學之道自致知始此聖
人文行忠信之先夫文小學之事自力行
始此弟子餘力學文之先夫行民無信不
立者全體之大信故為為政之先必信於
言者一事之小信故為為士之次知魯火
而不知廄焚非明於遠而暗於近也蓋抯
===
僖之廟功德不足以存火之者天道之必
然也廄牧之地人馬之所兩集焚之者人
事之偶然也拜南子而不拜陽貨非重於
此而輕於彼也古者仕於其國有見小君
之禮彼須見而吾則往見非行其禮之當
然乎大夫有賜於士雖有往拜之禮彼矙
亡而吾亦矙亡非欲其禮之相稱乎箕子
比干微子也觀其行雖有死生去就之殊
原其心同一至誠惻怛之意所以同謂之
punctuated: 為下不倍之道。從夫先進，非即所以從周乎？言無類，是我之教化有善反之功；云不移，乃彼之暴棄無自反之道。教雖無類，豈能移其下愚乎？大學之道自致知始，此聖人文行忠信之先夫文；小學之事自力行始，此弟子餘力學文之先夫行。民無信不立者，全體之大信，故為為政之先；必信於言者，一事之小信，故為為士之次。知魯火而不知廄焚，非明於遠而暗於近也。蓋抯僖之廟，功德不足以存，火之者天道之必然也；廄牧之地，人馬之所兩集，焚之者人事之偶然也。拜南子而不拜陽貨，非重於此而輕於彼也。古者仕於其國，有見小君之禮，彼須見而吾則往見，非行其禮之當然乎？大夫有賜於士，雖有往拜之禮，彼矙亡而吾亦矙亡，非欲其禮之相稱乎？箕子、比干、微子也，觀其行，雖有死生去就之殊；原其心，同一至誠惻怛之意，所以同謂之
translation_en:
…the way of serving as a subordinate without disloyalty. Is following the earlier generations not precisely the means of following Zhou? When he speaks of making no distinctions among classes in teaching, this means that his instruction has the power to turn people toward goodness; when he says that some cannot be changed, this means that they have maltreated and abandoned themselves and have no way to turn back through self-reflection. Although teaching makes no distinctions among classes, how can it change the very lowest in understanding? The way of advanced learning begins with extending knowledge: this is why, among cultural learning, conduct, loyalty, and trustworthiness, the Sage puts cultural learning first. Elementary learning begins with diligent practice: this is why, in saying that disciples should study cultural learning when they have energy to spare, he puts conduct first. The statement that the people cannot stand without trust concerns trust in its comprehensive and greater sense, and therefore gives it priority in governing. Insisting on keeping one’s word concerns trustworthiness in a single matter, in its lesser sense, and therefore gives it secondary place in being a gentleman.

That he knew of the fire in Lu but did not know that the stable was burning does not mean that he understood distant matters while remaining ignorant of those close at hand. The merits and virtues commemorated in the ancestral temples of Zha [?] and Xi were insufficient to warrant their preservation; their destruction by fire was an inevitable working of the Way of Heaven. The stables and pastures, however, were places where people and horses gathered together; their burning was a chance occurrence in human affairs. That he paid his respects to Nanzi but did not pay his respects to Yang Huo does not mean that he valued the former and slighted the latter. In antiquity, one who served in a state was ritually obliged to have an audience with the ruler’s consort. When she requested an audience and he went to see her, was he not performing what ritual properly required? When a grand master bestowed a gift upon a gentleman, although ritual required the recipient to visit and offer thanks, the donor had watched for his absence, and he likewise watched for the donor’s absence. Was this not a wish to make their ritual courtesies correspond?

As for Jizi, Bi Gan, and Weizi, if we examine their actions, they differed in dying or surviving, withdrawing or remaining. Yet if we trace their intentions, all shared the same utmost sincerity and compassionate concern. This is why they were all called…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
三仁大伯文王也或當為而不欲為以全
人子之孝或可為而不忍為以盡人臣之
忠所以同謂之至德殷夏之後尚有杞宋
之所存也故有據而可考杞宋之後無復
杞宋之所存矣此無徵而不信其於孔子
之知何所損不待結纓之日而豫知子路
之死人事之可必也不能於終日之頃而
先知顏淵之夭天命之不幸也其於孔子
之知何所虧荅昭公以為知禮所以諱其
===
君之過以存吾之忠厚斥管仲以不知禮
所以暴其人之罪以著彼之僭竊勤農事
以利天下者君子之公心也不适之褒而
誰褒學農事以利一已者小人之私心也
不遲之貶而誰貶必竭其兩端於鄙夫者
是我固無倦教之心不復於三隅之不反
者是彼終無受教之地論父母之國道在
可久也則遲遲於三日不朝之魯何過耶
論無道之君道在可去也則急急於一問
punctuated: 三仁。大伯、文王也，或當為而不欲為，以全人子之孝；或可為而不忍為，以盡人臣之忠，所以同謂之至德。殷夏之後，尚有杞宋之所存也，故有據而可考；杞宋之後，無復杞宋之所存矣，此無徵而不信，其於孔子之知何所損？不待結纓之日而豫知子路之死，人事之可必也；不能於終日之頃而先知顏淵之夭，天命之不幸也，其於孔子之知何所虧？荅昭公以為知禮，所以諱其君之過，以存吾之忠厚；斥管仲以不知禮，所以暴其人之罪，以著彼之僭竊。勤農事以利天下者，君子之公心也，不适之褒而誰褒？學農事以利一已者，小人之私心也，不遲之貶而誰貶？必竭其兩端於鄙夫者，是我固無倦教之心；不復於三隅之不反者，是彼終無受教之地。論父母之國，道在可久也，則遲遲於三日不朝之魯，何過耶？論無道之君，道在可去也，則急急於一問
translation_en:
…the three humane men. As for Taibo and King Wen, the former, though entitled to act, was unwilling to do so, thereby fulfilling a son's filial devotion; the latter, though able to act, could not bear to do so, thereby fulfilling a minister's loyalty. Thus both were said to possess consummate virtue. After the Yin and Xia dynasties, there remained what Qi and Song had preserved, so there was evidence available for examination. After Qi and Song, what they had preserved no longer remained; without corroboration, it could not be credited. How does this detract from Confucius's knowledge? That he foresaw Zilu's death before the day when Zilu tied his cap strings was because human affairs can have predictable outcomes. That he could not foresee Yan Yuan's premature death within the course of a day [?] was because it was a misfortune ordained by Heaven. How does this diminish Confucius's knowledge?

In answering concerning Duke Zhao, he said that the duke understood ritual: this concealed his ruler's fault and preserved his own loyalty and generosity. In censuring Guan Zhong for not understanding ritual, he exposed that man's offenses and made his usurpation of privileges manifest. To labor at agriculture for the benefit of all under Heaven expresses the gentleman's public-mindedness. Whom should he praise if not Kuo? To study agriculture for one's own benefit expresses the petty man's selfishness. Whom should he disparage if not Chi? That he invariably explored both ends of a question fully for an uncultivated man shows that he himself was never weary of teaching. That he did not repeat his instruction for someone who failed to infer the other three corners shows that the other person ultimately lacked the capacity to receive instruction.

When considering the land of one's parents, the Way permits a prolonged stay. What fault, then, was there in his lingering in Lu, where for three days he did not attend court [?]? When considering a ruler who lacks the Way, the Way permits departure. Thus his haste after a single inquiry…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
軍旅之衛何遽耶孔圉勤學好問是好善
而忘己之勢公叔錫氏爵祉是好善而忘
人之勢此皆合乎謚法之公者烏得不同
許其可以為文乎子貢因論學而知詩子
夏因論詩而知學是皆得於言意之表者
烏得不同許其可以言詩乎由是而觀則
知孔子之體即道而用即義聲為律而身
為度舉一身之言行誠萬世之標準也又
何彼此異同之可議哉愚生管窺蠡測不
能盡摹寫之詳惟執事其進教之謹對
===
第四問
汪偉
同考試官教諭馮　批〔五策皆善發此篇尤有見故錄之〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔書孔學者切務當求學古人書法〕
〔而約而有自得之趣此篇深究古書與夫運用之法盡實留心〕
〔於書學而有所得者也宜錄之以為學書者式〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔觀此條答必其能游于藝者〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔有筆手〕
punctuated:
軍旅之衛，何遽耶？孔圉勤學好問，是好善而忘己之勢；公叔錫氏爵祉，是好善而忘人之勢。此皆合乎謚法之公者，烏得不同許其可以為文乎？子貢因論學而知詩，子夏因論詩而知學，是皆得於言意之表者，烏得不同許其可以言詩乎？由是而觀，則知孔子之體即道，而用即義，聲為律而身為度，舉一身之言行，誠萬世之標準也。又何彼此異同之可議哉？愚生管窺蠡測，不能盡摹寫之詳，惟執事其進教之。謹對。

第四問
汪偉
同考試官教諭馮　批〔五策皆善發，此篇尤有見，故錄之。〕
同考試官教諭黃　批〔書孔學者切務，當求學古人書法，〕〔而約而有自得之趣。此篇深究古書與夫運用之法，盡實留心〕〔於書學而有所得者也，宜錄之以為學書者式。〕
考試官訓導孫　批〔觀此條答，必其能游于藝者。〕
考試官教諭柯　批〔有筆手。〕
translation_en:
…military affairs in Wei: why should his departure be considered hasty? Kong Yu studied diligently and readily asked questions; this was a love of goodness that made him forget his own standing. Gongshu bestowed a clan name, rank, and blessings [?]; this was a love of goodness that made him disregard another’s standing. Both accorded with the impartial principles governing posthumous names. How could Confucius fail to approve equally that they might be called Wen, “Cultured”? Zigong came to understand the Odes through discussing learning; Zixia came to understand learning through discussing the Odes. Both grasped what lay beyond the expressed words and meanings. How could Confucius fail to approve equally that they were fit to discuss the Odes?

Viewed in this light, we know that Confucius embodied the Way and acted according to righteousness. His voice was the pitch standard, and his person the measure. All the words and deeds of his life truly constituted a standard for ten thousand generations. What grounds, then, remain for disputing the similarities and differences between his various responses? With my narrow view, like peering through a tube or measuring with a ladle, I, an ignorant student, cannot portray this fully in all its detail. I can only hope that you, honored examiners, will offer further instruction. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Fourth Question
Wang Wei

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔All five policy essays develop their subjects well. This piece is particularly insightful, and so it has been selected for inclusion.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔Calligraphy is an urgent concern for students [?]; they should seek to learn the methods of the ancients,〕〔achieving concision and the savor of personal understanding. This piece investigates ancient calligraphy and the methods of putting it into practice in depth. Its author has truly devoted attention〕〔to the study of calligraphy and gained something from it [?]. It should be included as a model for those learning calligraphy.〕

Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Judging by this answer, its author must be someone capable of finding delight in the arts.〕

Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: 〔He has a skilled pen.〕

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
對字書作而變化之體滋學書精而運用
之法密盖書爲六藝之一所以宣人文數
治化紀六經應萬事經天而緯地皆有頼
於此者也豈他技藝之比哉誠不可以不
講也請因明問而陳其槩夫字書之作其
来尚矣自伏羲畫八卦而書契攸興蒼頡
觀鳥跡而字文以製以體天地之撰以類
萬物之情其圓應規其方應矩轉筆爲圓
摺筆爲方方之平爲準圓之直爲繩陰陽
===
五行所以成象成形者也書以方圓平直
爲之主而輕重大小低昂長短斜正寓其
變焉六書之義至矣盡矣然其迭更迭變
伏羲氏有龍書神農氏有穗書軒轅氏有
垂雲書因所見而創也太昊氏爲鸞書放
勲氏爲龜書夏后氏爲鍾鼎書隨所見而
製也自是而後史籀作大篆李斯作小篆
而隷則出於程邈焉史游作章草蔡邕作
飛白而揩則出於鍾繇焉乃若霧卷雲收
punctuated:
對：字書作，而變化之體滋；學書精，而運用之法密。盖書爲六藝之一，所以宣人文、數治化、紀六經、應萬事，經天而緯地，皆有頼於此者也。豈他技藝之比哉？誠不可以不講也。請因明問而陳其槩。
夫字書之作，其来尚矣。自伏羲畫八卦，而書契攸興；蒼頡觀鳥跡，而字文以製。以體天地之撰，以類萬物之情。其圓應規，其方應矩；轉筆爲圓，摺筆爲方；方之平爲準，圓之直爲繩。陰陽五行，所以成象成形者也。書以方圓平直爲之主，而輕重、大小、低昂、長短、斜正寓其變焉。六書之義，至矣，盡矣！然其迭更迭變，伏羲氏有龍書，神農氏有穗書，軒轅氏有垂雲書，因所見而創也；太昊氏爲鸞書，放勲氏爲龜書，夏后氏爲鍾鼎書，隨所見而製也。自是而後，史籀作大篆，李斯作小篆，而隷則出於程邈焉；史游作章草，蔡邕作飛白，而揩則出於鍾繇焉。乃若霧卷雲收
translation_en:
In reply: As writing was created, its changing forms multiplied; as the study of calligraphy became more refined, the methods of wielding the brush became more exact. Writing is one of the Six Arts. Through it human culture is expressed, governance and moral transformation are recounted [?], the Six Classics are recorded, and the myriad affairs are addressed. Ordering heaven and earth—all depend upon it. How could it be compared with other technical arts? It certainly must be studied. Allow me to respond to your illuminating question by setting out its general principles.
The creation of writing goes back to remote antiquity. When Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams, written records arose; when Cangjie observed birds’ tracks, written characters were fashioned. They embodied the workings of heaven and earth and represented the characteristics of the myriad things. Their roundness accorded with the compass, their squareness with the carpenter’s square. Turning the brush produced roundness; folding its movement produced squareness. The level aspect of squareness served as a leveling instrument, and the straight aspect of roundness as a marking line. Yin and yang and the Five Phases are that through which images and forms come into being. Writing takes squareness, roundness, levelness, and straightness as its foundations, while its variations reside in lightness and heaviness, largeness and smallness, lowness and height, length and shortness, and slanting and uprightness. The principles of the Six Categories of Writing are consummate and exhaustive! Yet its forms continually succeeded and transformed one another. Fuxi had dragon script, Shennong had grain-ear script, and Xuanyuan had hanging-cloud script: each originated in what they observed. Taihao made luan-bird script, Fangxun made tortoise script, and the rulers of Xia made bell-and-tripod script: each was fashioned after what they saw. Thereafter, Shi Zhou created large seal script, and Li Si created small seal script, while clerical script originated with Cheng Miao. Shi You created draft cursive script, and Cai Yong created flying-white script, while regular script [?] originated with Zhong Yao. As for mist rolling up and clouds drawing back…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
叔若踈而復密鳳翥龍翔勢若斜而反正
鍾王之筆妙矣然視顔魯公之雄秀獨出
有如杜詩者是其精神形於以死赴國之
時則顔之書尤濟於用也虞世南之所稱
五絶詞翰居一薛稷之筆力遒麗當時莫
及虞稷之書善矣然較之柳公拳之心正
筆正由中見外者是有得於虛靜精忠之
間則柳之書尤有所本也且古人之書逸
少嘗云得法於白雲子蔡邕嘗云得神人
===
所授八角垂芒之書人皆信其有異傳也
殊不知白雲子即心也神人亦心也心有
所契而寓言耳古人執筆逸少得其法於
羣鵞之運頸懷素得其妙於夏雲之廻風
人皆議其為好事也殊不知鵞之運頸周
回而容與也雲之廻風變幻而悠揚也目
有所擊而心悟耳夫書札於儒事最近不
可以不學也學書之法當以執筆為先用
筆次之執筆之法所謂虛拳實腕指齊掌
punctuated: 叔若踈而復密，鳳翥龍翔，勢若斜而反正。鍾王之筆妙矣，然視顔魯公之雄秀獨出，有如杜詩者，是其精神形於以死赴國之時，則顔之書尤濟於用也。虞世南之所稱五絶，詞翰居一；薛稷之筆力遒麗，當時莫及。虞稷之書善矣，然較之柳公拳之心正筆正，由中見外者，是有得於虛靜精忠之間，則柳之書尤有所本也。且古人之書，逸少嘗云得法於白雲子，蔡邕嘗云得神人所授八角垂芒之書，人皆信其有異傳也。殊不知白雲子即心也，神人亦心也，心有所契而寓言耳。古人執筆，逸少得其法於羣鵞之運頸，懷素得其妙於夏雲之廻風，人皆議其為好事也。殊不知鵞之運頸，周回而容與也；雲之廻風，變幻而悠揚也。目有所擊而心悟耳。夫書札於儒事最近，不可以不學也。學書之法，當以執筆為先，用筆次之。執筆之法，所謂虛拳實腕，指齊掌
translation_en:
…seemingly sparse yet dense [?]; like phoenixes soaring and dragons flying, their configurations seem slanted yet return to uprightness. The brushwork of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi is marvelous. Yet consider the uniquely powerful elegance of Yan Lugong—Yan Zhenqing, Duke of Lu—which resembles Du Fu’s poetry: this was his spirit taking visible form when he went to his death in service to the state. Yan’s calligraphy thus served a practical purpose all the more fully. Among the celebrated five excellences of Yu Shinan, literary composition and calligraphy held a place; the vigorous beauty of Xue Ji’s brushwork was unmatched in his day. The calligraphy of Yu and Xue is fine. Yet compare it with Liu Gongquan’s [?] principle that when the heart is upright, the brush is upright, with the inner self manifesting outwardly. This reflects an attainment grounded in emptiness and stillness, wholeheartedness and loyalty; Liu’s calligraphy thus had an especially firm foundation.

Moreover, concerning the calligraphy of the ancients, Yishao—Wang Xizhi—once said that he obtained his method from Baiyunzi, the Master of White Clouds. Cai Yong once said that he received from a divine being a script with eight corners and trailing points. Everyone believes that they received extraordinary transmissions. They fail to understand that Baiyunzi is simply the mind, and the divine being is also the mind. Their minds had grasped something, and they merely expressed it through allegory. As for how the ancients wielded the brush, Yishao obtained his method from the movements of a flock of geese’s necks, and Huaisu grasped its subtleties from summer clouds swirling in the wind. Everyone regards these accounts as a fondness for curious tales. They fail to understand that geese move their necks in easy, unhurried circles, while clouds swirling in the wind change form and drift freely. Something strikes the eye, and the mind understands: that is all.

Writing is very closely related to the work of a Confucian scholar and must be studied. In learning calligraphy, holding the brush should come first, and using it second. The method of holding the brush is what is called keeping the fist hollow and the wrist firm, the fingers aligned and the palm…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
空者執筆之際使虎口寬可容彈掌中虛
可容卵指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也所謂擫
捺鉤抉抵拒導送者擫用大指捺用食指
鉤抉用中指抵拒用無名指導送用小指
是也用筆之精鋒之或藏或出或正或側
與左用者藏則鋒藏畫中出則芒刃在外
正則鋒不偏露側則轉側取妍而左則𢧐
力過勁如反竹為弓者矣筆之有引有屻
有縱有複與舞動者引則引短為長屻則
===
屻長為短縱則送之欲迅複則重覆其畫
而舞則欲下不下如景山興雲者矣夫執
筆既熟用筆既精則其為書也可以追倣
古人而傳後世者矣抑豈徒為人觀美哉
蓋天文地文人文一也景星卿雲人共覩
之精金美玉人共寶之書人之心畫也人
之文也烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉愚也
行而不著習而不察姑揣摩以對未知是
否惟進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 空者，執筆之際，使虎口寬可容彈，掌中虛可容卵，指淺抱筆而腕惟實者也。所謂擫捺鉤抉抵拒導送者，擫用大指，捺用食指，鉤抉用中指，抵拒用無名指，導送用小指是也。用筆之精，鋒之或藏或出，或正或側，與左用者，藏則鋒藏畫中，出則芒刃在外，正則鋒不偏露，側則轉側取妍，而左則𢧐力過勁，如反竹為弓者矣。筆之有引有屻，有縱有複，與舞動者，引則引短為長，屻則屻長為短，縱則送之欲迅，複則重覆其畫，而舞則欲下不下，如景山興雲者矣。夫執筆既熟，用筆既精，則其為書也，可以追倣古人而傳後世者矣。抑豈徒為人觀美哉！蓋天文、地文、人文，一也。景星卿雲，人共覩之；精金美玉，人共寶之。書，人之心畫也，人之文也，烏可苟且而不求臻其妙哉！愚也，行而不著，習而不察，姑揣摩以對，未知是否，惟進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en:
…“hollow” means that, when holding the brush, one leaves the opening between thumb and forefinger wide enough to accommodate a pellet and the hollow of the palm spacious enough to accommodate an egg; the fingers clasp the brush lightly, while the wrist remains firm. As for the techniques called pressing, bearing down, hooking, pushing out, supporting, resisting, guiding, and sending: pressing uses the thumb; bearing down uses the index finger; hooking and pushing out use the middle finger; supporting and resisting use the ring finger; guiding and sending use the little finger.

Refinement in handling the brush involves concealing or exposing its tip, keeping it upright or inclining it, and using it in reverse. When concealed, the tip remains within the stroke; when exposed, its sharp point appears outside. When upright, the tip does not show to either side; when inclined, it turns sideways to achieve beauty. In reverse movement, the force strains with excessive strength [?], like bamboo bent backward to make a bow. The brush also has movements of extending, shortening [?], releasing, retracing, and dancing. Extending draws out what is short to make it long; shortening [?] reduces what is long to make it short. Releasing sends the brush forward swiftly; retracing goes back over the stroke. Dancing means seeming about to descend yet not descending, like clouds arising over a lofty mountain.

Once one is practiced in holding the brush and refined in handling it, one’s calligraphy can emulate the ancients and be transmitted to later generations. Surely it is not merely intended to look beautiful to others! The patterns of heaven, earth, and humankind are one. Auspicious stars and felicitous clouds are sights all behold; refined gold and beautiful jade are treasures all prize. Writing is the delineation of a person’s heart and the expression of that person’s cultivation. How could one treat it carelessly and fail to seek its utmost subtlety?

In my ignorance, I act without understanding and practice without discernment. I have ventured to ponder these matters in making my reply, but do not know whether it is correct. If you would offer me further instruction, I would be most fortunate.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
第五問
范希淹
同考試官教諭劉批斷制養士詰兵之道發揮無餘
蘊故錄之
同考試官教諭俞批處置養士詰兵之事允當諸卷
無如此篇是宜錄出
考試官訓導孫批正得問意可取
考試官教諭柯批時務所論鑿鑿可行有□□□
論養士詰兵之法行於古者有優劣不能
===
不隨時以為興衰行於今者雖盡善不可
不因時而為損益盖歷代養士詰兵之法
迄今凡幾變大率皆隨其優劣以為興衰
耳為治者欲使之常興而不衰可不因時
損益而求以盡其善哉請詳言之自古君
天下者固必資文德以致太平亦必資武
功以戡禍亂文武並用誠長治久安之計
也然而欲興文教必在於設學以養士故
成周之時遐不作人詠歌於棫樸薪槱之
