translation_en:
Fifth Policy Question
Fan Xiyan
Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: His judgments concerning the principles of nurturing scholars and maintaining military preparedness develop the subject fully, leaving nothing unexplored. We therefore include this answer.
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: His proposals for nurturing scholars and maintaining military preparedness are appropriate. None of the other papers equals this one; it should be selected for inclusion.
Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor, comments: He grasps precisely the intent of the question. Worth selecting.
Examiner Ke, Instructor, comments: His discussion of current affairs offers concrete, practicable proposals. It has [three illegible characters].
Considering the methods of nurturing scholars and maintaining military preparedness, those practiced in antiquity had their strengths and weaknesses and inevitably flourished or declined with changing times. Those practiced today, even if entirely sound, must nevertheless be modified as circumstances require. Through successive dynasties, how many changes have these methods undergone down to the present? Broadly speaking, they have flourished or declined according to their strengths and weaknesses. If those who govern wish them always to flourish and never to decline, can they fail to modify them with the times, seeking to perfect them? Allow me to explain in detail.
Since antiquity, those who ruled the realm have certainly had to draw upon civil virtue to bring about universal peace, but they have also had to rely on military achievement to quell calamity and disorder. Employing civil and military means together is indeed the way to secure lasting order and enduring peace. Yet promoting civil instruction necessarily depends upon establishing schools to nurture scholars. Thus, in the flourishing days of Zhou, “Does he not nurture men?” was sung in The Oak and the Shrub (Yupu), amid its imagery of firewood heaped for burning …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
餘鎬京辟雍揄揚於豐芑有事之際養士
之美無以加矣自是而後若漢武帝爲博
士而置弟子員明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮
唐太宗徵天下名儒增廣生員玄宗令天
下州縣里皆置學宋初旣設太學武學以
教天下之士其後復設宗學以教宗室之
士漢唐宋之養士大槩如此而永平貞觀
爲最盛惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以爲
教耳我
===
太祖高皇帝旣定天下乃設學校以養士其始
也士有定額而選之也精學有常規而教
之也嚴斥異端而以正道淑人黜詞賦而
以經術取士其法美矣漸漸旣久秀民日
多遂因而漸變至于今名州大邑增至數
倍司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中或
䠊於逸樂而挑達城闕或急於進取而貪
緣奔競至屢
宸慮特
punctuated:
餘，鎬京辟雍揄揚於豐芑有事之際，養士之美無以加矣。自是而後，若漢武帝爲博士而置弟子員，明帝臨辟雍而行養老禮，唐太宗徵天下名儒，增廣生員，玄宗令天下州縣里皆置學，宋初旣設太學、武學以教天下之士，其後復設宗學以教宗室之士。漢唐宋之養士大槩如此，而永平、貞觀爲最盛，惜其不能如成周躬行仁義以爲教耳。
我太祖高皇帝旣定天下，乃設學校以養士。其始也，士有定額而選之也精，學有常規而教之也嚴，斥異端而以正道淑人，黜詞賦而以經術取士，其法美矣。漸漸旣久，秀民日多，遂因而漸變。至于今，名州大邑增至數倍，司政教者乃不能約之於規矩之中，或䠊於逸樂而挑達城闕，或急於進取而貪緣奔競，至屢宸慮，特
translation_en:
…and the Biyong academy at Haojing was celebrated in verses about the luxuriant millet at Feng and the king’s undertakings. Nothing could surpass this excellence in nurturing scholars. Thereafter, Emperor Wu of the Han established student places under the Erudites; Emperor Ming visited the Biyong and performed the ceremony honoring the aged. Emperor Taizong of the Tang summoned renowned Confucian scholars from throughout the realm and increased the number of students. Emperor Xuanzong ordered schools established in every prefecture, county, and village throughout the realm. Early in the Song, the Imperial University and the Military School were established to educate scholars throughout the realm; later, a school for the imperial clan was also established to educate its members. Such, in broad outline, was the nurturing of scholars under the Han, Tang, and Song. It flourished most during the Yongping and Zhenguan reign periods. Regrettably, they could not emulate the Zhou at its height by personally practicing benevolence and righteousness as the basis of instruction.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had pacified the realm, he established schools to nurture scholars. Initially, student numbers were fixed and selection was exacting; schools had standing regulations and instruction was strict. He rejected heterodox teachings and improved people through the correct Way; he set aside verse and rhapsodies and selected scholars for their learning in the Classics. These were excellent methods. As time passed, however, talented commoners grew daily more numerous, and the arrangements gradually changed accordingly. By now, student numbers in prominent prefectures and large counties have increased severalfold. Those responsible for governance and education have proved unable to keep them within the rules. Some indulge in idle pleasures [?], roaming frivolously about the city gates and towers; others, impatient for advancement, greedily cultivate connections and scramble for preferment. This has repeatedly caused imperial concern [?], prompting a special …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
勑憲臣以提督之猶不能盡弭其弊也爲今
之計竊以爲宜沙汰之使玉石不得以
兼收莠之鋤之使苗莠不得以雜植仍愼
擇有德行道藝者以爲之帥躬廉恥以正
其行明義理以澤其文尊其賢以激其不
及嘉其善而矜其不能則養士之法其庶
幾乎欲奮武衛又在於講武以詰兵故成
周之時居則爲比閭族黨州鄉之民行則
爲伍兩卒旅軍師之衆其詰兵之法無以
===
尚矣自是而後南軍主守衛王宮北軍主
巡徼京城此漢之兵也諸府六百三十四
所關中三百六十一所得強幹弱枝之法
有居重馭輕之勢其後一變而爲彍騎其
制遂壞再變而爲方鎭其制大壞此唐之
兵也以五代之樞密偏重則以文臣爲之
以五代之藩鎭太横則以文臣任之禁將
之貴者爲三衙禁旅之要者爲四廂諸司
募者曰役兵諸州募者曰廂兵什伍其民
punctuated:
勑憲臣以提督之，猶不能盡弭其弊也。爲今之計，竊以爲宜沙汰之，使玉石不得以兼收；莠之鋤之，使苗莠不得以雜植。仍愼擇有德行道藝者以爲之帥，躬廉恥以正其行，明義理以澤其文，尊其賢以激其不及，嘉其善而矜其不能，則養士之法，其庶幾乎！
欲奮武衛，又在於講武以詰兵。故成周之時，居則爲比閭族黨州鄉之民，行則爲伍兩卒旅軍師之衆，其詰兵之法無以尚矣。自是而後，南軍主守衛王宮，北軍主巡徼京城，此漢之兵也。諸府六百三十四所，關中三百六十一所，得強幹弱枝之法，有居重馭輕之勢。其後一變而爲彍騎，其制遂壞；再變而爲方鎭，其制大壞，此唐之兵也。以五代之樞密偏重，則以文臣爲之；以五代之藩鎭太横，則以文臣任之。禁將之貴者爲三衙，禁旅之要者爲四廂，諸司募者曰役兵，諸州募者曰廂兵，什伍其民
translation_en:
…ordered censorial officials to oversee them, yet even this could not entirely eliminate the abuses. For present purposes, I humbly believe that the unworthy should be weeded out, so that jade and common stones are not accepted together. Weed them out and hoe them away [?], so that grain and weeds are not planted together. Moreover, men possessing virtuous conduct and mastery of the Way and the arts should be carefully selected to lead them. By personally exemplifying integrity and a sense of shame, these leaders would rectify their conduct; by elucidating moral principles, they would enrich their writing. They should honor the worthy to spur those who fall short, commend what is good in them, and show compassion for their shortcomings. Would this not come close to a proper method of nurturing scholars?
To invigorate military defense likewise requires practicing the martial arts and putting the troops in order. Thus, in the time of the Zhou, when at home the people belonged to neighborhood and township units—bi, lü, zu, dang, zhou, and xiang—and when on campaign they formed military units—wu, liang, zu, lü, jun, and shi. No method of organizing troops could surpass this. Thereafter, the Southern Army was responsible for guarding the imperial palace, and the Northern Army for patrolling the capital: such were the armies of the Han. There were 634 military headquarters, of which 361 were in Guanzhong. This fulfilled the principle of strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches, creating a configuration in which the stronger center controlled the weaker periphery. Subsequently, a first transformation produced the Expanded Cavalry (guoqi), and the system fell into decay; a second transformation produced regional military commands, and the system deteriorated gravely. Such were the armies of the Tang. Because the Bureau of Military Affairs had exercised disproportionate power during the Five Dynasties, civil officials were appointed to direct it; because the regional military commands of the Five Dynasties had been excessively overbearing, civil officials were appointed to take charge of them. The senior commanders of the imperial guards constituted the Three Commands, and the principal formations of the imperial troops constituted the Four Divisions. Those recruited by the various offices were called service troops, and those recruited by the prefectures were called prefectural troops. The people were organized into groups of ten and five…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
而敎之曰民兵番民內附而用之曰番兵此
宋之兵也漢唐宋之詰兵大槩如此而唐
之府兵則爲最優以其有成周寓兵於農
之遺意耳我
太祖高皇帝旣一宇內乃設衛所以詰兵其詰
也軍數盈而行伍以飭師律嚴而訓練以
時以戰則勝以攻則克其兵法善矣承平旣
久文恬武嬉遂因而漸弊已絕者無自而
續逃避者莫從而稽名數雖存在伍無幾
===
司兵柄者恒無以遡瓣於緩急之際無事
則僅備差遣有事則借募民兵至屢
宸慮特
勅御史以清理之終亦不能悉復其舊也爲
今之計竊以爲宜復
祖宗官吏枉法受財之典以補其已絕之數復
祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律以警其脫放之弊其
於清理之際則審閱其板籍以清其源及
其發遣之時則嚴切其文移以防其欺仍
punctuated:
而敎之，曰民兵；番民內附而用之，曰番兵。此宋之兵也。漢、唐、宋之詰兵大槩如此，而唐之府兵則爲最優，以其有成周寓兵於農之遺意耳。
我太祖高皇帝旣一宇內，乃設衛所以詰兵。其詰也，軍數盈而行伍以飭，師律嚴而訓練以時，以戰則勝，以攻則克，其兵法善矣。承平旣久，文恬武嬉，遂因而漸弊。已絕者無自而續，逃避者莫從而稽，名數雖存，在伍無幾。司兵柄者恒無以遡瓣於緩急之際，無事則僅備差遣，有事則借募民兵，至屢宸慮，特勅御史以清理之，終亦不能悉復其舊也。
爲今之計，竊以爲宜復祖宗官吏枉法受財之典，以補其已絕之數；復祖宗軍官有犯私罪之律，以警其脫放之弊。其於清理之際，則審閱其板籍以清其源；及其發遣之時，則嚴切其文移以防其欺，仍
translation_en:
… and training them, they were called militia troops; non-Han peoples who submitted to imperial rule and were employed as soldiers were called tribal troops. These were the forces of the Song. Such, in broad outline, were the military arrangements of the Han, Tang, and Song. The Tang garrison militia system was the best, for it preserved something of the mature Zhou practice of embedding the military within the farming population.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had united all under Heaven, he established guards and battalions to put the military in order. Under these arrangements, troop complements were full and the ranks orderly; military discipline was strict, and training took place at the prescribed times. In battle they won; in attack they prevailed. His military system was excellent indeed. Yet after a long period of peace, civil officials became complacent and military officers idle, and the system gradually deteriorated. Military households whose lines had died out could not be replenished, and deserters and evaders could not be traced. Although names and numbers remained on the rolls, few men were actually in the ranks. Those who wielded military authority were constantly unable to respond effectively [?] when emergencies arose. In quiet times the troops barely sufficed for routine assignments; when trouble arose, officials resorted to recruiting militia. This repeatedly occasioned imperial concern, and special orders were issued to investigating censors to rectify the situation. In the end, however, they could not fully restore the former arrangements.
As a plan for the present, I humbly submit that we should reinstate the statutes of our imperial ancestors concerning officials and clerks who accept bribes and pervert the law, to make up the numbers lost through the extinction of military households. We should also reinstate our imperial ancestors’ laws concerning military officers who commit private offenses, to deter the abuse of improperly releasing men from service. During the rectification process, the registers should be carefully examined to put the underlying records in order. When men are dispatched, official correspondence should be rigorously controlled to prevent fraud. Furthermore, …

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪痛革官吏侵漁
朘剝之暴使各遂事育之願而不動懷土
之思則詰兵之法其庶幾乎夫養士詰兵
二者皆
國家之大政而九有志於學古入官者誠不
可以不究心也然管見如斯未知是否惟
執事進而教之
punctuated: 中嚴衛所剋減月粮之罪，痛革官吏侵漁朘剝之暴，使各遂事育之願，而不動懷土之思，則詰兵之法，其庶幾乎？夫養士、詰兵二者，皆國家之大政，而九有志於學古入官者，誠不可以不究心也。然管見如斯，未知是否，惟執事進而教之。
translation_en: …strictly punish [?] the withholding and reduction of monthly grain rations in the guards and battalions, and thoroughly abolish the brutal exploitation and exactions of officers and clerks. Let each man fulfill his wish to support his parents and raise his children, without stirring thoughts of his native place. Would this not come close to the proper way of putting the armed forces in order? Nurturing scholars and putting the armed forces in order are both great affairs of state. Anyone [?] aspiring to study antiquity and enter official service must indeed give them careful thought. Such, however, are my limited views; I do not know whether they are correct. I ask you, honored examiners, to offer me further instruction.

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
弘治壬子秋
今聖天子取士第二科也江西試
事畢將錄所得士以
獻當序其後竊惟科目以文
章校士蓋欲於言語文字之
間以觀人耳非徒以其辭而
===
已也士患不深於道爾深於
道將自裕於言以是觀人其
庶幾哉若乃移舊綴之曲折
於短褐而謂世方無華裾取
殘餕而飣餖爲華饌而謂世
方無正味若此者吾不知其
於道何如耶如是而欲觀其
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

弘治壬子秋，今聖天子取士第二科也。江西試事畢，將錄所得士以獻，當序其後。竊惟科目以文章校士，蓋欲於言語文字之間以觀人耳，非徒以其辭而已也。士患不深於道爾，深於道，將自裕於言。以是觀人，其庶幾哉！若乃移舊綴之曲折於短褐，而謂世方無華裾；取殘餕而飣餖爲華饌，而謂世方無正味。若此者，吾不知其於道何如耶？如是而欲觀其
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

The autumn of the renzi year of Hongzhi [1492] marked the second examination for selecting scholars under our present sage Son of Heaven. With the Jiangxi examination concluded, the names of the scholars selected were to be recorded and presented to the throne, and an afterword was called for. I humbly consider that the examination system assesses scholars through their compositions because it seeks to discern the person through his words and writing, not merely to judge his phrasing. What scholars should worry about is simply their lack of depth in the Way. With a deep understanding of the Way, they will naturally have ample resources for expression. To judge people on this basis would surely come close to the ideal!

But there are those who transfer the intricate patterns of old patchwork onto coarse clothing [?], claiming that the world now has no splendid robes; who take leftovers and arrange them into a sumptuous feast, claiming that the world now has no true flavors. As for such people, I do not know where they stand in relation to the Way. Under these circumstances, to seek to discern their…

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
人不亦難乎此擇士者所以
林心臆目不敢以易視也剡
爲
國家得一天下士則異時亦足
以爲天下重然舉者非私黨
舉之者非私恩此翟璜所以
不敢與魏成比而李克所以
===
不敢比周翟璜也或曰燕得
樂毅亦自隗起駿骨不遺則
千里之材自至於乎緋細熟
視於沙丘之野尚恐或失之
牝牡驪黃之外敢謂吾能得
其内而忘其外哉尚敢爲消
人之獻哉
punctuated:
人，不亦難乎？此擇士者所以林心臆目，不敢以易視也。剡爲國家得一天下士，則異時亦足以爲天下重。然舉者非私黨，舉之者非私恩。此翟璜所以不敢與魏成比，而李克所以不敢比周翟璜也。
或曰：「燕得樂毅，亦自隗起；駿骨不遺，則千里之材自至。」於乎！緋細熟視於沙丘之野，尚恐或失之牝牡驪黃之外，敢謂吾能得其内而忘其外哉？尚敢爲消人之獻哉？
translation_en:
…the person—is this not difficult? This is why those who select scholars strain their minds and eyes [?] and dare not regard the task lightly. If [?] one obtains for the state a scholar of outstanding ability, he may in time become a person of weight throughout the realm. Yet those recommended are not private partisans, and those who recommend them confer no private favors. This is why Di Huang did not dare compare himself with Wei Cheng, and why Li Ke did not dare join in partisan collusion with Di Huang.
Someone says: “Yan’s acquisition of Yue Yi likewise began with Guo Wei. If even the bones of a fine horse are not cast aside, talent capable of traveling a thousand li will come of its own accord.” Ah! Even scrutinizing closely [?] in the fields of Shaqiu, I still fear that I may miss what lies beyond distinctions of mare and stallion, black and yellow coats. How could I dare claim that I can grasp the inward qualities and forget the outward appearance? How could I further dare present this humble offering [?]?

title: 弘治五年江西鄉試錄
text:
直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓
導孫鑰謹序
punctuated: 直隸常州府宜興縣儒學訓導孫鑰謹序。
